_provenance: Synthetic distractor memories generated 2026-10-19 by claude-haiku-5-5 (40 areas x 25), deduplicated by title and filtered so none states a target fact of the core or tk families (9 removed by the filter). Not real team knowledge. Generation cost $0.1221.

learnings.title: Shipyard readiness probe must target 8081, not the app port
learnings.body: The Shipyard chart template defaults the readiness probe to the app port 8080, but the metrics sidecar now owns the health endpoint on 8081. Services that were migrated after March report CrashLoop-free but never Ready, so the rollout hangs at 0/3. Set readinessProbe.port to 8081 in values.yaml and run shipyard lint before pushing.

learnings.title: Rollouts stall when PDB minAvailable equals replica count
learnings.body: If a PodDisruptionBudget has minAvailable equal to replicas, kubectl rollout status never completes because no old pod can be evicted. We hit this on ledger-sync with replicas: 2 and minAvailable: 2. Use maxUnavailable: 1 on the PDB, or set minAvailable to replicas minus one.

learnings.title: Rollback: use shipyard rollback, not raw kubectl rollout undo
learnings.body: kubectl rollout undo reverts the Deployment spec but not the ConfigMap hash annotation, so the old pods come back with the new config. Shipyard rollback --to-revision N restores both. Always check the revision number with shipyard history first, since revisions are per-release and not per-Deployment.

learnings.title: Pods rejected by ns-quota-default unless limits are set
learnings.body: Every namespace inherits ns-quota-default, which rejects any container without explicit resources.limits. The error shows up as a ReplicaSet event 'exceeded quota', not on the Deployment itself, so people miss it. Add limits.cpu and limits.memory to the container spec; requests alone are not enough.

learnings.title: Batch pool taint: batch-spot needs an explicit toleration
learnings.body: The batch-spot node pool carries the taint pool=batch-spot:NoSchedule so that web workloads never land on preemptible nodes. Any Job or CronJob that should run there needs a toleration for that key and a nodeSelector of pool: batch-spot. Without both, the pod sits Pending with a FailedScheduling event that mentions untolerated taints.

learnings.title: Registry mirror: pull from registry.ci.internal in prod
learnings.body: Prod clusters cannot reach the public registry, and the old mirror path has been retired. Images must reference registry.ci.internal/<team>/<image>:<tag>, and the Helm chart's image.registry value should be set accordingly. ImagePullBackOff with 'no such host' almost always means someone copied a Docker Hub reference from an old README.

learnings.title: PR preview namespaces get reaped after 72 hours
learnings.body: Preview environments are created as namespaces named pr-<number> by the preview bot. A CronJob called tidecleaner deletes any pr- namespace older than 72 hours, regardless of activity. If you need a preview to live longer, add the label keep-until with a date in YYYY-MM-DD form, and tidecleaner will skip it.

learnings.title: Queue workers need 120s terminationGracePeriodSeconds
learnings.body: The default terminationGracePeriodSeconds is 30, which is shorter than the p99 job duration for the invoice-render worker. When pods were killed mid-job during deploys, the same jobs were retried and some were processed twice. Set terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 120 and make the worker handle SIGTERM by finishing the current message before exiting.

learnings.title: HPA on orders_queue_depth via prometheus-adapter
learnings.body: The orders-api HPA scales on the external metric orders_queue_depth, which prometheus-adapter exposes from the broker exporter. Target averageValue is 50 per replica, with minReplicas 3 and maxReplicas 24. The scale-down stabilization window is 300 seconds, so do not shorten it or the HPA will flap during batch arrivals.

learnings.title: ConfigMap edits do not restart pods by themselves
learnings.body: Changing a ConfigMap does not trigger a rollout, so the new values are silently ignored until the pods restart. The fix we use is the configHash helper in the Shipyard template, which adds a checksum annotation to the pod template. Make sure your chart includes the helper, or run shipyard restart after a config change.

learnings.title: Prod deploy freeze: Thursdays 14:00 to 18:00 UTC
learnings.body: The release train freezes all production namespaces every Thursday from 14:00 to 18:00 UTC because of the on-call handover overlap. Emergency fixes need a freeze exception from the incident channel, and the bot records the exception in the deploy log. Staging is not affected by the freeze.

learnings.title: kubectl context names and the kx wrapper
learnings.body: Our contexts are named prod-use1, prod-euw1, staging-use1, and dev-sandbox, and the default context on new laptops is staging-use1. Run kx prod-use1 to switch, since it also sets the namespace from your last session and prints a red banner for prod. Running plain kubectl config use-context in prod shells has caused two accidental deletes this year.

learnings.title: Ingress returns 504 at 15s; set edge proxy timeout
learnings.body: The edge ingress class has a default proxy-read-timeout of 15 seconds, so report generation endpoints that take 20 seconds return 504 to clients. Set edge.internal/proxy-read-timeout: 45s on the Ingress annotations for these routes. Do not raise the timeout globally, because it ties up connections on the shared edge pool.

learnings.title: Migrations run as a pre-upgrade Job, not an init container
learnings.body: Database migrations used to run in an init container, which meant every replica raced to apply them. The current pattern is a Helm pre-upgrade hook Job using shipyard migrate, with hook weight -5 so it runs before the Deployment update. If the migration fails, the release stops and the old pods keep serving.

learnings.title: Secrets refresh hourly from vault; force sync after rotation
learnings.body: External-secrets pulls from kv/data/svc/<name> in Vault every hour, so a rotated secret can take up to an hour to appear in the cluster. To force an immediate sync, run kubectl annotate externalsecret <name> force-sync=$(date +%s) --overwrite. Pods still need a restart to read the new value, because secrets mounted as env vars are not live-updated.

learnings.title: ndots:5 causes slow external DNS lookups; set ndots to 2
learnings.body: The default ndots of 5 in the pod resolv.conf means every lookup for an external hostname tries five search domains first. For the payments-gateway client this added about 180 ms per call and showed up as a latency regression after the cluster move. Set dnsConfig.options ndots to 2 on services that call third-party APIs.

learnings.title: CronJobs: concurrencyPolicy Forbid and history limits of 3
learnings.body: All CronJobs in our clusters should set concurrencyPolicy to Forbid, because the default Allow caused overlapping ledger reconciliations in 2023. Set successfulJobsHistoryLimit to 3 and failedJobsHistoryLimit to 5, otherwise the etcd object count grows and the nightly backup job slows down. The linter shipyard lint enforces both rules.

learnings.title: Pod Security restricted label requires USER 10001 in Dockerfile
learnings.body: Namespaces are labeled pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted, which rejects containers that run as root. Our base images set USER 10001, and the pod spec must include runAsNonRoot: true. If a third-party image runs as root, wrap it in the sandbox-shim image instead of relaxing the namespace label.

learnings.title: Sizing rule of thumb: CPU request at p50, memory limit at 1.5x request
learnings.body: For new services, set the CPU request to the p50 usage from the last two weeks in Grafana, and leave CPU limits unset to avoid throttling. Memory request should be the observed p95, with a memory limit of 1.5 times the request. Exit code 137 with reason OOMKilled in kubectl describe pod means the limit was too low, not that the node ran out of memory.

learnings.title: Cluster upgrade drains: use kdrain, not kubectl drain directly
learnings.body: The kdrain script wraps kubectl drain with the flags our policy requires, including --delete-emptydir-data only for namespaces on the approved list. Running kubectl drain by hand without --ignore-daemonsets fails halfway and leaves nodes cordoned. kdrain also waits for PDBs to clear and prints the pods it is waiting on.

learnings.title: Canary rollout: shipyard canary with 10 percent weight and 15 minute hold
learnings.body: A standard canary is shipyard canary --weight 10 --hold 15m, which routes 10 percent of traffic to the new ReplicaSet. The slo-gate check aborts automatically if the 5xx rate exceeds 2 percent over the hold window. After a green gate, promote with shipyard canary promote, not by editing the Deployment image.

learnings.title: Debugging crashloops: logs --previous and the Loki label
learnings.body: For a crashlooping pod, kubectl logs <pod> --previous shows the output from the last terminated container, which is usually where the stack trace is. Our logs also ship to Loki, where the query {app_kubernetes_io_part_of="checkout"} filters across replicas. If the previous container logged nothing, check the exit code before assuming an app bug.

learnings.title: Meshlet sidecar startup race: await-ready annotation
learnings.body: The app container often starts before the meshlet sidecar is ready, so the first outbound calls fail with connection refused. Adding meshlet.internal/await-ready: "true" to the pod annotations makes the app container wait for the sidecar health check. This adds about 2 to 4 seconds to startup, which is acceptable for all services except the low-latency quote API.

learnings.title: ImagePullBackOff after re-push: registry tags are immutable
learnings.body: The registry enforces immutable tags on release branches, so pushing a new image under an existing tag fails silently in CI but the old digest stays. Pods then pull the stale image or show ImagePullBackOff if the tag was deleted. Always bump the tag with the git SHA, and check the digest with shipyard image inspect before debugging the cluster.

learnings.title: Find recent failures: sort events by lastTimestamp
learnings.body: Plain kubectl get events lists events in no useful order, so newer failures get buried. Use kubectl get events -n <ns> --sort-by=.lastTimestamp and add --field-selector type=Warning to cut the noise. This is the fastest way to see FailedScheduling and FailedMount messages during a bad deploy.

learnings.title: Deploy approvals: two sign-offs via the Beacon bot for prod
learnings.body: Any prod deploy needs two approvals in Beacon, one from the owning team and one from an SRE on call. The deploy owner is recorded in the deploy.internal/owner annotation, and Beacon rejects the rollout if that annotation is missing. Staging deploys need only the owning team's approval.

learnings.title: Ops checklist before first prod deploy of a new service
learnings.body: Confirm the readiness and liveness probes are on separate endpoints, and that the PDB uses maxUnavailable. Check that resource requests and limits are set, the namespace has the restricted Pod Security label, and CronJobs (if any) use Forbid. Finally, add the service to the dashboard list in grafana/services.yaml so the on-call rotation sees it.

learnings.title: Node affinity for GPU pool uses gpu.internal/class label
learnings.body: The GPU node pool is labeled gpu.internal/class=a10 instead of the usual nvidia.com/gpu.product, because the older label is inconsistent across the two regions. Pods requesting GPUs should set nodeAffinity on gpu.internal/class and request nvidia.com/gpu: 1 in limits. Without the affinity, the scheduler places the pod on a CPU pool node and the device plugin fails silently.

learnings.title: Stuck state lock after a killed CI apply
learnings.body: If a CI run dies mid-apply, the lock row in the tf-locks DynamoDB table stays behind and the next plan fails with ConditionalCheckFailed. Check #infra-deploys to confirm nobody is applying, then run 'terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>' using the ID printed in the error. Do not force-unlock while a prod apply job is still showing as running in Atlantis.

learnings.title: House rule: no -target flags in prod plans
learnings.body: We do not use -target against stacks/prod/* because it hides drift in unrelated resources and has bitten us twice. If you truly need a targeted apply to unblock an incident, get a second SRE to approve in the incident channel and log it in the change ticket. Staging is fine with -target.

learnings.title: AWS provider pinned to ~> 5.31 for now
learnings.body: We pin the hashicorp/aws provider to '~> 5.31' in every stack's versions.tf. Version 5.40 changed how default_tags merge into aws_autoscaling_group tags and produced a plan that wanted to rewrite 60 ASG tag blocks. Bumps go through the provider-bump runbook on the wiki, one stack at a time.

learnings.title: Atlantis approval rule for prod network stack
learnings.body: Changes under stacks/prod/network require two approvals from the @sre-oncall group before 'atlantis apply -p prod-network' will run. The approval count is set in server-side repo config, so editing the PR's CODEOWNERS file will not bypass it. If the bot says 'Plan is stale', just rerun 'atlantis plan -p prod-network' rather than applying the old plan.

learnings.title: Nightly driftwatch runs at 02:15 UTC
learnings.body: The driftwatch job runs every night at 02:15 UTC across all workspaces and posts a summary to #drift-report. The ECS service desired_count drift on api-worker is expected because autoscaling owns that field, and the module already has lifecycle ignore_changes set for it. Anything else in the report should be triaged the same day.

learnings.title: Missing cost_center tag fails plan with TAG-001
learnings.body: Every resource must carry cost_center, owner, and env tags, and the internal tagkit module enforces this during plan. A missing tag fails with error code TAG-001 and the message names the resource address. Set the values in the stack's default_tags block, not on each resource, since tagkit only reads the provider-level defaults.

learnings.title: Ingress 0.0.0.0/0 allowed only on 443 for public ALB
learnings.body: The sg-lint rule SG-07 blocks any ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 except TCP 443 on security groups tagged role=public-lb. Port 22 from anywhere is always blocked, and there is no exception process for it. If you need SSH access, use the bastion via 'hvd-ssh connect' instead of opening a rule.

learnings.title: aws_ami data source picks up community images
learnings.body: A data 'aws_ami' block with only most_recent = true will happily return a community AMI that matches your name filter, which happened with an unpatched Ubuntu build in March. Always set owners = ["self", "amazon"] or our account ID 412890357716. The sec-images team publishes the approved hardened AMIs under the prefix hvd-base-.

learnings.title: Private zone hvd.internal is managed in one stack
learnings.body: The Route53 private hosted zone for hvd.internal lives in stacks/shared/dns and is the only place records should be created for it. Creating a record from an app stack causes the next apply in shared/dns to delete it as drift. Ask #platform-help if you need a new record and they will add it to the dns-records.yaml input.

learnings.title: RDS deletion_protection on all prod databases
learnings.body: Every prod RDS instance has deletion_protection = true, so a destroy plan will error until the flag is removed. To tear one down, run 'rdsctl unprotect --db <name>' which requires a linked decommission ticket, then destroy through the normal pipeline. Do not toggle the flag in the console because the next apply will put it back.

learnings.title: Pin Terraform to 1.6.6 with tfenv
learnings.body: Each repo has a .terraform-version file containing 1.6.6, and tfenv will switch to it automatically in the repo directory. We stayed off 1.7.x because the new plan renderer changed the output of sensitive values in our custom drift parser. Bumping this file is a separate PR from provider bumps.

learnings.title: Use stacks/ directories, not workspaces
learnings.body: We do not use Terraform workspaces for environments because state keys got confused during a 2023 migration. Each environment is its own directory under stacks/ with its own backend key, for example stacks/staging/app and stacks/prod/app. Copy an existing stack rather than adding a workspace.

learnings.title: hvd-vpc module subnet math
learnings.body: The internal hvd-vpc module v3.2.0 carves subnets with cidrsubnet(var.vpc_cidr, 4, index), so a /16 yields sixteen /20 subnets. Indexes 0 through 5 are reserved for the public tier, 6 through 11 for app, and 12 through 15 for data. Run 'terraform console' with the cidrsubnet call to check before you change any index.

learnings.title: Use for_each, not count, for ECS services
learnings.body: Our ECS service modules key services by name using for_each because removing an item from a count list shifted indexes and recreated the wrong service in staging. Keep this pattern in new modules. If you inherit a count-based module, migrate it with 'terraform state mv' before changing the list.

learnings.title: Recovering an overwritten state file
learnings.body: State bucket versioning keeps 90 days of noncurrent versions, so an accidental overwrite is recoverable. List candidates with 'aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket hvd-tfstate-prod --prefix stacks/prod/app/terraform.tfstate' and restore by copying the chosen VersionId to the current key. Notify #platform-help afterwards so the lock state can be checked.

learnings.title: Keep plan artifacts out of the apply path
learnings.body: CI saves the plan as a binary file named tfplan and apply must consume that exact file, never a fresh plan. Plan artifacts are kept for 7 days in the pipeline store. If an apply job fails with 'saved plan is stale', rerun the plan job rather than editing the apply script.

learnings.title: Lower DNS TTL 24 hours before a cutover
learnings.body: Before moving a record to a new load balancer, set its ttl to 60 in the dns-records.yaml input at least 24 hours in advance. Our resolvers cache longer than the authoritative TTL for some ISPs, so a 300 second TTL can still take 40 minutes to drain. Restore the TTL to 300 once the cutover is verified.

learnings.title: api-gw-prod load balancer idle timeout is 350 seconds
learnings.body: The api-gw-prod ALB idle_timeout is set to 350 seconds because the mobile SDK holds long-poll connections that were getting cut at 60. The module default is 60, so do not remove the override when you refactor the stack. Changing it requires a note in #api-platform since client retry logic depends on it.

learnings.title: CloudFront ACM certificates come from the us-east-1 alias
learnings.body: CloudFront only accepts ACM certificates from us-east-1, so the stacks define a second provider block with alias = 'use1' and region us-east-1. Pass it to the certificate resource explicitly with provider = aws.use1. Forgetting the alias produces a plan error saying the certificate ARN is not found, which is misleading.

learnings.title: CloudFront updates take 15 to 20 minutes
learnings.body: A change to a CloudFront distribution typically takes 15 to 20 minutes to deploy, and the CI job will look hung during that time. Do not cancel the apply job mid-update because the distribution can be left in InProgress with a half-applied config. Wait for the job to finish and check the status with 'aws cloudfront get-distribution'.

learnings.title: Importing an existing Route53 record
learnings.body: To import an existing record into state, use the ID format ZONEID_name_type, for example 'Z0ABCDEF123456_api.hvd.internal_A'. Run 'terraform import aws_route53_record.api Z0ABCDEF123456_api.hvd.internal_A' from the owning stack only. Add a matching resource block first or the import will error with a missing configuration message.

learnings.title: Lambda archive_file needs dist/ built before plan
learnings.body: The data archive_file for the ingest Lambda reads from dist/ingest, and if that directory is empty the plan shows the function as replaced every time. Run 'make build' before 'terraform plan' locally, and CI does this in the build stage automatically. A zero-byte zip in the plan output means the build step was skipped.

learnings.title: CloudWatch log groups must set retention
learnings.body: Log groups created without retention_in_days keep logs forever, and we were paying for about 14 TB of stale logs before we fixed it. The hvd-logging module sets 30 days by default, so only override it with a value approved by #finance-eng. Raw resource blocks without the module will be flagged by sg-lint rule LOG-02.

learnings.title: Athena adhoc workgroup has a 10 GB scan limit
learnings.body: The analytics-adhoc Athena workgroup defined in infra/analytics/workgroups.tf caps each query at 10 GB scanned. Queries over the cap fail with a message about bytes_scanned_cutoff_per_query, which is a limit and not a bug. Ask #data-platform to raise it for a specific project rather than editing the workgroup yourself.

learnings.title: Infracost comment blocks PRs over $500 per month
learnings.body: Each Terraform PR gets an Infracost comment, and any increase above $500 per month blocks merge until someone adds the cost-approved label. The estimate uses on-demand pricing, so reserved instance discounts are not reflected and the number will look high for reserved fleets. Note the reason in the PR description when you request the label.

learnings.title: Secrets come from SSM, never tfvars
learnings.body: Do not put secret values in .tfvars files or environment variables in CI. Read them with a data aws_ssm_parameter block using paths under /hvd/<env>/, and mark the consuming outputs sensitive. Remember that values still land in state, so the state bucket is restricted to the tf-deployer role.

learnings.title: EKS managed node group caps at 40 nodes in prod
learnings.body: The prod EKS managed node groups have max_size set to 40 to protect the account from runaway cluster-autoscaler behavior. If a load test needs more capacity, request a bump in #sre-capacity with the expected duration, and we will raise max_size for the test window only. Remember to revert it, since the stack will otherwise hold the higher value.

learnings.title: Run 'hvd-tf fmt' before committing
learnings.body: The pre-commit hook tffmt-hook v1.4 runs terraform fmt -recursive on staged files, but it skips the modules/ directory on purpose because vendored code is pinned. If CI fails the fmt check on a file you did not touch, pull main first since someone probably merged an unformatted vendored change. Do not reformat vendored modules by hand.

learnings.title: pgbouncer transaction mode silently drops session SET commands
learnings.body: Our pgbouncer pools (ledger-rw and ledger-ro) run in transaction mode, so a SET search_path or SET timezone issued on one request may not apply to the next. Wrap per-request settings in BEGIN ... COMMIT or use SET LOCAL instead. The CI lint rule dbcheck-session-set flags raw session SETs in service code.

learnings.title: Set lock_timeout on every migration or it can queue behind a long reader
learnings.body: A plain ALTER TABLE needs ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, and while it waits it blocks every query behind it on that table. Our migration runner hopper applies lock_timeout = '3s' by default, and the override is --lock-timeout. If you see 'canceling statement due to lock timeout', just retry the deploy off-peak instead of raising the value.

learnings.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY fails silently in our migration wrapper
learnings.body: Concurrent index builds cannot run inside a transaction, and hopper wraps migrations in one unless the file starts with the header '-- nontransactional'. A failed concurrent build leaves an INVALID index behind, which still slows writes. Find them with SELECT indexrelid::regclass FROM pg_index WHERE NOT indisvalid; then DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY and retry.

learnings.title: Nightly pgBackRest schedule for core-prod stanza
learnings.body: Full backups run Sunday 02:00 UTC and differentials run every other day at the same hour, retention is 14 fulls. Manual one-off: pgbackrest --stanza=core-prod --type=diff backup. Check status in the #db-alerts channel bot output, not on the host, because the cron job logs to /var/log/pgbackrest-wrapper.log only.

learnings.title: events_raw autovacuum tuning that stopped bloat
learnings.body: events_raw has about 900M rows and default autovacuum scale factors let it bloat to roughly 2.3x its live size. We set autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.02 and autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit = 2000 on that table only. Bloat dropped under 15% within a week, and vacuum runtime went from 6 hours to about 70 minutes.

learnings.title: Q: why did pg-lag-core page at 01:45?
learnings.body: The replica lag alert fires above 45 seconds, and the nightly reindex window runs 01:30 to 02:10 UTC, which pushes replay behind. This is expected and the alert is muted via pagerctl silence reindex-window. To check live lag on a replica, run SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp();.

learnings.title: Connection budget per service lives in cfg/pools.yaml
learnings.body: Primary max_connections is 400, with superuser_reserved_connections set to 25 so on-call can still log in during saturation. Each service declares its pool size in cfg/pools.yaml, and the sum must stay under 350. Adding a service without updating that file fails the deploy check pool-budget.

learnings.title: Analytics read replica access and timeouts
learnings.body: Ad-hoc analyst queries should go to analytics-ro.internal on port 5433, not the primary. The role analyst_ro has statement_timeout set to 120s, so long exports need to be chunked by created_at. If you need a longer window, ask in #data-access and we will add a temporary role with a 15 minute limit.

learnings.title: Monthly partitions of events are pre-created by partman
learnings.body: The events table is range-partitioned by month, and the job make_partitions runs at 00:15 UTC to create partitions three months ahead. If the job fails, inserts start failing with 'no partition of relation events found for row'. Recovery is to run make_partitions --force and then rerun the failed ingest batch from the dead-letter bucket.

learnings.title: Expand-contract is required for column renames
learnings.body: A rename on a live column breaks the previous app version during a rolling deploy, which we usually keep running for about 25 minutes. The house rule is two releases: add the new column and dual-write in release one, then drop the old column in release two. The reviewer checklist item is named expand-contract-ok.

learnings.title: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout is 60 seconds
learnings.body: Sessions sitting idle inside an open transaction for more than 60 seconds get terminated on all app roles. Long-running reports that hold a transaction open will see 'terminating connection due to idle-in-transaction timeout'. Use a separate connection without an open BEGIN, or open a snapshot with SET TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT when you need consistency.

learnings.title: lockwatch alias shows blockers in one screen
learnings.body: Run lockwatch on any primary host to see blocked and blocking sessions joined from pg_locks and pg_stat_activity. It prints the blocking query text truncated to 120 characters and the owning application name. Most of our incidents last quarter were a single forgotten BEGIN from a migration shell.

learnings.title: WAL volume alert usually means archive_command is failing
learnings.body: When /pgwal crosses 70 percent we get a page, and nearly every time the cause is archive_command failing on S3 permissions. Check pg_stat_archiver for last_failed_wal and the error text, then run pgbackrest --stanza=core-prod check. Do not delete WAL files by hand, because the standby may still need them.

learnings.title: Major upgrade 14 to 16 on db-core-07 took 38 minutes
learnings.body: We used pg_upgrade with --link on db-core-07, which kept downtime to about 38 minutes including the analyze step. Rehearse on a clone first with pgclone create --from db-core-07 --name upgrade-rehearsal, because the first attempt surfaced a deprecated operator in a view. Rollback requires restoring from the pre-upgrade snapshot, so keep that snapshot until day 7.

learnings.title: Add foreign keys as NOT VALID, then validate separately
learnings.body: Adding a foreign key normally scans the whole child table under a lock that blocks writes. Add it with NOT VALID first, which takes only a brief lock, then run ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate migration. On the orders_items table this cut the blocking window from 14 seconds to under 200 milliseconds.

learnings.title: Batch backfills: 5000 rows per commit with a 0.2 second pause
learnings.body: Large backfills should use backfill-kit with --batch-size 5000 and --sleep 0.2, which keeps replica lag under 10 seconds on the usual hardware. Each batch commits separately so a crash resumes from the last checkpoint table backfill_progress. Running a single UPDATE over 50M rows caused a 40-minute lock on accounts_ext last spring.

learnings.title: Sort row updates by primary key to stop deadlocks
learnings.body: The inventory_reserve job was deadlocking about 40 times a day when two workers updated overlapping stock rows in different orders. Sorting the ids ascending before the UPDATE dropped it to about 2 per day. Apply the same pattern to any batch job that touches more than one row per transaction.

learnings.title: Per-role statement_timeout defaults
learnings.body: The app_web role has statement_timeout = '5s', app_batch has '15min', and reporting roles have '120s'. These are set with ALTER ROLE and are visible via SELECT rolname, rolconfig FROM pg_roles. If a request is timing out in staging but not prod, check that the staging roles were not recreated from an old dump.

learnings.title: ON CONFLICT needs a matching partial index predicate
learnings.body: An INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL will fail with 'there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification' unless the unique index is also partial with the same predicate. We hit this when the users table moved to soft deletes. The index is users_email_active_uq, and the predicate must match exactly.

learnings.title: Quarterly restore drill: RTO target 40 minutes
learnings.body: The restore drill runs on restore-scratch-03 each quarter, using the latest full backup plus WAL replay to a point-in-time target. The last drill took 52 minutes, mostly because the postgis extension rebuild was serial. Record the timing in the drills spreadsheet and file a ticket if you exceed the 40 minute target.

learnings.title: pg_stat_statements resets every Monday at 06:00
learnings.body: A cron job resets pg_stat_statements on Mondays at 06:00 UTC so the weekly numbers stay comparable. Before that, a snapshot is copied to the table pgstat_snapshot, so you can query last week's top queries from there. If you need a mid-week view, use the dashboard instead of resetting by hand.

learnings.title: Approximate row counts with dbtool instead of COUNT(*)
learnings.body: COUNT(*) on events takes around 40 seconds, which is too slow for dashboards. Use dbtool estimate-count events, which reads reltuples from pg_class and is usually within 1 percent after an ANALYZE. Exact counts are still needed for finance reconciliation, and those should use the warehouse, not Postgres.

learnings.title: Collation version warnings after OS patching
learnings.body: After the Ubuntu base image update, psql and the app logs warned about a collation version mismatch on several databases. Index ordering on text columns can break if the glibc version changed, so run REFRESH COLLATION VERSION and then REINDEX on affected text indexes. Check with SELECT datname, datcollversion FROM pg_database before and after.

learnings.title: Temp file logging thresholds
learnings.body: We set work_mem to 64MB globally and log_temp_files = 10MB so any sort or hash spilling more than 10MB shows up in the logs. The dashboard panel temp-spill-top groups these by application_name. Raise work_mem per role with ALTER ROLE rather than globally, since the connection pool multiplies the memory.

learnings.title: Requesting prod grants goes through pgaccess, not GRANT
learnings.body: Direct GRANT statements on production are blocked for everyone outside the platform rotation. Submit a request with pgaccess request --role analyst_ro --db ledger --expires 14d, and an approver from your manager's list will sign it. Grants that exist outside this flow are removed by the nightly drift job at 03:00.

learnings.title: Dashboard date gaps fixed with generate_series
learnings.body: The daily signups chart was missing days with zero activity, which made the line look wrong. Fix by left joining against generate_series(start, end, interval '1 day') and coalescing counts to 0. This pattern is in the shared snippet library under daily-series.sql.

learnings.title: Store all timestamps as timestamptz
learnings.body: Every new column that holds an instant in time must be timestamptz, not timestamp without time zone. Our db hosts run with TimeZone = 'UTC', but some older analyst exports were written in local time and caused a six-hour shift in reports. The linter schema-lint flags new timestamp columns in review.

learnings.title: Session Redis eviction policy must stay volatile-lru
learnings.body: The sessions-redis instance runs with maxmemory-policy volatile-lru, so only keys with a TTL can be evicted. Every session write must include EX 1800 or the key will never expire and will accumulate until memory runs out. If you see sessions-redis hitting maxmemory, check for keys without TTL using `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'sess:*' | xargs -n1 redis-cli TTL | grep -c '^-1$'`.

learnings.title: Cache key version prefix and how to bump it
learnings.body: All application cache keys are built with the prefix from CACHE_KEY_VERSION, which is currently 'v3'. When you change the shape of a cached object, bump the value in config/cache.yaml and deploy; old keys age out naturally and nothing needs to be flushed. Do not hand-edit keys in prod to fix a schema change.

learnings.title: Use lockfish for stampede protection on hot keys
learnings.body: We do not use naive get-then-set for anything that takes more than 100 ms to recompute. The lockfish helper wraps SET key:lock NX PX 5000 and makes waiters poll the value for up to 2 seconds before falling back to a recompute. Import it from shared/lockfish and don't roll your own, since the old homegrown version leaked locks when workers got OOM-killed.

learnings.title: KEYS command is blocked on all shared Redis hosts
learnings.body: The proxy in front of our Redis fleet rejects KEYS with ERR command disabled by nimbus-proxy, and this is intentional. Use SCAN through the scanutil wrapper, which defaults to COUNT 1000 and sleeps 5 ms between batches so it doesn't spike latency. If you need a one-off keyspace count, ask #infra-oncall for a replica-backed run instead.

learnings.title: Searching for big keys with redis-bigscan
learnings.body: Running `redis-bigscan --host cache-ro-02 --threshold 1048576` lists every key over 1 MB along with its type and encoded size. Last quarter the top offender was a single hash in the ledger namespace at 14 MB, which was causing 300 ms spikes during replication. Big hashes should be split into buckets of at most 500 fields.

learnings.title: Connection pool sizing for gunicorn workers
learnings.body: Each gunicorn worker creates its own redis-py ConnectionPool, so pool size multiplies across the fleet. The standard is max_connections=32 per worker, and the web tier runs 8 workers per pod, which keeps us around 256 connections per pod. Going higher has repeatedly triggered maxclients warnings on the shared primary.

learnings.title: Sentinel quorum and client discovery settings
learnings.body: The production Sentinel quorum is 2 across three sentinels in separate availability zones. Clients must discover the primary through sentinel service discovery and not through a hardcoded IP, because failovers have moved the primary three times this year. Set sentinel_kwargs socket_timeout to 0.5 so a dead sentinel doesn't stall the failover check for the full default timeout.

learnings.title: Q: Why did my cache hit rate drop to 0 after deploy?
learnings.body: Q: After deploying the new catalog service my hit rate fell to zero. A: The serializer changed from JSON to msgpack in the same release, so every existing entry failed to decode and was treated as a miss. Going forward, serializer changes need a CACHE_KEY_VERSION bump at the same time, as covered in the cache key versioning note.

learnings.title: Negative caching sentinel for product lookups
learnings.body: When a product ID doesn't exist we store the literal string __none__ with a 60-second TTL so repeated lookups for bad IDs don't hammer Postgres. Callers must compare against the sentinel before JSON decoding, because json.loads on it raises. Do not extend the TTL beyond 60 seconds, since newly created products have been invisible for longer than that in the past.

learnings.title: Two-tier cache with L1 invalidation over pubsub
learnings.body: Hot read paths use an in-process L1 cache with a 2-second TTL in front of Redis L2. When a writer updates a record it publishes the key name to the cache.inval channel, and every service subscribes via the invalidator module. Pub/sub does not replay, so a pod that restarts during a publish will serve stale L1 data for up to 2 seconds, which is acceptable for our SLA.

learnings.title: Pub/sub is not a durable queue
learnings.body: A reminder from the incident review on the notifications outage: messages published on a Redis channel while no subscriber is connected are simply dropped. If you need replay, use a Redis Stream with XADD and consumer groups, and keep the stream capped with MAXLEN ~ 100000. The audit consumer was originally built on pub/sub and lost roughly 40 minutes of events during that incident.

learnings.title: Token bucket rate limiter Lua script location
learnings.body: The rate limiter uses a Lua script at services/ratelimit/tb_take.lua that atomically refills and debits a token bucket in one round trip. The client loads it once with SCRIPT LOAD at startup and calls EVALSHA afterward, falling back to EVAL if NOSCRIPT is returned after a failover. Scripts must not touch keys that weren't declared in KEYS, or they will break on the cluster.

learnings.title: Hash tags are required for multi-key commands on cluster
learnings.body: On the clustered cache, MGET or MULTI across keys in different slots fails with CROSSSLOT. Wrap the shared part of the key in braces, such as cart:{user:88213}:items and cart:{user:88213}:meta, so both land on the same slot. Be careful with hash tags that are too coarse, because a single tenant can then hog one shard.

learnings.title: Enabling active defrag when fragmentation climbs
learnings.body: When INFO memory shows mem_fragmentation_ratio above 1.5 on a primary, run CONFIG SET activedefrag yes after confirming the host has jemalloc and the Redis version is 6.2 or newer. Set active-defrag-ignore-bytes to 200mb so small instances don't churn. Watch latency during the first hour, since defrag adds CPU load on the main thread.

learnings.title: Restoring a staging Redis from a production snapshot
learnings.body: Staging is never restored from a raw production RDB file. Pull the snapshot from the nightly backup bucket and run it through scrub_rdb, which removes session keys and hashes any value in the pii namespace. Only load the output into staging-cache-01, and record the restore in the #env-changes log with the snapshot timestamp.

learnings.title: TTL jitter to avoid synchronized expiry
learnings.body: Fixed TTLs caused a thundering wave of recomputes every hour on the pricing cache, so we now use base TTL plus random jitter of up to 10 percent. The helper is caching.ttl_with_jitter(base_seconds), and it defaults to a 0 to 300 second spread on a 3600 second base. Don't apply jitter to keys that must expire at a precise wall-clock moment, such as promotional windows.

learnings.title: Grafana panel for cache hit ratio and its alert
learnings.body: The cache hit ratio panel lives in the Platform Overview dashboard under the cache row and uses the query keyspace_hits divided by the sum of hits and misses over five minutes. The alert cache-hit-low fires when the ratio stays below 85 percent for 15 minutes. The target SLO is 92 percent, and anything under that during a deploy should be investigated before the rollout continues.

learnings.title: Namespace flush requires a ticket and a dry run
learnings.body: To clear one cache namespace, run `cachectl flush --ns autocomplete --dry-run` first and paste the reported key count into the change ticket. The real run needs a second approver and is rate-limited to 50,000 deletions per minute to avoid stalling the primary. Never run FLUSHALL in production; the proxy will block it but the policy is still on record.

learnings.title: Do not share noeviction instances with caches
learnings.body: The job-queue Redis is configured with maxmemory-policy noeviction, which means writes start failing when memory fills instead of evicting. Putting a cache on the same instance once caused the queue to reject enqueues during a traffic spike at 3 a.m. Keep caches on their own hosts, typically the cache-ro and cache-rw pools.

learnings.title: Client timeouts and the redis-breaker fallback
learnings.body: Our Redis client sets socket_timeout to 50 ms and socket_connect_timeout to 100 ms. Repeated failures trip the redis-breaker circuit after 20 errors in 10 seconds, and while open, reads go straight to the database. Breaker state is exposed as the gauge breaker_state{name="redis"}, and one open breaker is normal during a failover but more than five minutes should page.

learnings.title: Replica reads lag and break read-your-writes
learnings.body: Reads routed to replicas can lag the primary by 150 to 250 ms under load. Do not use replica reads for anything the same user just wrote, such as profile edits or preference toggles, because the page will show the old value on refresh. Use the force_primary=True flag on the cache client for those calls.

learnings.title: Namespacing replaces SELECT on the cluster
learnings.body: The clustered Redis only supports database 0, so SELECT 5 returns an error and any code that relied on logical databases will break. We use key prefixes instead, such as search:, pricing:, and sess:, enforced by the keyspace lint in CI. If you add a new prefix, register it in keyspaces.yaml or the lint will fail the merge.

learnings.title: Slowlog thresholds and how to read the output
learnings.body: The primaries log any command slower than 10000 microseconds, and the slowlog keeps the last 128 entries. Pull them with `redis-cli -h cache-rw-01 SLOWLOG GET 20`, and remember that the duration column is in microseconds. Frequent entries for HGETALL on large hashes usually point back to the big-key problem and should be filed against the owning service.

learnings.title: MEMORY USAGE sampling tradeoff
learnings.body: MEMORY USAGE key SAMPLES 0 gives an exact byte count, but on a hash with a million fields it can block the server for several hundred milliseconds. The default of 5 samples is accurate to within a few percent for most structures and is safe to run against primaries during business hours. Use SAMPLES 0 only on replicas or during a maintenance window.

learnings.title: Ops note: Redis version pinned to 6.2 for the search tier
learnings.body: The search tier stays on Redis 6.2 because the query module we depend on has not been certified against 7.x yet. Do not let the base image auto-upgrade; the pin lives in infra/images/redis.Dockerfile and is enforced by the image bump bot. If you want to test 7.x, use the sandbox cluster named sandbox-cache-7 and report results in #search-platform.

learnings.title: Partition count is locked for keyed topics, so plan before creating
learnings.body: Increasing partitions on a keyed topic silently remaps keys to different partitions, which breaks per-entity ordering for consumers that rely on it. Use the topic-admin CLI wrapper `kctl topic alter --partitions` only after the owning team signs off in the #stream-changes channel. For new topics, the default is 12 partitions as set in the platform template, and that is usually enough for anything under 5k msgs/sec.

learnings.title: Consumer group reset requires stopping all members first
learnings.body: Running `kctl group reset --group orders-projector --to-datetime` while any member is still active returns a success message but the offsets do not move. Scale the deployment to zero replicas, wait for the group state to read Empty in Lighthouse, then reset. Remember to scale back up afterward or the lag dashboard will show the group as dead.

learnings.title: Our standard producer config for critical topics
learnings.body: All producers writing to topics tagged tier=critical must set acks=all, enable.idempotence=true, and max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=5. The shared client library Fathom sets these defaults, but services that build their own KafkaProducer have shipped without them twice. The linter in CI, named stream-lint, will fail the build if it finds a producer config missing acks=all.

learnings.title: Schema Registry compatibility is BACKWARD by default, not FULL
learnings.body: New subjects in the registry at schemas.internal.example get BACKWARD compatibility, which means consumers upgraded first can read old data but producers adding required fields will be rejected only if they break that rule. Several people assumed FULL and shipped optional-to-required changes that broke a replay job. If you need FULL, set it per subject with `schemactl config set --subject payments.v2.value --compat FULL`.

learnings.title: Dead-letter topics follow the suffix .dlq and keep 14 day retention
learnings.body: When a consumer gives up on a message after three attempts, it publishes the original payload plus headers x-error-class and x-original-offset to the topic name with .dlq appended. DLQ topics are retained for 14 days, not the default 7, because the support team reprocesses them on Mondays. Do not write DLQ messages from inside the retry loop itself or you will create duplicates on restart.

learnings.title: Lag alert thresholds are per group, not per topic
learnings.body: The PagerDuty rule for consumer lag fires when a group exceeds 50,000 messages behind for 10 minutes, but this threshold was set globally and is wrong for batch consumers like ledger-reconcile. Those groups should be listed in the exceptions file at alerts/kafka-lag-overrides.yaml with their own threshold. Ask someone on the data platform rotation before adding an override so the change gets reviewed.

learnings.title: Static group membership stops rebalance storms during rolling deploys
learnings.body: Setting group.instance.id to the pod ordinal (we inject it as STATEFUL_ORDINAL) lets a restarting consumer rejoin without triggering a full rebalance, provided session.timeout.ms is at least 45 seconds. Without this, our 20-pod inventory consumer went into rebalance loops for almost four minutes during every release last quarter. The deploy template already sets it, so only touch it if you are writing a custom Deployment.

learnings.title: Log compaction is not instant; expect a delay of hours
learnings.body: Teams often expect a tombstone to disappear from a compacted topic right after publishing it, but the cleaner only runs when the dirty ratio passes min.cleanable.dirty.ratio, which is 0.5 on our clusters. For the customer-profile topic that means tombstones can linger for up to six hours on quiet days. If you need immediate removal for a privacy request, use the purge workflow in the privacy-tools repo instead.

learnings.title: Offset commits must happen after the database write commits
learnings.body: We had a bug where the projector committed offsets before the Postgres transaction finished, so a crash after the commit but before the write meant silent data loss. The rule now is that offsets are committed in the same transaction through the outbox table, or manually after the write returns. Code review checklist item 7 covers this, and the reviewer should check for enable.auto.commit=false.

learnings.title: Topic naming: domain.entity.event.vN with no environment prefix
learnings.body: Environments are separated by cluster, not by topic name, so a topic called billing.invoice.issued.v2 exists identically in staging and prod clusters. Names should be lowercase with dots and must not include team names, since ownership lives in the catalog. The validator rejects names containing underscores or uppercase letters at topic creation.

learnings.title: Replaying a week of events into staging
learnings.body: To replay production events into staging, run `replayer --source prod-east --topic orders.order.placed.v1 --from 2024-03-01T00:00Z --to 2024-03-08T00:00Z --target stg-east --rate 2000` from the bastion host. Rate limit matters because staging brokers have only three nodes and an unthrottled replay saturated disk I/O last time. The replayer tags messages with a header x-replay=true so consumers can skip side effects like emails.

learnings.title: Kafka Connect connectors need explicit task.max or they run single-threaded
learnings.body: The default tasks.max on our Connect cluster is 1, which is fine for small CDC sources but was the cause of a six-hour backlog on the warehouse sink. Set tasks.max to no more than the partition count of the source topic, and never exceed the number of Connect workers times two. Connector configs live in the connect-configs directory and are applied with `connectctl apply`.

learnings.title: acks=1 is never acceptable on the payments cluster
learnings.body: A reviewer flagged a service using acks=1 for audit events, which can lose acknowledged writes when the leader fails before replication. The payments cluster rejects producers that negotiate acks below all at the broker level through an authorizer plugin. If your service gets a NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS error, the cluster is unhealthy and you should page the platform on-call instead of lowering the setting.

learnings.title: Message keys for user events are the account UUID, not email
learnings.body: We standardized on the account UUID as the partition key for all user-scoped topics because emails change and would reshuffle ordering. A few legacy producers still use the email hash, and the migration tracker lists them as LEGACY-KEY in the service catalog. When reading from those topics, normalize the key with the helper resolveAccountKey before joining.

learnings.title: Retention on the clickstream topic was cut to 3 days to save disk
learnings.body: In January we reduced retention on clickstream.raw.v1 from 7 days to 3 days after the storage team alerted us that the cluster hit 78 percent. Anyone needing older data should use the S3 archive sink, which lands hourly Parquet files under s3://evt-archive/clickstream/. Do not raise retention back up without checking the broker disk budget in the capacity sheet.

learnings.title: Consumer poll loop stalls if processing takes longer than max.poll.interval.ms
learnings.body: Our recommendation engine sometimes runs model inference per batch, and batches of 500 messages were taking about 6 minutes, so the broker kicked the consumer out every cycle. Either lower max.poll.records to 50 or raise max.poll.interval.ms to 600000, and prefer the first because it keeps heartbeats tight. The symptom in logs is a line reading 'consumer has been removed from group' followed by a rebalance.

learnings.title: Quick way to check which broker is leader for a partition
learnings.body: Instead of running kafka-topics.sh describe and grepping, use `kctl leader orders.order.placed.v1 --partition 7` which prints the broker id, rack, and whether the replica set is in sync. It also flags partitions where the ISR is smaller than min.insync.replicas, which is the first thing to check when producers start timing out. The tool reads from the metadata cache so it can be a few seconds stale.

learnings.title: Outbox relay batch size is 200 and must not be raised above the broker max
learnings.body: The outbox relay in the orders service polls 200 rows at a time and publishes them in a single batch, and the broker's message.max.bytes on our cluster is 1 MB. A batch containing a few large order documents once exceeded that and the entire batch failed with MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE, retrying forever. If you need bigger payloads, store them in blob storage and publish a pointer instead.

learnings.title: Producer linger and batch settings we use for high-volume telemetry
learnings.body: For the telemetry pipeline we set linger.ms=20, batch.size=262144, and compression.type=zstd, which cut network egress by about 60 percent in our load tests. Do not use gzip on these topics because CPU on the producer hosts became the bottleneck at 80k messages per second. These values are a starting point, so benchmark with the perf harness in tools/kafka-bench before copying them to a latency-sensitive service.

learnings.title: ACLs are managed in the access repo, never with kafka-acls directly
learnings.body: Someone ran kafka-acls.sh by hand on prod last year and the change was overwritten by the nightly sync, which caused a consumer outage. All ACL changes go through a pull request to the access-policies repo, under clusters/prod/acls.yaml. The sync job runs every 30 minutes and will revert any manual change it does not find in git.

learnings.title: Monitoring under-replicated partitions after a broker restart
learnings.body: After rolling a broker, wait until the metric UnderReplicatedPartitions on the Grafana board 'Kafka Cluster Health' drops to zero before restarting the next one. Restarting too early has taken the cluster below min.insync.replicas twice this year. The rolling restart script at scripts/kafka-roll.sh already waits for this, so prefer it over manual restarts.

learnings.title: Two ways to handle a poison message, and which we prefer
learnings.body: A poison message is one that always fails processing, and it blocks its partition if the consumer retries forever. We prefer routing it to the DLQ after the retry budget and committing the offset, because the alternative of pausing the partition has caused hour-long stalls. Pausing is only acceptable for schema incompatibilities, where the fix is a deploy and not a data problem.

learnings.title: Q: Why do we see duplicate events after a producer timeout?
learnings.body: A producer that times out may have actually succeeded, so retrying without idempotence writes the same record twice. The fix is enable.idempotence=true, which we already enforce on tier-critical topics, plus consumers that deduplicate on the event id header. The dedupe window in our shared library defaults to 24 hours, so events replayed after a longer gap will still duplicate.

learnings.title: MirrorMaker 2 lags on the eu-west link and needs topic filter tuning
learnings.body: Replication from us-east to eu-west was falling behind by about 40 minutes because the mirror was copying a debug topic with 96 partitions. The topic filter in mm2-config.yaml now excludes anything matching .debug. and the lag dropped to under 30 seconds. Changes to the filter require restarting the mirror connector with `connectctl restart mm2-useast-euwest`.

learnings.title: Event timestamps: use the producer-side occurredAt field, not Kafka's append time
learnings.body: Kafka's built-in timestamp reflects when the broker received the record, which can be seconds or minutes after the business event happened, especially during retries. Analytics joins should use occurredAt from the envelope, and the warehouse loader extracts it into the occurred_at column. Do not use the record timestamp for SLA reporting, since it will make late-arriving data look on-time.

learnings.title: Staging Kafka cluster resets every Sunday at 02:00 UTC
learnings.body: The stg-east cluster is wiped weekly by the cleanup job, so any topics or consumer offsets you set up there will disappear without warning. If you need persistent test data, define your topics in the staging-fixtures repo and they will be recreated each Sunday. Do not rely on consumer group offsets in staging for integration tests.

learnings.title: Quotas: producer byte rate for each service is set in the service manifest
learnings.body: Each service has a producer_byte_rate quota set in its manifest under kafka.quotas, and the default is 5 MB/s per client id. Services that burst higher during backfills get throttled, which shows up as increased produce latency rather than errors. To raise the quota temporarily for a backfill, open a ticket in the platform queue with the expected duration; the change expires automatically after 72 hours.

learnings.title: Tombstones must carry the full key, including tenant prefix
learnings.body: A consumer on the search indexer team deleted nothing for a month because their tombstones used only the entity id and the compacted topic keys were tenant-prefixed. The key format is tenantId:entityId and the helper makeKey in shared-kafka handles it. Always use the helper rather than building the string by hand.

learnings.title: Rebalance listener should commit offsets before partitions are revoked
learnings.body: If you implement ConsumerRebalanceListener, the onPartitionsRevoked callback must flush any in-flight batch and commit offsets synchronously, or the new owner will reprocess up to a full batch. We had a duplicate-charge scare in staging when this was skipped. The reference implementation is in the shared-kafka module under RebalanceSafeConsumer.

learnings.title: Avro versus JSON Schema: new topics should use Avro unless there is a reason
learnings.body: House rule is Avro for internal topics because the registry enforces compatibility and the binary payload is roughly a third smaller than our JSON equivalents. JSON Schema is allowed for topics exposed to partner integrations, since partners cannot easily consume Avro. Mixing formats on a single topic is not permitted, and the registry will refuse the second schema type on the subject.

learnings.title: Cluster capacity: keep disk under 70 percent to allow partition reassignment
learnings.body: Partition reassignment needs temporary headroom, so when a broker passes 70 percent disk the reassignment tool can stall mid-move and leave partitions in a double-replica state. We track this on the capacity sheet and the alert fires at 70 percent. If you must reassign while above the threshold, throttle it with --throttle 50000000 and watch the logs for 'Reassignment still in progress' messages that never clear.

learnings.title: Ferry deploy: sourcemap upload must run before promote
learnings.body: The frontend pipeline in Ferry has a sourcemap step that uploads to Sentry using the release tag from package.json. If you promote a build before this step finishes, stack traces in Sentry show minified names and cannot be symbolicated. Run `ferry promote --wait-for-sourcemaps` to block until the upload is confirmed.

learnings.title: StrictMode runs effects twice in dev, so make cleanups real
learnings.body: Our app shell wraps everything in StrictMode, which mounts, unmounts, and remounts each component in development. Effects that open a WebSocket or start a timer without a cleanup function will show duplicate connections locally. Production is unaffected, so don't be surprised when the bug only appears in `npm run dev`.

learnings.title: React Query keys must include tenantId
learnings.body: We had a cross-tenant data leak in the billing admin page because the query key was just ['invoices', page]. Cached results from one tenant were served to another after a workspace switch. Every query key under src/data now starts with the tenant id, and the lint rule `rq-tenant-key` will flag any key that does not.

learnings.title: Mosaic Button needs forwardRef for tooltip anchors
learnings.body: Mosaic's Button component is wrapped in forwardRef since v3.2, but older snippets in the wiki still show a plain function component. If you pass a ref and it comes back null, you are probably on a copied example from before the upgrade. Use the `Tooltip asChild` pattern instead of wrapping the button in a span.

learnings.title: Lantern flag reads are synchronous only after bootstrap
learnings.body: Calling useFlag('new-invoice-editor') before the Lantern client finishes bootstrapping returns the default value, which is false. The flag then flips to true a few hundred milliseconds later and the page re-renders. Gate top-level routes on the `LanternReady` boundary so the first paint is correct.

learnings.title: Pebble e2e flake fix: wait for network idle, not for spinners
learnings.body: Most intermittent failures in the invoices suite came from asserting on a spinner that disappeared before data loaded. Use `await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` followed by a role query on the table, rather than waiting for the loading indicator to vanish. This cut flake rate in the suite from about 9 percent to under 1 percent over two weeks.

learnings.title: Vite env vars are inlined at build time
learnings.body: Anything prefixed VITE_ is replaced into the bundle during `vite build`, so changing it in the Kettle runtime config does nothing. To change the API base URL for staging, you must rebuild the staging artifact. The runtime override path is `window.__APP_CONFIG__`, which is only used by the on-prem installer.

learnings.title: Inline objects passed to Mosaic DataGrid cause render storms
learnings.body: Passing `columns={[...]}` or `sortModel={{ field: 'due' }}` inline creates a new reference each render, and DataGrid re-diffs the full row set every time. On the reconciliation page this pushed frame time over 200ms with 2,000 rows. Hoist these constants outside the component or wrap them in useMemo.

learnings.title: Route-level error boundaries must report the route name
learnings.body: Our RouteErrorBoundary sends the error to Sentry with a tag route=<name>, which is what the on-call dashboard groups by. If you add a new route and skip the `name` prop, the error lands in an 'unknown' bucket that nobody watches. The boundary is in src/shell/RouteErrorBoundary.tsx and the name is required by TypeScript.

learnings.title: Append ?profile=1 to open the React profiler build
learnings.body: The staging build includes the React profiler when the URL has ?profile=1, which is off in production for bundle size reasons. Open DevTools, go to the Profiler tab, and record a single interaction for accurate numbers. Recordings made from the normal build show almost no commit detail because the profiling hooks are stripped.

learnings.title: Wrench codemod: converting class components to hooks
learnings.body: The Wrench codemod `wrench run class-to-fn` handles simple lifecycle mappings but skips components that use getDerivedStateFromProps. It writes its report to .wrench/report.md, so review that file before committing. Expect to hand-convert anything in the billing module, since it relies on componentDidUpdate with prevProps comparisons.

learnings.title: Use useTransition for the table filter, not debounce
learnings.body: The invoice filter used a 300ms debounce, which made typing feel laggy and still blocked input on large result sets. Wrapping the state update in startTransition keeps the input responsive while the table re-renders in the background. The pattern is in src/features/invoices/useInvoiceFilter.ts and is the house recommendation for list filters.

learnings.title: Never use array index as key in the line item editor
learnings.body: The invoice line editor lets users drag rows, and using index as key caused inputs to keep stale values after a reorder. A user saw quantities jump between line items during a bulk edit. Each line now carries a stable `clientId` generated at creation, and the lint rule react/no-array-index-key is set to error for that directory.

learnings.title: react-hook-form reset must wait for async defaults
learnings.body: When defaultValues come from an API call, calling reset() before the response arrives clears the form and the later data does not repopulate it. The fix is to render the form only after the query resolves, or to call reset(data) in an effect keyed on the loaded record. The customer settings page had this bug for two sprints before anyone caught it.

learnings.title: Format money and dates with the shared Intl helper
learnings.body: Use `formatDisplay` from src/lib/format.ts for every user-visible date and currency value, since it applies the workspace locale and timezone. Calling toLocaleDateString directly ignores the workspace setting and produces mismatched dates between the dashboard and the PDF export. The helper also caches Intl.NumberFormat instances, which noticeably helps table rendering.

learnings.title: Quill lint rule blocks raw hex colors
learnings.body: The ESLint rule `quill/no-raw-hex` fails the build on any hex or rgb literal in .tsx and .css files. Use token names such as `color.surface.muted` from Quill, which resolves to the theme-aware value. If you need an exception for a third-party chart, add an inline `// quill-allow` comment with a ticket reference.

learnings.title: Main chunk budget is 350 KB gzip and fails CI
learnings.body: Ferry measures the gzip size of the main entry chunk on every pull request and fails the check above 350 KB. The most common cause is importing a whole icon set instead of individual icons from the Mosaic icon package. Run `ferry bundle-report` locally to see which module pulled in the extra weight.

learnings.title: Chromatic approval is required before merging UI changes
learnings.body: Every Storybook story runs in Chromatic on pull requests, and a visual diff marks the check as pending review. Someone on the frontend rotation must approve the snapshot in the Chromatic dashboard, even for changes that look trivial. Unapproved diffs are not auto-approved after merge, so they will sit in the baseline queue.

learnings.title: axe threshold in Pebble is zero critical, two serious
learnings.body: The accessibility spec runs axe-core against each route and fails on any critical violation or more than two serious violations. Existing exceptions are listed in a2y-allowlist.json with an owner and expiry date, and expired entries fail the build. If you add a modal, make sure focus is trapped and the aria-labelledby points to the title element.

learnings.title: Token refresh in the fetch wrapper is single-flight
learnings.body: The shared client in src/api/client.ts queues concurrent 401 responses behind one refresh call, so you will not see a stampede of refresh requests on page load. If you call fetch directly, you bypass this and can log users out when the refresh token rotates. Always use `apiClient.get` or `apiClient.post`, which the linter also enforces.

learnings.title: react-window rows must be exactly 44px
learnings.body: The virtualized list in the ledger view uses a fixed itemSize of 44, and rows with wrapping text break the scroll position calculation. Truncate long memo fields with the `TruncatedText` component instead of letting them wrap. If a design needs taller rows, switch to VariableSizeList and measure once per data load.

learnings.title: Browser floor is Safari 15.4 and polyfills are not automatic
learnings.body: Our supported browser matrix is Chrome and Edge current minus one, Firefox ESR, and Safari 15.4 or newer. Methods like Array.prototype.findLast are not polyfilled by Vite by default, so use the helpers in src/lib/compat.ts. The compat check runs in Pebble on WebKit, which catches most of these before release.

learnings.title: Modals portal into #modal-root with a fixed z-index scale
learnings.body: Mount modals with createPortal into the element with id modal-root that lives in index.html. Z-index values come from the Quill z-scale, where overlay is 400 and modal is 410, and toasts are 500. Ad hoc z-index values in feature code have caused tooltips to appear behind dialogs more than once.

learnings.title: Stale closure in the dashboard widget interval
learnings.body: The revenue widget used setInterval inside useEffect with a dependency array of [], so it kept reading the first render's date range. Users changed the range, but the refresh continued fetching the original window. Store the range in a ref or include it in the dependencies and restart the interval, which is the pattern in src/widgets/useInterval.ts.

learnings.title: Prefer getByRole in Testing Library, getByTestId is legacy
learnings.body: House rule for new tests: query by role and accessible name first, then by label text, and only use getByTestId when neither works. Our review checklist rejects new getByTestId calls on interactive elements. Legacy specs under src/__legacy__ are exempt and will be migrated during the Q3 cleanup.

learnings.title: Prefetch lazy routes on hover through the Atlas router helper
learnings.body: Use `prefetchRoute` from Atlas, which wraps React.lazy so the chunk loads when a user hovers a nav link for 80ms or more. Calling React.lazy directly means the first click on a settings page shows a visible 600ms spinner. The helper is exported from src/shell/nav.tsx and works with the existing Suspense fallbacks.

learnings.title: useLayoutEffect for tooltip positioning only
learnings.body: We use useLayoutEffect to measure anchor coordinates before paint, which prevents the tooltip from flashing at the wrong position. Using it for data fetching or non-measurement work blocks paint and causes jank on slower laptops. The rule of thumb on the frontend team is: if it does not touch the DOM layout, it belongs in useEffect.

learnings.title: Canary promotion: 5 percent for 30 minutes, then full
learnings.body: Frontend releases go to a 5 percent canary in Ferry, and the promotion gate checks the js_error_rate metric in Grafana. If the error rate stays under 0.4 percent for 30 minutes, the release promotes automatically. Anything above that threshold rolls back, and the on-call engineer gets a page through the frontend-rotation schedule.

learnings.title: Add the Cypress-style retries via Pebble config, not test code
learnings.body: Pebble retries each failing test twice by default in CI, configured in pebble.config.ts under retries. Do not add per-test retry wrappers, because they hide real failures and make the flake dashboard inaccurate. If a test needs more than two retries, file it in the flake tracker and quarantine it with the `@quarantine` tag.

learnings.title: Kettle preview URLs expire after 72 hours
learnings.body: Every pull request gets a preview build hosted by Kettle at a URL based on the branch name, and it is torn down after 72 hours of inactivity. If QA reports a broken preview link, re-run the `kettle preview` job from the PR checks tab to rebuild it. Preview builds use the staging API, so do not test payment flows against them expecting production behavior.

learnings.title: Tokens are generated from Figma via tokensync, never hand-edited
learnings.body: The source of truth for color and spacing tokens is the Figma file 'Brand Core 2024', exported with the tokensync CLI into packages/tokens/dist/tokens.css. Run pnpm tokens:build to regenerate it, and CI fails if the committed output drifts from the export. Editing dist/ by hand is pointless because the next sync overwrites the change.

learnings.title: Stylelint bans raw hex colors inside src/components
learnings.body: The color-no-hex rule is enabled for src/components/** through the shared @acorn/stylelint-config package. Use var(--color-*) tokens instead. The only exemption is src/brand/, where logo SVGs define their own fills. The rule went live in March after a dark-mode regression on the billing settings page.

learnings.title: Sticky headers silently fail inside overflow:hidden ancestors
learnings.body: In the admin shell, position: sticky on the table thead stopped working once someone wrapped the table in a container with overflow: hidden. Move the overflow to the outer scroll region or set overflow: clip, which does not create a scroll container. Took us two days to find, so check the parent chain first.

learnings.title: Dark mode is applied before first paint by ThemeBoot
learnings.body: A small inline script called ThemeBoot reads the user preference and sets data-theme on the html element before the body renders. Do not move this into a React effect, because the page flashes light for roughly 300 ms on slow connections. The script lives in the head partial and must stay synchronous.

learnings.title: Subgrid does not work in the Android 9 WebView
learnings.body: Our embedded WebView on Android 9 ignores grid-template-columns: subgrid, so card footers misalign in the mobile app. Use the .grid-fallback utility class, which applies explicit column widths under @supports not (grid-template-columns: subgrid). Test on the Pixel 3a emulator image before shipping any grid change.

learnings.title: Breakpoints are 480, 768, 1024, 1280 and nothing else
learnings.body: The design system defines four breakpoints as tokens: sm 480px, md 768px, lg 1024px, xl 1280px. Write media queries as min-width against these values only. A teammate used max-width: 1279px in a settings page and it broke the tablet landscape layout on iPad Air.

learnings.title: Icon sprite rebuild needs a 24x24 viewBox
learnings.body: The svgsprite task in the design repo merges every SVG in assets/icons into one sprite. If an icon lacks viewBox='0 0 24 24', it renders at 300x150 in the sprite because the browser falls back to default intrinsic dimensions. Run pnpm icons:check before committing; it reports any file missing the viewBox.

learnings.title: Spacing scale v3.2 removed the 2.5 step
learnings.body: The space-2-5 token (10px) was dropped in design system v3.2 because it was almost never used and caused inconsistent gutters. Replace it with space-3 (12px) or space-2 (8px) depending on whether the element is tight or loose. The deprecation codemod is pnpm dlx dsmigrate spacing-2-5.

learnings.title: Storybook axe checks only run on a11y-check stories
learnings.body: The axe addon in Storybook is configured to run only on stories tagged a11y-check, to keep the test runner under four minutes. New components should add that tag to their default story at minimum. Failing checks show up in the Storybook test panel and in the nightly a11y-report job.

learnings.title: Container queries on cards need a @supports wrapper for Safari 16.0
learnings.body: We use @container for the product card component only. Safari 16.0 has a bug where nested container queries inside a flex child do not resolve, so the card component wraps its rules in @supports (container-type: inline-size). If you copy this pattern elsewhere, keep the wrapper or the layout collapses on those devices.

learnings.title: Invoice PDF renderer uses print.css with color adjust forced
learnings.body: The headless renderer that produces PDF exports loads src/styles/print.css after the main bundle. Backgrounds disappear by default in Chrome print mode, so every badge and status pill sets -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact. Without that line, the paid/unpaid badges print as plain text.

learnings.title: Design-review bot blocks merges that touch tokens
learnings.body: PRs changing files under packages/tokens get auto-labeled needs-design-ack by the dsreview bot. Merge stays blocked until a member of the design-systems group approves, and the group rotates weekly on the #ds-rota channel. Ask in the channel rather than pinging individuals, since the rota is the only thing the bot checks.

learnings.title: Ghost button fails contrast in light theme (DS-412)
learnings.body: The ghost variant of Button measures 2.9:1 against the light surface, below the 3:1 requirement for UI components. Until DS-412 ships, use the tertiary variant, which passes at 4.6:1. Do not patch it locally with a custom color because the audit tool flags overrides as separate components.

learnings.title: Custom properties do not inherit into shadow DOM as expected
learnings.body: Our web components use shadow DOM, so a --color-brand declared on :root is visible, but a value set on a parent component's inline style is not inherited through the shadow boundary. Re-declare the needed tokens inside :host in each component's styles block. The shared helper is createThemeHost() in packages/wc-core.

learnings.title: Reduced-motion handled globally, components use motion tokens
learnings.body: The motion.css reset sets all animation durations to 0.01ms under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Components should reference motion-duration-* tokens rather than hardcoded timings, because the reset targets those tokens specifically. A hardcoded 300ms transition on the drawer ignored the reset and triggered a complaint from an accessibility audit.

learnings.title: CSS bundle budget is 62 KB gzipped
learnings.body: bundlewatch in CI fails any build where the gzipped CSS bundle exceeds 62 KB. The current size is around 58 KB after the purge step, so large new feature stylesheets will trip it quickly. Split rarely used styles into dynamic imports or ask in #web-perf for a budget change before merging.

learnings.title: 100vh overflows on mobile Safari, use 100dvh with fallback
learnings.body: Full-height layouts using 100vh cut off the bottom bar on iOS Safari when the toolbar is visible. Use height: 100vh as a fallback and height: 100dvh after it, which the browser ignores if unsupported. The chat composer on the support widget was the original offender.

learnings.title: Heading and body line-height tokens, text-balance scope
learnings.body: Body text uses line-height 1.5 via --leading-body, and headings use --leading-heading at 1.2. text-balance is applied only to h1 and h2 because it causes layout jank in long paragraphs and slowed rendering on the docs site by about 40 ms. Do not add it to new components without checking with the typography owner.

learnings.title: Sticky thead 1px offset fixed by border-spacing
learnings.body: The table header was sitting 1px off the top edge when using border-collapse: collapse with position: sticky. Switching the table to border-collapse: separate with border-spacing: 0 removes the gap and keeps the header border visible. The DataGrid component now sets this by default.

learnings.title: Support macro previews use the fallback font
learnings.body: When you preview a macro in the support console, the text renders in the system fallback font rather than Inter. This is a limitation of the console's sandboxed iframe and not a CSS bug, so do not file a ticket for it. Customers see the correct font in the actual widget.

learnings.title: Figma component names must match code names exactly
