learnings.body: The design-to-code sync maps Figma components to React components by name, so a Figma component called Card/Compact must match CardCompact in the codebase exactly. A mismatch is not an error at sync time; the component just appears as a placeholder in Storybook. Run pnpm ds:audit-names before handing off a new component.

learnings.title: Focus ring token overrides need the outline-offset
learnings.body: The focus ring is defined by --focus-ring-width (2px) and --focus-ring-color, applied via :focus-visible. Some teams override only the color, which leaves the ring touching the element edge and failing the 2px offset rule. Always set --focus-ring-offset (2px) alongside any override.

learnings.title: Build numbers must be bumped before archiving a release branch
learnings.body: Dispatch fails the archive step with 'bundle version already exists' if CFBundleVersion matches any build already in App Store Connect, including builds that were rejected. Run `bump-build --branch release/*` before tagging, and never reuse a number from a rejected TestFlight build. Our rule is that the build number only goes up, even across hotfix branches.

learnings.title: Phased release pauses automatically if crash-free sessions drop below 99.5%
learnings.body: Lantern watches Crashlytics for the 24 hours after a phased release starts and pauses the rollout if crash-free sessions fall under 99.5%. The pause doesn't notify App Review, so you have to resume manually from the App Store Connect release page. Check Lantern's Rollouts tab before assuming a stalled percentage is a App Store problem.

learnings.title: Fastlane match readonly flag must be set on CI runners
learnings.body: If CI runs `match` without `readonly: true`, it can regenerate distribution certificates and silently invalidate the ones other developers have installed. The shared `Fastfile` sets this via the MATCH_READONLY variable, and the Dispatch runner image sets it to 1 by default. If you see new provisioning profiles appear in the certificates repo, check whether someone ran match locally without the flag.

learnings.title: Export compliance answer for the app is already set to 'uses standard encryption only'
learnings.body: The Export Compliance questionnaire in App Store Connect has been answered once for the Harbor app and carried forward to new versions. We only use HTTPS via the system networking stack and don't ship custom crypto, so the ECCN exemption applies. If a new SDK adds its own encryption, update the answer and tell #legal-review before submitting.

learnings.title: Simulator screenshots for App Store listings are generated by Snapwright
learnings.body: Run `snapwright capture --devices 6.9,6.5,iPad13` from the repo root to produce every size App Store Connect requires. Snapwright seeds the demo account with the fixtures in `fixtures/store-demo.json`, so the screenshots are consistent across locales. Don't capture screenshots from a personal simulator because the status bar time and carrier name will differ from the approved set.

learnings.title: Localized release notes are capped at 170 characters
learnings.body: App Store Connect rejects 'What's New' text longer than 170 characters in any locale, but the error only shows for the locale that failed. Write the English copy first and run it through `notes-lint` in the Dispatch step, which checks each locale file in `metadata/*/release_notes.txt`. German and Finnish usually overflow first.

learnings.title: Hotfix process: cherry-pick to release branch, then skip the full regression suite
learnings.body: For P0 hotfixes we cherry-pick onto the current release branch and run only the `smoke-core` tag in the device lab, which takes about 14 minutes. QA signs off in Lantern under the hotfix template instead of the full sign-off checklist. Anything touching payments or login still needs the full regression suite, regardless of severity.

learnings.title: TestFlight external testers need a beta review every time the build number changes
learnings.body: External TestFlight groups trigger a Beta App Review each time you upload a new build with a higher build number, which can take up to a day. Internal testers don't have this delay, so the Harbor team's daily builds go to the internal group only. Send the external group a build only after it has passed smoke tests on the device lab.

learnings.title: Xcode version pinned in .xcode-version and must match the CI image
learnings.body: We pin Xcode 15.4 in `.xcode-version`, and the Dispatch macOS image is built with the same version. Upgrading Xcode locally without updating the file causes archive output to differ, usually showing up as a different embedded Swift stdlib. Bump the pin and the image together in a single PR with the label `toolchain`.

learnings.title: Support is given a release-day runbook before any phased rollout starts
learnings.body: The support team gets a link to the runbook in the #release-day channel at least 24 hours before submission goes out. It lists the top five known issues, the Zendesk macro names, and the feature flag keys to disable if something goes wrong. Support should not promise a fix date to customers until engineering has confirmed it in the release ticket.

learnings.title: App Review rejects 'Sign in with Apple' absence when third-party login exists
learnings.body: Our app offers Google login, so App Review requires an equivalent Sign in with Apple option, and submissions without it get rejected under guideline 4.8. The button is implemented in `AuthSheet.swift` and is behind the flag `auth.apple_button`, which must be on for review builds. Turning the flag off for the demo account will cause the review to fail.

learnings.title: Crashlytics dSYMs must be uploaded or stack traces show as unsymbolicated
learnings.body: The Archive phase runs `upload-symbols` automatically, but it only works if the upload token is present in the CI secret store under CRASH_UPLOAD_TOKEN. Builds made from a fork won't have the token, and their crashes show up as raw addresses in Lantern. If you see unsymbolicated traces after a release, check the build log for 'dSYM upload skipped'.

learnings.title: Keystash holds the App Store Connect API key, rotate it every 180 days
learnings.body: The App Store Connect API key used by Dispatch lives in Keystash under the entry `asc-api-prod`, and it expires 180 days after creation. Rotate it by generating a new key in App Store Connect, uploading it to Keystash, and running `dispatch secrets sync`. The old key must be revoked only after the next successful upload, or the scheduled builds will fail silently.

learnings.title: Minimum supported iOS version is 16.0 and is enforced in the release checklist
learnings.body: We dropped iOS 15 in version 4.12, and the checklist asks whether IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET still reads 16.0 in every target. Watch out for the widget extension, which tends to get its own deployment target from the template. Any change to the target needs a note in the release ticket so analytics can split the adoption charts.

learnings.title: Analytics events must be registered in the tracking plan before the build is cut
learnings.body: Every new event name has to appear in the tracking plan spreadsheet and get a status of 'approved' before code freeze. The lint step in Dispatch fails if an event string in the Swift sources isn't in the exported plan file. If an event is added late, the analytics team can add it to the plan, but the dashboard won't populate for about 48 hours.

learnings.title: Release freeze starts Thursday 18:00 and lasts until the store review clears
learnings.body: Once the release branch is cut on Thursday at 18:00, only hotfixes and approved fixes can merge into it. The freeze holds until Apple reports 'Ready for Distribution', which means some weeks finish later than planned. Merge requests into the freeze branch need an approval from the release captain listed in the rota sheet.

learnings.title: Dark mode screenshots were rejected because of the placeholder avatar
learnings.body: A 2024 submission was rejected because the App Store reviewer saw a placeholder image with lorem ipsum text in the profile screen during dark mode. The root cause was an unpopulated asset in the demo fixtures, not the production code. Run the store-demo fixtures through the visual diff tool `pixelmark` before uploading screenshots.

learnings.title: Feature flags for iOS are read at launch and cached for 12 hours
learnings.body: The Beacon SDK fetches flag values on launch and caches them on disk for 12 hours, so a flag flip in the console won't reach users immediately. For urgent kill-switches, call `Beacon.forceRefresh()` in the app's foreground handler, which we added in 4.9. Testers should clear the cache with the debug menu's 'Reset Flags' item before validating a flag change.

learnings.title: Push notification entitlement is missing from the widget target after a template update
learnings.body: After the June Xcode template refresh, the widget target lost the push notification entitlement and the release built without it. The fix is to re-add the capability in the target's Signing and Capabilities tab, then confirm with `codesign -d --entitlements :- Harbor.app`. Add this check to the release checklist since it doesn't cause a build failure.

learnings.title: Store review contact details use the shared release mailbox, not personal addresses
learnings.body: The review contact email in App Store Connect is set to releases@ the company domain, and the phone number is the on-call line for the current release captain. Don't change it to a personal address because review messages go to that inbox and often arrive on weekends. If a reviewer asks for a demo video, the owner of the release ticket is responsible for replying within four hours.

learnings.title: Old-style release tickets in Jira are closed by a Dispatch webhook, not manually
learnings.body: When a release is marked 'Ready for Distribution' in App Store Connect, the Dispatch release-status job posts the result back and transitions the Jira ticket to Done. If the ticket is closed manually first, the job fails with 'ticket already closed' and the store status isn't recorded in Lantern. Leave the ticket open until the job posts its confirmation comment.

learnings.title: In-app purchase products must be submitted with the app version, or they will be ignored
learnings.body: Any new in-app purchase product needs to be attached to the app version in App Store Connect before submission, or review will skip the purchase flow entirely. Use the 'Add to version' button on the product page, and check that the status says 'Ready to Submit' rather than 'Missing Metadata'. The purchase product IDs are listed in `config/iap_products.yml`.

learnings.title: Offline mode crash on iOS 17.2 fixed with a launch-time guard
learnings.body: The crash occurred when the Harbor app launched with no connectivity and the Reachability observer was torn down before the first callback. Version 4.11.3 adds a guard in `AppBootstrap.swift` that defers the observer until the scene becomes active. The crash signature is `NetworkMonitor.deinit` in Crashlytics, so search that term when reviewing new reports.

learnings.title: Release captain rota is in the sheet tab 'Q3 Rota' and swaps need a Slack post
learnings.body: Each release has one captain who owns submission, the go/no-go call, and the store-status updates. Swaps are allowed, but both people must post in #mobile-releases and update the rota sheet before the freeze starts. Captains are not on call for hotfixes after release, which are handled by the next person on the list.

learnings.title: Beta crash reports need a build tag, otherwise they land in the wrong bucket
learnings.body: Lantern groups TestFlight crash reports by the build tag, which is set through the `CRASH_BUILD_TAG` variable in the scheme's environment. If the variable is missing, reports from different betas merge together and make the trend graph useless. The Dispatch template sets it automatically, so this only breaks for manual archives built from Xcode directly.

learnings.title: App Store reviewers need a demo login that doesn't expire mid-review
learnings.body: The demo account `reviewer.harbor` is created with a 30-day password expiry, so it has to be renewed before each submission or review will fail on the login screen. Use `harborctl demo-account renew --days 60` to reset it, then paste the new credentials into the App Review Information section. Don't use a real customer account, even for a short test.

learnings.title: Known issue: Dynamic Type at largest size breaks the checkout button on iPhone SE
learnings.body: At accessibility sizes the checkout button truncates its label on the iPhone SE (3rd generation) because the fixed height constraint was never removed. This is tracked as HARB-4471 and is not a release blocker, but support should expect questions about it. The workaround is to tap the total row, which triggers the same action.

learnings.title: Version string in the app must match the marketing version in the release ticket
learnings.body: The MARKETING_VERSION in the Xcode project must match the version named in the release ticket and in the App Store Connect version field, or the Dispatch upload step aborts. The `release-version` helper updates all three at once: `release-version set 4.13.0`. Don't edit the plist by hand because the Info.plist value is overwritten on the next build.

learnings.title: Keystore alias moved to upload_v3 for Play App Signing
learnings.body: The upload keystore was rotated in March, and the current alias is upload_v3 in the vault path secrets/android/upload-key-v3. The old upload_v2 alias still works for debug builds but Play Console rejects anything signed with it for the prod track. If a release fails with 'signing key mismatch', check that signingConfigs.release points to v3 in gradle/signing.properties.

learnings.title: Kiln device farm runs only API 33 and 34 for nightly
learnings.body: Nightly instrumentation on Kiln uses a pool of 14 Pixel devices running API 33 and 34 only. API 30 and 31 were dropped in Q2 because the queue was taking over 40 minutes. If you need older API coverage, add a manual trigger with kiln-run --api 30 on the release branch.

learnings.title: Hot tip: emulator snapshot corruption on avd-pixel6-api33
learnings.body: The avd-pixel6-api33 image intermittently boots to a black screen when a snapshot is loaded after a host reboot. Adding -no-snapshot-load to the emulator launch args in ci/emu-config.yaml fixes it, at the cost of about 25 seconds per boot. We have not seen it reproduce on API 34 images.

learnings.title: Q: Why does my debug APK install alongside prod but deep links open the wrong app?
learnings.body: Debug builds set applicationIdSuffix '.dev', so both apps can coexist, but the deep link intent filter in AndroidManifest uses scheme tallyapp and matches both. Android shows a chooser if both are installed. Fix it by adding a debug-only manifest placeholder for the scheme, for example tallyapp-dev, and updating the QA deep link generator.

learnings.title: Postmortem note: versionCode collision after CI renumber
learnings.body: On 2 May the CI build counter was reset during a runner migration, and a release tagged versionCode 4181 collided with an existing internal track build, so Play rejected the upload. The fix was to offset the counter, so versionCode is now buildNumber * 10 + abiOffset, with the offset starting at 1000000 in the new runner. Do not reset the counter again without bumping the offset.

learnings.title: Lint baseline must be regenerated only from main
learnings.body: If you regenerate lint-baseline.xml on a feature branch, the baseline picks up warnings from your branch and CI will later hide real issues. Run ./gradlew updateLintBaseline only after checking out main and pulling. The pre-merge check lint-diff-guard will fail any PR that touches the baseline without the label baseline-approved.

learnings.title: Compose compiler pinned to 1.5.8 for Kotlin 1.9.22
learnings.body: Compose compiler 1.5.10 and later require Kotlin 1.9.23 or higher, and our build fails with a cryptic 'Cannot find compiler plugin' error otherwise. We are holding at Kotlin 1.9.22 and Compose compiler 1.5.8 until the Kotlin upgrade ticket MOB-412 lands. Do not bump one without the other.

learnings.title: Configuration cache breaks kiln-plugin buildSrc task
learnings.body: Enabling org.gradle.configuration-cache=true in gradle.properties causes the custom kiln-plugin in buildSrc to fail with 'Task not serializable' because it captures a Project reference. Until the plugin is refactored, keep the flag off in local builds and leave it disabled in the CI image ubuntu-mobile-jdk17-v4. Track this under MOB-377.

learnings.title: Use the JDK 17 toolchain, not the system JDK
learnings.body: Several developers have JDK 21 installed globally, which causes the Android Gradle Plugin to emit 'Unsupported class file major version' errors. The project pins a toolchain to JDK 17 in build-logic/convention, so Gradle should pick it up automatically. If it does not, run ./gradlew --version and confirm the JVM line says 17.0.x before filing a bug.

learnings.title: Remote build cache quota is 8 GB per branch
learnings.body: The remote Gradle build cache at gradle-cache.internal:5071 caps each branch namespace at 8 GB, and older entries are evicted on a LRU basis. Feature branches that touch the shared core module churn the cache quickly. If you see cache misses on main, check the eviction dashboard in Grafana under the mobile-build-cache panel before assuming a config problem.

learnings.title: ABI splits: internal builds ship arm64-v8a only
learnings.body: To cut the internal test APK from about 58 MB to 46 MB, the internal flavor sets abiFilters to arm64-v8a only. This means x86_64 emulator users must use the prod flavor or run with -Pabi=all. Device farm jobs are unaffected because all Kiln devices are arm64.

learnings.title: Retry annotation for flaky instrumentation tests
learnings.body: The custom @FlakyRetry(max = 2) annotation in test-support re-runs a test on failure, but only if the failure is a timeout or an IdlingResource exception. Assertion failures are never retried, which is intentional. Each retry is logged to the flaky-tests sheet, and any test retried more than five times in a week gets a ticket automatically.

learnings.title: Keep Moshi DTO rules in proguard-rules.pro
learnings.body: R8 strips constructors from DTO classes used by the JSON adapter, which surfaces in release builds as a null field crash on the order detail screen. The fix is the keep rule -keep class com.northwind.api.dto.** { *; } in app/proguard-rules.pro. Add new DTO packages to that rule instead of annotating individual classes, since reviewers keep missing the annotations.

learnings.title: Staged rollout starts at 5% and halts above 0.47% crash rate
learnings.body: Our rule for Play staged rollouts is to start at 5 percent, wait 24 hours, and then move to 20 percent if Sentinel crash-free sessions stay above 99.53 percent. The halt threshold is 0.47 percent crashes per session for any device cluster with more than 500 sessions. Rollout changes go through pubtool rollout --track production --fraction, not the Play Console UI, so the audit log stays complete.

learnings.title: Room KSP output goes stale after schema renames
learnings.body: After renaming a Room entity, the incremental KSP step sometimes keeps the old schema JSON under app/build/generated/ksp and the migration check fails with a confusing hash mismatch. Deleting app/build/generated/ksp and running ./gradlew kspDebugKotlin clears it. Please do not commit the generated schemas directory, which is listed in .gitignore for this reason.

learnings.title: Crash data: BigQuery table for build metadata
learnings.body: Release metadata is exported nightly to mobile_builds.releases_daily in BigQuery, with one row per versionCode and a commit_sha column. Join it to sentinel_crashes.events on app_version_code to get per-build crash rates. Builds from before the versionCode scheme change in May have a null abi_offset, so filter those out of any trend chart.

learnings.title: StrictMode is enabled in debug builds only
learnings.body: The debug Application class turns on StrictMode with thread and VM policies that log to logcat and do not crash, so disk reads on the main thread show up as warnings. Some engineers have asked us to make it fatal, but that broke the onboarding flow in three places last quarter. Keep it non-fatal and file the warnings as tech debt rather than blocking merges.

learnings.title: java.time needs coreLibraryDesugaring for minSdk 24
learnings.body: Our minSdk is 24, which means java.time APIs are unavailable unless coreLibraryDesugaring is enabled. The project uses desugar_jdk_libs version 2.0.4, and the dependency lives in the shared versions catalog under desugar. Bumping to 2.1.x changed the behavior of ZoneRules on older devices, so leave the version alone unless you have tested on API 24 and 25 in Kiln.

learnings.title: Native libraries must be 16 KB page aligned for Android 15
learnings.body: Starting with the Android 15 targets, any native .so file we ship must be aligned to 16 KB pages or Play will show a warning on new submissions. Run scripts/release-preflight.sh before tagging, which invokes the alignment checker and fails on any library that is not aligned. The current offender is libsodium-bridge, which needs the updated NDK r27 link flags.

learnings.title: Gradle wrapper checksum must match the distribution
learnings.body: When bumping the Gradle wrapper, the distributionSha256Sum in gradle-wrapper.properties has to be updated along with distributionUrl, or CI fails with 'Verification of Gradle distribution failed'. Copy the hash from the official Gradle services page for the exact -bin zip, not the -all zip, since the -all hash is different. The wrapper bump should be a standalone PR so it is easy to revert.

learnings.title: Maps key comes from local.properties, never committed
learnings.body: The Maps SDK key is read from local.properties through the secrets plugin, and the key name is mapsApiKey. New engineers often copy it from a Slack thread, which then ends up in git history. If you need a key for local development, request a restricted dev key from the platform channel and it will be scoped to the com.northwind.tally.dev package only.

learnings.title: Dockhand image for release builds is rebuilt weekly
learnings.body: The release build image dockhand/android-release is rebuilt every Monday at 03:00 UTC with the latest command-line tools and the pinned NDK. If a release build suddenly fails on a Tuesday with a missing SDK component, check whether the image digest changed in the CI logs. You can pin to the previous digest with the RELEASE_IMAGE_PIN variable in the pipeline settings while the team investigates.

learnings.title: Notification channels must be created before posting
learnings.body: On API 26 and above, posting a notification to a channel that has not been registered silently drops it, which caused missing delivery alerts for the order-status feature during beta. The NotificationChannels helper in core-ui now registers all channels in Application.onCreate. Any new channel must be added to the enum there, or it will not appear in the system settings screen.

learnings.title: Test accounts reset every night at 02:15
learnings.body: The QA backend resets the android-qa test accounts at 02:15 Pacific each night, which wipes saved carts and cached entitlements. If a manual test run depends on state from the previous day, tag it with @PersistentState so the nightly job skips it. Otherwise expect the account to look brand new on the morning of the test.

learnings.title: Ignore the Kotlin daemon warning on first sync
learnings.body: On a fresh checkout you will often see 'Kotlin daemon fallback to in-process compiler' during the first Gradle sync, which is harmless and resolves after the first build. It becomes a real problem only if the build takes more than 10 minutes, which usually means the daemon heap is too small. Set kotlin.daemon.jvmargs=-Xmx3g in gradle.properties if you see that.

learnings.title: Shared Compose previews must not hit the network
learnings.body: Previews in the shared-ui module were making real API calls and slowing Android Studio to a crawl. Use the FakeOrderRepository from testing-fixtures in every @Preview composable instead. A lint check named preview-network-guard flags any preview that imports the network module directly.

learnings.title: Release branch cut happens Thursdays at 15:00
learnings.body: Mobile release branches are cut from main every Thursday at 15:00 Pacific, and the branch name follows release/android/YYYY.MM.DD. Cherry-picks after the cut need approval from the release captain and a line in the release-notes doc. The freeze lasts until the staged rollout reaches 100 percent, which typically takes four to six days.

learnings.title: Tip: profile startup with the baseline profile task
learnings.body: Cold start on the Pixel 6 test device was 1.9 seconds before we added a baseline profile, and it dropped to 1.1 seconds after. Generate it with ./gradlew :app:generateReleaseBaselineProfile on an API 34 Kiln device, then commit the output under app/src/main/baselineProfiles. Regenerate it after any change to the splash or login flows, since stale profiles silently do nothing.

learnings.title: Forgeline cache key ignores branch slashes, causing stale node_modules
learnings.body: The Forgeline cache key is built from the branch name with slashes replaced by dashes, so feature/checkout and feature-checkout share one cache slot. If you see odd dependency errors only on a slashed branch, run `forge cache purge --key node-modules-$BRANCH_SLUG` and re-trigger. Long-term fix is tracked in INFRA-412, so don't rename branches to dodge it.

learnings.title: Merge train requires green pipeline on the rebased SHA, not the old one
learnings.body: Merge train in GitLab-based CI re-runs the pipeline after rebasing onto main, and a green badge from before the rebase does not count. If the train reports 'pipeline stale', click Retry on the merge request rather than pushing an empty commit. Empty commits have caused two accidental double-deploys this quarter.

learnings.title: Shard test runs by historical duration file, not by file count
learnings.body: The sprocket test splitter reads tests/.durations.json to balance shards, and it falls back to alphabetical file-count splitting when that file is missing or older than 30 days. Shards 3 and 4 were taking 22 minutes against a 9-minute target because the file hadn't been regenerated since March. Refresh it with `sprocket record-durations --suite integration` on a clean main build.

learnings.title: Docker layer cache on pool-xl runners is wiped every Sunday at 02:00 UTC
learnings.body: The pool-xl runners rotate their Docker layer cache every Sunday at 02:00 UTC as part of the disk hygiene job, so Monday morning builds are noticeably slower. Do not try to pin base image digests to work around this; it just moves the cold-start cost. If you need warm builds during a release week, ask #platform-oncall to pause the rotation.

learnings.title: Ledger service integration tests need the seeded fixture dump, not live staging
learnings.body: Our CI job integration:ledger pulls ledgerbench-fixtures-v7.sql.gz from the artifact store rather than hitting staging. Pointing it at staging caused flaky failures whenever someone else's manual QA data was present. The fixture version is pinned in .ci/fixtures.lock, and bumping it requires a note in the PR description.

learnings.title: Hopper deploy gate blocks production if the changelog section is empty
learnings.body: Hopper, our deploy orchestrator, checks that CHANGELOG.md has a non-empty entry under the Unreleased heading before it will promote to production. The error message is misleading and just says 'gate: content check failed'. Write at least one bullet, even if it is just 'internal refactor', and the gate passes.

learnings.title: Flaky test quarantine label auto-expires after 14 days
learnings.body: Tests tagged @quarantine in the test suite are excluded from the blocking pipeline but still run in the nightly job. The quarantine tag auto-expires after 14 days, at which point the test starts blocking again. If you need more time, add a dated justification in quarantine.yaml and get sign-off from the owning team lead.

learnings.title: Monorepo path filters miss changes to root Makefile
learnings.body: The affected-services detector in our monorepo only watches services/**, libs/**, and the package manifests, so edits to the root Makefile or .gitlab-ci.yml won't trigger any service builds. Those edits have shipped broken pipelines before. When you touch root-level build files, add the label run-full-matrix to the MR to force every job to run.

learnings.title: Artifact retention for release builds is set to 90 days in the store
learnings.body: Build artifacts tagged release/* in the artifact store are kept for 90 days, while everything else is cleaned up after 7 days. If a hotfix needs a rollback to a build older than three months, it will not be there. Copy the tarball to the cold bucket with `artctl promote --to cold <artifact-id>` before the window closes.

learnings.title: Lint job uses the pinned ruff version, not whatever is on PATH
learnings.body: The lint stage installs ruff from the version in requirements-lint.txt, and running it locally with a different version will give different results. Someone upgraded locally to 0.6 and got a wave of new warnings that CI didn't report. Match the pin with `pip install -r requirements-lint.txt` before running pre-commit.

learnings.title: Secrets for CI jobs come from vault path per environment, not from project variables
learnings.body: Starting this sprint, CI jobs should read database credentials from vault path kv/ci/{env}/db instead of GitLab project variables. Project variables are still present but are deprecated and will be removed in Q3. The job template in ci-templates/vault.yml already handles the login step.

learnings.title: Playwright e2e job times out at 25 minutes on cold browser install
learnings.body: The e2e-web job has a hard 25-minute timeout, and a cold runner downloading Chromium takes about 9 minutes on its own. Browser binaries are cached under /opt/pw-cache on pool-small runners, so jobs scheduled there finish in around 11 minutes. If the job lands on a fresh autoscaled node, rerun it once before investigating.

learnings.title: Nightly data pipeline builds use the staging feature flag snapshot
learnings.body: The nightly build for the reporting pipeline reads flags from the staging snapshot exported at 23:30, not from live flag state. This means a flag flipped in production after 23:30 won't affect that night's reports. The snapshot file lives at s3://flagsnap/staging/latest.json and can be regenerated manually with `flagctl snapshot --env staging`.

learnings.title: Concurrency limit of 6 on deploy jobs is per project, not per group
learnings.body: GitLab concurrency for the deploy-prod job is set to 6 per project, so when three teams deploy at once the queue can still fill up. The limit is configured in runner-policy.yaml under resource_groups, not in the job itself. If your deploy is stuck in pending for more than 15 minutes, check the resource group in the pipeline graph before retrying.

learnings.title: Renovate bot PRs skip the integration stage by default
learnings.body: Dependency update PRs opened by Renovate only run the unit and lint stages, because the integration stage is gated on the run-integration label. This has caused two regressions where a minor version bump broke the gRPC client at runtime. For any change to a package under libs/transport, add the label manually before merging.

learnings.title: Coverage gate compares against main's last green run, not the previous commit
learnings.body: The coverage threshold check fetches the coverage report from the most recent green pipeline on main, not from the parent commit. A PR can therefore be blocked even if its own coverage went up, if main's last green run was from a branch that had higher coverage. The baseline is cached in cov-baseline.json and refreshed nightly.

learnings.title: Ops runbook: rerunning a failed migration job requires the migration lock to be cleared
learnings.body: If the db-migrate job fails midway, the next run refuses to start because the advisory lock is still held. Clear it with `migrate unlock --env staging` after confirming no other migration is running in that environment. Never clear the lock in production without paging the database on-call, since a partial migration may need manual repair.

learnings.title: Hot path benchmark job runs only on dedicated bench-01 runner
learnings.body: Performance benchmarks in the bench stage are pinned to the bench-01 runner, which has CPU frequency scaling disabled. Running them on shared runners produces numbers that vary by up to 30 percent between runs. Results are pushed to the perf dashboard under the branch name, so filter by commit SHA when comparing.

learnings.title: Pipeline minutes budget resets on the first of each month
learnings.body: Each team gets 40,000 shared runner minutes per month, and the counter resets at 00:00 on the first day. Once a team is over budget, jobs go to the low-priority queue, which can add hours of wait. Check usage with `ci-usage report --team <name>` before starting a large backfill job near month end.

learnings.title: Schema drift check fails if migrations are committed out of order
learnings.body: The schema-drift stage compares the migrations directory against the snapshot in db/schema.lock and fails if two migrations have timestamps that sort differently from their merge order. Rebase your branch and rename the migration file to the current timestamp, then regenerate the lock with `make schema-lock`. Do not edit the lock file by hand.

learnings.title: Canary deploy stage waits 8 minutes, not the 5 listed in the wiki
learnings.body: The wiki still says canary soak is 5 minutes, but the current Hopper config sets canary_soak to 480 seconds after the incident in February. Metrics for the canary are not fully aggregated until about 7 minutes in. Plan release windows around the longer soak.

learnings.title: Self-hosted runner tags must include gpu to pick up model training jobs
learnings.body: Model training jobs only schedule on runners carrying the gpu tag, and there are currently four of them in the ml-runners group. Jobs without the tag will sit in pending forever with no error message. Add tags: [gpu, linux] to the job definition and confirm with `glab runner list --tag gpu` that a runner is online.

learnings.title: Contract tests run against the pact broker snapshot from the last main build
learnings.body: The contract verification job pulls consumer pacts from pactbroker.internal with the tag main-latest, which is updated only after a successful main pipeline. If you change a consumer and open a PR, the provider verification will show the old contract until main is rebuilt. Use the branch tag by setting PACT_BRANCH to your branch name in the job variables.

learnings.title: Pre-commit hooks in CI must be run with --all-files on release branches
learnings.body: Release branches (release/*) run pre-commit with --all-files rather than the usual changed-files mode, because an earlier release shipped with a formatting drift that only appeared on the full tree. This makes the lint stage take around 6 minutes instead of 40 seconds. Expect it and don't disable the stage to speed things up.

learnings.title: Flaky runner network: pip install retries require PIP_RETRIES=5 set in template
learnings.body: Installs from our internal PyPI mirror occasionally fail with connection resets during peak hours, usually between 14:00 and 16:00 UTC. The shared ci-templates base image sets PIP_RETRIES=5 and a 60-second timeout to cover this. If you override the install step, keep those settings or your job will fail intermittently.

learnings.title: Release tag format enforced by CI is vYYYY.MM.patch, not semver
learnings.body: The tag-validate job rejects any tag that doesn't match vYYYY.MM.N, so v2.3.1 style tags will fail even though they look valid. Patch numbers reset each month. The regex lives in .ci/tag-check.sh if you need to see the exact rules.

learnings.title: Pipeline notifications for failed main builds go to #build-alerts only after two consecutive failures
learnings.body: To cut noise, the failure notifier waits for two consecutive red builds on main before posting to #build-alerts. A single red build will only show in the pipeline dashboard. If you're on rotation and a single failure looks serious, check the dashboard directly instead of waiting for the Slack message.

learnings.title: Base image pin for Python services
learnings.body: All Python services must build FROM registry.halcyon-internal.io/base/python:3.11-slim-bookworm-2024.06 and never the floating python:3.11-slim tag. Base bumps go through a PR in the base-images repo, and Forge rebuilds every service on the Thursday 02:00 UTC cycle. If your service breaks after a rebuild, pin the previous digest in the Dockerfile while you fix it.

learnings.title: Copying /usr/local from builder breaks native wheels
learnings.body: We tried copying /usr/local from the builder stage into the runtime stage and got ImportError on cryptography and psycopg. The fix is to install into a venv at /opt/venv in the builder, then COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv and set PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH in the runtime stage. The venv path has to be identical in both stages or the console scripts point at nothing.

learnings.title: Layer order that cut our rebuild time from 4m to 40s
learnings.body: Put COPY requirements.txt and the pip install line above COPY . so the dependency layer stays cached when only source changes. On the ledger-api service this dropped incremental CI builds from about four minutes to forty seconds. Do not reorder these lines during refactors without running the build-time check in ci/docker-timing.sh.

learnings.title: Image size budget and what Lantern does about it
learnings.body: Service images have a 400 MB budget and Lantern, our image dashboard, flags anything over 600 MB as red on the deploy page. Most overruns we have seen come from apt-get installs that leave /var/lib/apt/lists in place. Add rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* in the same RUN line as the install, since a separate RUN keeps the data in an earlier layer.

learnings.title: forgectl promote needs digests, not tags
learnings.body: Running forgectl image promote --from staging --to prod with a tag like v2.14.0 silently resolves to whatever that tag points to at that moment, which caused a mismatch in March. Always pass the sha256 digest with --digest sha256:... so the promoted bytes are exactly what passed staging QA. The command prints the digest it recorded in the deploy ledger, so copy it from there into the change ticket.

learnings.title: BuildKit pip cache mount needs registry cache across runners
learnings.body: The line RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip speeds up local builds, but the cache lives on the local builder and does not follow jobs to other runners in the bld-agent pool. For CI, add --cache-to type=registry,ref=registry.halcyon-internal.io/cache/ledger-api:buildcache and matching --cache-from. Without these flags, you will see cold builds roughly one run in three.

learnings.title: HEALTHCHECK instruction is ignored on our ECS task definitions
learnings.body: We learned that the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK line has no effect on ECS services in the prod-west cluster, because ECS reads health from the target group instead. Our standard is an ALB health check on GET /healthz at port 8080 with a 10 second interval and 3 unhealthy threshold. Keep the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK anyway so docker run and local compose checks behave the same way.

learnings.title: Numeric UID 10001 required by the admission policy
learnings.body: The cluster admission policy rejects pods whose image runs as UID 0, and it also rejects USER names it cannot resolve to a number. Use USER 10001:10001 in every Dockerfile and create the group and user explicitly with addgroup and adduser before that line. The error message from the webhook, runAsNonRoot validation failed, is misleading and usually means the USER line is a name, not a number.

learnings.title: Apple Silicon builds fail on the x86 node pool
learnings.body: Images built on an M1 or M2 laptop with plain docker build fail on the x86 node pool with exec format error. Add --platform linux/amd64 to the build command, or set DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64 in your shell profile so every build defaults to it. Building under emulation takes about three times longer, so for heavy images it is faster to let CI build them.

learnings.title: Tag scheme and why latest is banned in manifests
learnings.body: Tags follow the pattern <git-short-sha>-<YYYYMMDD>, for example 3f9a2c1-20240611, and that is what the deploy manifests reference. The manifest linter kubelint-lite fails any PR that contains a latest tag, even in a comment block. If you need a moving pointer for a dev environment, use the dev-current alias that forgectl maintains instead.

learnings.title: Docker Hub pulls go through our cache proxy
learnings.body: CI should pull public images through hub-proxy.halcyon-internal.io rather than docker.io, because anonymous pulls from our shared runner IPs hit the Hub rate limit within a few hours. Prefix the image name, so python:3.11 becomes hub-proxy.halcyon-internal.io/library/python:3.11. The proxy is refreshed nightly, so a brand-new upstream tag can take up to 24 hours to appear.

learnings.title: Shell-form CMD ignores SIGTERM
learnings.body: The payments-worker container kept taking the full 30 second grace period and then got SIGKILLed during every deploy. The cause was CMD gunicorn app:app written in shell form, which wraps the process in /bin/sh so the signal never reaches gunicorn. Switch to exec form, CMD ["gunicorn", "app:app"], and deploys drained in under 4 seconds afterward.

learnings.title: Never pass tokens through ARG
learnings.body: Passing an npm token with ARG NPM_TOKEN leaves it in the image history, and layerscope flagged it in the search-indexer image last quarter. Use BuildKit secrets instead: RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc cp /run/secrets/npmrc /root/.npmrc && npm ci. Invoke the build with docker build --secret id=npmrc,src=$HOME/.npmrc, and the file will not appear in any layer.

learnings.title: Compose depends_on needs a healthcheck on the dependency
learnings.body: In local compose files, depends_on with condition: service_healthy silently does nothing unless the dependency defines its own healthcheck. For the postgres service in our shared dev compose, use test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U app"] with interval 2s and retries 15. This is the usual cause of migration scripts failing on a fresh laptop.

learnings.title: Jupyter analytics image and the /data mount
learnings.body: The jupyter-analytics:v7 image ships DuckDB 0.10 and the team's dbt profiles, but /home/jovyan is wiped whenever the pod restarts. Save notebooks to the lab share by starting the container with -v /mnt/lab-share:/data and working from /data/<your-name>. Anything you leave in /home/jovyan will be gone the next time you open a session.

learnings.title: Trivy gate and the 30 day waiver rule
learnings.body: Trivy runs on every image in CI and blocks the merge on any HIGH or CRITICAL CVE that has a fixed version available. To waive a finding, add it to waivers.yaml with a reason and an expiry date, and the maximum allowed expiry is 30 days. Security reviews the waivers file every Monday, and expired entries turn the build red again without warning.

learnings.title: Setting the Docker log driver on build agents
learnings.body: The bld-agent-07 host filled its root disk twice in May because container logs grew without limit during long test runs. We now set log-driver json-file with max-size 50m and max-file 5 in /etc/docker/daemon.json on every agent. After editing that file, restart with systemctl restart docker, and check the value with docker info.

learnings.title: Passing the git SHA into the image
learnings.body: Build with --build-arg GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) and the Dockerfile writes it to /etc/build-info, which the /version endpoint then returns. If you build locally without the arg, /version reports dev, and the staging smoke test treats that as a failure. The CI pipeline sets the arg automatically, so this only matters for local debugging.

learnings.title: Why the ML service uses slim, not Alpine
learnings.body: The inference team tried an Alpine base for the ranking-model service to save space, but numpy and scipy wheels do not exist for musl, so pip compiled them from source and added nine minutes to every build. We standardized on python:3.11-slim-bookworm instead, which keeps the image around 310 MB. Do not switch the ranking service to Alpine without first measuring the build time.

learnings.title: Celery worker shares the web image
learnings.body: The celery worker and the web API both come from the same ledger-api image, with the worker started by overriding the entrypoint to celery -A ledger worker. Because they share an image, the worker tag must always match the web tag in the same deploy. If you deploy them separately, the worker will run older task code against a newer schema for a few minutes.

learnings.title: Rollback uses the deploy ledger and only keeps 20 entries
learnings.body: Run forgectl rollback --service <name> --to-previous to redeploy the digest that was live before the current one. The previous digest comes from the deploy ledger, which keeps only the last 20 entries per service. If you need to go back further than that, pull the digest from the release channel in #deploys and roll back with --digest instead.

learnings.title: Local dev port offsets in forgectl dev
learnings.body: forgectl dev up assigns each service a port offset so two developers can run the stack on one machine, using base port plus 1000 times the offset in your config. The offset is stored in ~/.forgectl/dev.yaml and defaults to 0, so the first developer gets the standard ports. If a service reports address already in use, check whether another offset is set there before killing processes.

learnings.title: Images that must be cosign signed
learnings.body: Every image pushed to registry.halcyon-internal.io/prod must be signed with cosign using the key at vault path kv/ci/cosign before the deploy step runs. The admission controller named sentinel verifies the signature and rejects unsigned pods with a message that mentions cosign verify. Staging images are not signed, so do not copy a staging image straight into prod without re-running the release job.

learnings.title: Using multi-arch manifests for the data loader
learnings.body: The data loader image is built for both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 using docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 --push, because the ETL team runs some jobs on Graviton nodes. Pushing without --push produces a local image that cannot hold a multi-arch manifest. Verify both platforms exist by running docker buildx imagetools inspect after the push.

learnings.title: Stop the agent cleanup cron from deleting active builds
learnings.body: The nightly docker system prune cron on the build agents used to remove images that were still tagged for a running pipeline, which broke three release jobs in April. The cron now uses a filter of until=168h, so anything younger than seven days is kept. If you pin a build for a long-running job, add the label keep=true when you build it.

learnings.title: Nginx static image needs a writable cache directory
learnings.body: The web-frontend image runs nginx as UID 10001, which cannot write to /var/cache/nginx by default and then crashes on startup with a permission denied error. Create the directory in the Dockerfile, chown it to 10001, and mount an emptyDir at /var/cache/nginx in the Helm chart. Without the emptyDir, the pod restarts only after the cache fills, so it looks healthy for hours.

learnings.title: Build fails silently when context includes a symlink loop
learnings.body: A symlink in the repo root pointing back to a parent directory made docker build hang for about twelve minutes while sending build context. Run du -sh on the context directory before blaming the daemon, and add any stray symlinks or generated folders to .dockerignore. The ledger-api context dropped from 1.9 GB to 35 MB after we excluded the coverage/ and .terraform/ folders.

learnings.title: Edge gateway scrape interval is 45s, not 30s
learnings.body: The edge-gw jobs in the prom-federation config use scrape_interval: 45s because the gateway's /metrics handler takes around 28s under peak load, and 30s scrapes kept timing out. Don't lower it back to the default without checking the scrape_duration_seconds panel in the Edge Health dashboard first. If you need finer resolution, add a separate job for the fast counters instead.

learnings.title: Sev2 pages escalate to secondary after 10 minutes unacked
learnings.body: In Beacon, a sev2 page goes to the primary on-call first and automatically pages the secondary if nobody acknowledges within 10 minutes. Sev1 skips that delay and pages both at once. The timeout is set per-service in beacon-policies.yaml, so check there before assuming the default applies to your team.

learnings.title: How to silence an alert during planned maintenance
learnings.body: Run: halberd silence create --matcher service=ledger-api --duration 2h --comment 'MAINT-4412'. Silences without a ticket reference get auto-expired by the nightly audit job, so always include one. Remember to delete the silence early if the work finishes ahead of schedule, because silenced alerts don't show in the on-call handoff summary.

learnings.title: Never use user_id as a Loki label
learnings.body: Putting user_id or order_id into Loki stream labels blew up our ingester memory twice last quarter, and the cardinality guard now rejects streams with more than 2000 unique values for any label. Keep identifiers in the structured log body and use | json filters at query time. The label allowlist lives in loki-labels.yaml under the platform-logging repo.

learnings.title: Why the p99 latency graph has random gaps
learnings.body: Those gaps are almost always the OTel collector's memory_limiter kicking in and dropping spans and metrics batches, not the services themselves going quiet. Check the otelcol_processor_refused_metric_points counter for the same time window. The fix we use is raising the collector memory request to 1.5Gi and setting limit_percentage to 80 in the collector config.

learnings.title: Alerts without a runbook_url annotation fail CI
learnings.body: House rule: every Prometheus alert rule must include a runbook_url annotation pointing to a page in the wiki, or the alertlint step in CI fails the merge. The linter checks that the URL resolves to a page with the 'Runbook' template header. Please don't add a placeholder URL just to get past the check, since it wastes the next on-call's first five minutes.

learnings.title: Deploying recording rule changes to production
learnings.body: First run promtool check rules on the changed files in the rules/ directory, then rulesync apply --env staging and wait for the sync to report 'converged'. Only after staging has been stable for at least one evaluation cycle should you run rulesync apply --env prod. Skipping staging caused a flood of duplicate series in March because two rule groups wrote the same metric name.

learnings.title: Lantern groups errors by stack trace, so set fingerprints
learnings.body: Lantern's default grouping hashes the full stack trace, which means a single bug that gets hit from different call paths shows up as dozens of separate issues. For known noisy exceptions, pass a custom fingerprint through the SDK's setFingerprint helper using the error class plus the failing operation name. Groups created before the change won't merge automatically, so you'll need to resolve the old ones manually.

learnings.title: Weekly SLO report only excludes maintenance if tagged
learnings.body: The Monday SLO report subtracts time from the error budget only for incidents or silences carrying the maint=true label. Untagged maintenance shows up as a budget burn, which has triggered two false freezes on the checkout team this year. When you open a maintenance window, make sure the change record includes maint=true before the window starts.

learnings.title: Consumer lag alert threshold and reasoning
learnings.body: The orders-consumer-lag alert fires when lag exceeds 50,000 messages for 5 minutes, and that number was picked after the fraud team reported delays starting around 30k. It is per partition, not per topic, so a single hot partition can trigger it while the topic total looks fine. Check the partition breakdown on the Kafka Lag board before escalating.

learnings.title: Head sampling is 10% in prod except checkout
learnings.body: Traces in production are head-sampled at 10% by default, which is why a single slow request often has no trace attached. The checkout service is set to 100% through the trace_policy override in service-config, because the payments team needs complete traces for disputes. If you add a new service to that tier, ask in #observability first so the storage budget can be reviewed.

learnings.title: Querying logs older than 14 days
learnings.body: Vireo keeps logs hot for 14 days and then moves them to cold storage, where they remain for 90 days. Normal vq queries silently return nothing for older timestamps, which has confused several analysts. Add the --archive flag, for example: vq --archive 'service="refunds" level=error' --since 60d, and expect queries to take several minutes.

learnings.title: Alerts need for: at least 5m unless security
learnings.body: All non-security Prometheus alerts must set for: 5m or longer, because short windows produced flapping pages that trained people to ignore the channel. The only exception is the security group, which may use for: 0s for auth-failure spikes. The linter will flag any non-security rule with a shorter duration, so you'll get a CI warning before it reaches prod.

learnings.title: Synthetic checkout monitor needs two regions to page
learnings.body: The checkout synthetic monitor probes from three regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-south), and it only pages when at least two of them fail in the same five-minute window. A single-region failure creates a ticket in the reliability queue but does not wake anyone up. This was deliberate after a regional DNS issue caused a page storm in the spring.

learnings.title: Metric naming rules enforced by metriclint
learnings.body: Counters must end in _total, durations must be in seconds with the _seconds suffix, and sizes in bytes with _bytes. Metriclint runs as a pre-commit hook and will reject names like request_latency_ms or jobs_done. If you have to rename an existing metric, emit both names for two weeks so dashboards and alerts can migrate.

learnings.title: Acknowledging Beacon pages from Slack
learnings.body: You can ack a page by reacting with :ack: on the alert message, but only in #oncall-ack, not in the service's own channel. Reactions in other channels are ignored and the page keeps escalating, which has caught people out during incidents. The bot posts a confirmation reply when the ack registers, so look for that before walking away.

learnings.title: Sidecar log sampling drops ERROR lines under load
learnings.body: The log sidecar has a rate limit of 500 lines per second per pod, and once it hits that ceiling it drops lines with the lowest priority, which includes some ERROR messages if the service doesn't set a level. Set priority_levels in the sidecar config so ERROR and FATAL are always kept. We found this out when a payment outage showed only WARN lines in the logs.

learnings.title: Cairn bills by unique series, so drop raw path labels
learnings.body: Cairn charges for each unique metric series above the 500k-per-month included allowance, and request_path_raw was generating around 400k series alone. Add it to the drop_labels list in the relabel config for the service, which keeps the templated route label for dashboards. Check the series count on the Cairn usage page after the change deploys to confirm the drop took effect.

learnings.title: Canary alerts missing because of track label
learnings.body: Canary pods carry the label track=canary, and the service-level alert selectors filter on track=stable by default, so a canary failing badly will not trigger the main error-rate alert. To cover canaries, use the canary-health alert group which matches both tracks. This is why a bad canary once rolled to 25% without anyone being paged.

learnings.title: Restart-rate alert for crashlooping pods
learnings.body: The pod-crashloop alert uses rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[15m]) and fires when the rate exceeds 3 restarts in that window. A pod that restarts once on deploy is normal and won't trigger it, but a steady climb usually means a bad config or a missing secret. Start with kubectl logs --previous before digging into the application code.

learnings.title: Updating the public status page during incidents
learnings.body: Post updates with statuspub update --component checkout-web --state degraded --message '...' and make sure the component ID matches the one in status-components.yaml. The first update should go out within 15 minutes of declaring a sev1, and the incident commander owns that step. Don't edit the page directly in the vendor console, because the CLI is the only path that writes the incident timeline.

learnings.title: Churn dashboard data is stale until 02:30
learnings.body: The churn_daily materialized view is refreshed by a nightly job that finishes around 02:15 but sometimes runs late when the warehouse is busy. Numbers on the Churn Overview board before about 02:30 can show zeros for the most recent day, which is not a real drop. Check the refresh_log table for a completed entry before raising a question with the growth team.

learnings.title: Node-down alerts inhibit pod alerts on the same node
learnings.body: Alertmanager has an inhibition rule where NodeNotReady suppresses all pod-level alerts whose node label matches the failed node. This keeps a single host failure from producing dozens of pages, but it also means you won't see application errors caused by a pod that moved elsewhere. If the on-call says they're missing alerts, check the inhibition list on the Alertmanager status page first.

learnings.title: Gitleaks false positives in tests/fixtures: scope the allowlist by path, not by regex
learnings.body: The `.gitleaks.toml` at the monorepo root flags fake AWS keys in `tests/fixtures/` on almost every run. Add an allowlist entry with `paths = ['''tests/fixtures/.*''']` and leave the global rules alone. Do not add a broad `password` or `secret` regex to the allowlist, because that disables detection for the whole repo and AppSec will reject the PR.

learnings.title: Vault DB credential leases expire after 45 minutes; apps must reconnect, not just renew
learnings.body: Dynamic Postgres creds issued by vaultctl have a 45m TTL, and renewing the lease does not refresh the password. Services that cache the connection string will start failing auth around the 40-minute mark. Use `vaultctl lease watch --path db/orders-ro` in the sidecar, which triggers a pool drain when the lease is within 5 minutes of expiry.

learnings.title: Rolling out the storefront CSP: run report-only for 14 days before enforcing
learnings.body: Ship the new policy as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` first, pointed at `csp-sink.internal/storefront`. Review the top 20 violation sources in the Grafana panel 'CSP Violations by Directive' each Monday. Only flip to enforcing after the panel has shown zero new unique blocked hosts for 7 consecutive days.

learnings.title: Image fetcher SSRF: outbound requests must go through egress-proxy, direct sockets are blocked
learnings.body: The thumbnail service runs in a network namespace with no default route, so `requests.get` to internal IPs fails silently with a connect timeout. Any new host has to be added to `egress/allowlist.yaml` in the platform-infra repo and go through the egress-proxy at `egress-proxy.corp:3128`. Do not work around this by resolving hostnames in-app, because the proxy re-resolves and checks against private ranges.

learnings.title: Gradle lockfiles: Renovate does not bump transitive deps unless the parent is in a constraints block
learnings.body: Our Renovate config only watches direct dependencies declared in `build.gradle.kts`, so a CVE in a transitive jar like `jackson-databind` will sit unpatched. Pin it with a `constraints { implementation('com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind:2.15.3') }` block. Then run `./gradlew dependencies --write-locks` and commit the lockfile diff, or the security scanner will still report it.

learnings.title: Export download path traversal: resolve the path and check it against the export root
learnings.body: The report export endpoint joined user-supplied `file` params onto `/srv/exports` without normalising, and `../` sequences escaped the directory in pen test FX-2291. The fix pattern is `target = (EXPORT_ROOT / name).resolve()` followed by `target.is_relative_to(EXPORT_ROOT.resolve())`, rejecting the request otherwise. Symlinks inside the export root are also followed by resolve(), which is intentional for our archive mounts.

learnings.title: Login throttling keys on X-Forwarded-For, which clients can spoof behind our old load balancer
learnings.body: Until the LB migration finishes, the rate limiter in `authgate` trusts the left-most X-Forwarded-For value, so attackers can rotate it to bypass the 10 attempts per 15 minutes limit. Use the `X-Real-Client-IP` header that the new edge sets instead, and only after `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` includes the edge subnet. Confirm in staging with `curl -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4'` that the bucket key does not change.

learnings.title: Pen test FX-2291 summary: reflected XSS in support chat widget via the title query parameter
learnings.body: The support chat widget echoed `?title=` into the page header without encoding, which the tester used for session theft against logged-in agents. The fix shipped in widget v3.4.1 and uses the `escapeHtml` helper from `ui-kit`, not a custom regex. Retest is scheduled for the vendor's next quarterly engagement, and the finding stays open until that retest passes.

learnings.title: Password hashing for new accounts: argon2id with m=64MiB, t=3, p=1; migrate legacy bcrypt on login
learnings.body: All new credential writes use argon2id through the `credhash` library with memory cost 65536 KiB, time cost 3, and parallelism 1. Legacy bcrypt hashes are rehashed on successful login, which is handled in `credhash.verify_and_upgrade()`. Do not call `argon2.hash` directly from service code, because it skips the pepper lookup from Vault.

learnings.title: CSRF tokens must be rotated at login, not only at session creation
learnings.body: We found that the admin console kept the anonymous CSRF token after login, so a token planted before authentication remained valid. The middleware now calls `rotate_csrf_token(request)` inside the login view after `session.cycle_key()`. Add a test that asserts the token value differs between the anonymous GET and the POST response.

learnings.title: Distroless base images: pin by digest in prod manifests, tags only in dev
learnings.body: The `base-images` pipeline publishes `distroless/python3:stable` every Tuesday, and the tag moves without warning. Prod Helm values must reference `@sha256:` digests, which `imgpin` writes into `values-prod.yaml` during release. The admission controller `image-policy` rejects any tag-only reference in the `prod-*` namespaces.

learnings.title: S3 policy-lint rejects s3:* and Resource: '*' in service roles; use the prefix-scoped templates
learnings.body: The `policy-lint` check in the infra pipeline fails any IAM document that grants `s3:*` or uses a wildcard resource. Start from the `s3-prefix-readwrite` module and pass your bucket and prefix as inputs. If you genuinely need a broader grant, open a request in the SEC queue with the access pattern, since exceptions expire after 30 days.

learnings.title: Session cookies in embedded iframes: Safari drops SameSite=Lax, so use None with Secure
learnings.body: The partner embed widget broke on Safari 17 because the session cookie was set as SameSite=Lax and the browser refused to send it in a cross-site iframe. Set `SameSite=None; Secure` only on the `/embed/*` routes via the `embed_session` cookie config, and keep Lax for everything else. Verify with Safari's Develop menu, Storage tab, since the console does not show blocked cookies.

learnings.title: Upload scanner quarantine: user files sit in the quarantine bucket for 24h before release
learnings.body: Every file uploaded through the attachments API lands in `quar-uploads-prod` and is scanned by the `clamd-pool` service before it is copied to the serving bucket. The scan job adds a `scan-status` object tag, and the release job only copies files tagged `clean`. If a customer reports a missing file older than 24 hours, check the tag before escalating, because `infected` files are never released and the customer gets a generic message.

learnings.title: pre-commit security hook takes 40 seconds on the monorepo; run it on changed files only
learnings.body: The `precommit-sec` hook runs the full secret and dependency scan, which makes commits on the monorepo feel stuck. Set `SEC_HOOK_SCOPE=changed` in your shell profile to scan only staged files, and the full scan still runs in CI. Do not disable the hook with `--no-verify`, because the CI gate rechecks and your branch will be blocked anyway.

learnings.title: Incident 2024-03: staging API key found in a public gist; rotation checklist
learnings.body: A developer pasted a staging key into a public gist while debugging a webhook consumer, and the key was active for about 6 hours. Revoke it with `keyctl revoke --env staging --key-id`, then search the access logs for that key id across all regions. Post the timeline in the SEC-incident channel and file a follow-up for why the paste service was not blocked by the egress DLP rule.

learnings.title: Never unpickle queue payloads from partner integrations; use the msgpack envelope
learnings.body: Partner integrations publish to the `partner-ingest` queue, and the consumer must treat the body as untrusted. The legacy consumer used `pickle.loads` and was flagged in the last audit, so the new `ingest-core` library only accepts msgpack with a schema from `partner-schemas`. If a partner needs a new type, add it to the schema repo rather than adding a pickle fallback.

learnings.title: Dependency vulnerability SLAs: critical 72 hours, high 14 days, tracked in riskboard
learnings.body: Riskboard auto-creates a ticket for every CVE with CVSS 7.0 or higher found by `depwatch` in a production image. Critical findings need a fix or a documented mitigation within 72 hours, and high findings within 14 days. Tickets that age past SLA show as red on the team scorecard and are escalated to the engineering manager automatically.

learnings.title: Audit sink drops fields matching *ssn* and *card_pan*, but not free-text notes
learnings.body: The `audit-sink` service redacts any JSON key that matches `*ssn*` or `*card_pan*` before writing to the warehouse. Free-text fields such as `notes` or `comment` are not scanned, so do not put customer identifiers there when logging support actions. The data team's nightly query `audit_pii_scan` will flag any row where the regex for SSN-format numbers hits, and the owner gets a ticket.

learnings.title: Staging returns full stack traces when the DEBUG profile is set; check the deploy config first
learnings.body: The `profile` value in staging Helm charts was switched to `debug` during a load test and never reverted, so error responses included stack traces and internal hostnames. Prod is protected by a guard in the chart that refuses `debug` when `env=prod`, but staging is not. Add `profile: standard` to the staging values file and confirm with `curl -s https://staging-api.corp/does-not-exist | grep -c Traceback` returning 0.

learnings.title: HSTS preload is on for the www domain but not api; the edge config needs includeSubDomains first
learnings.body: The `edge-config` repo sets `Strict-Transport-Security` with max-age 31536000 on the www domain, but the api subdomain still serves a shorter max-age without includeSubDomains. Preload submission requires includeSubDomains and max-age of at least one year, so fix the api block before requesting inclusion in the browser list. Check the current state with `securityheaders-cli scan api.corp` before filing the change.

learnings.title: Threat model template lives in the appsec wiki; required sections for any new external endpoint
learnings.body: Every new externally reachable endpoint needs a threat model using the `tm-template-v2` page, and the reviewer will not approve the design doc without it. The template requires sections for trust boundaries, authentication method, data classification, and abuse cases with at least three entries. Start by copying the page into your team space and link the SEC ticket in the first line.

learnings.title: Tabletop exercise: credential compromise scenario runs quarterly, owner is the on-call security lead
learnings.body: The quarterly tabletop for credential compromise walks through a leaked service account token in a CI log. The on-call security lead owns the scenario script in the `tabletops` folder and rotates the facilitator each quarter. Results go into the incident runbook within two business days, and any gap in the rotation steps becomes a SEC ticket.

learnings.title: Login redirect param: only relative paths on the allowlist are honoured
learnings.body: The `next` parameter on `/login` used to accept any URL, which allowed open redirects in phishing tests. The current check in `redirect_guard.py` accepts only paths that start with a single slash and match the allowlist in `ALLOWED_RETURN_PREFIXES`. Protocol-relative values such as `//evil.example` are rejected explicitly, so do not loosen the check to a startswith on the domain.

learnings.title: Profile update endpoint: role and plan are explicitly denied fields, not just omitted from the schema
learnings.body: A mass assignment bug let customers send `role: admin` in the profile PATCH body, and the ORM happily wrote it. The fix added `DENIED_FIELDS = {'role', 'plan', 'is_staff'}` in `profile_serializer.py`, and the serializer raises a 400 before the model is touched. Any new privileged column must be added to this set in the same PR that adds the column.

learnings.title: Analytics dashboards on the warehouse: row-level security is per workspace, not per user group
learnings.body: The BI tool connects to the warehouse using the `bi_reader` role, and row-level policies are attached to workspaces rather than to individual analyst groups. An analyst who is added to a workspace sees all rows that policy allows, including customer emails in the `contacts_raw` table. Ask the data governance channel for a masked view such as `contacts_masked` before sharing any dashboard externally.

learnings.title: Halyard SAML ACS URL needs a trailing slash for staging tenants
learnings.body: Staging tenants on Halyard reject SAML responses when the ACS URL is registered without a trailing slash, returning a generic 'invalid audience' error. Production tenants accept both forms. When you copy the ACS config from prod to staging, add the slash manually and re-run the metadata import in the Halyard admin console under Apps > SAML > Metadata.

learnings.title: AccessDesk auto-approves read-only warehouse roles only within the same cost center
learnings.body: The auto-approve rule for the WH_READONLY role applies only when the requester and their manager share a cost center code. Cross-cost-center requests always route to the data owner, which adds about one business day. If you need faster turnaround, put the justification in the 'Business reason' field and reference the approved project ID, since the rule engine matches on that string.

learnings.title: SCIM deprovisioning can take up to 40 minutes to reach downstream apps
learnings.body: When someone is removed from the HR system, the SCIM sync job runs every 20 minutes and downstream apps poll the IdP on their own schedule, so the total lag can reach 40 minutes. Do not tell offboarding managers that access is cut instantly. For urgent cases, use sigil-cli sessions revoke --user <email> --all, which kills active sessions immediately even though group membership updates lag.

learnings.title: Contractor accounts expire at 90 days unless the sponsor re-attests
learnings.body: Contractor identities created through AccessDesk have a hard expiry of 90 days from creation. The sponsor receives a re-attestation email at day 75 and day 85, and a missed re-attestation disables the account without warning at day 90. Re-attesting in AccessDesk under My Sponsorships resets the clock to 90 days and does not require a new background check.

learnings.title: ROLEMAP group keys are case-sensitive and silently drop mismatches
learnings.body: The ROLEMAP config maps IdP group names to internal roles, and the match is case-sensitive. An IdP group called 'Finance-Analysts' will not map to a rule written as 'finance-analysts', and the login succeeds with zero roles instead of failing. Check the rolemap.yaml diff for case before merging, and use the rolemap-lint check in CI, which flags mismatches against the live IdP group list.

learnings.title: Break-glass accounts: vault-issued password, two approvers, four-hour window
learnings.body: Break-glass access is only issued after two people from the on-call security rotation approve the request in the vault approval queue. The issued password works for four hours and then rotates automatically, so anything you need to do must fit in that window. Log the incident ID in the break-glass register before you start, because the audit job flags any break-glass login without a matching register entry the next morning.

learnings.title: Requiring re-auth on admin apps breaks sigil-cli device flow
learnings.body: Turning on 'Require re-authentication every 8 hours' for the admin app group also applies to the device authorization flow that sigil-cli uses. Scripts that run longer than the window fail mid-run with a 401 that looks like a permissions problem. Scope the re-auth policy to the browser-based admin app only, or have automation use a service identity instead of a human's device session.

learnings.title: Force a session refresh after a role change, because the old roles stick
learnings.body: After someone's role changes, the active session keeps the old role set until it expires, which is up to 12 hours by default. Users often report that they still see the previous permissions and assume the change failed. Run sigil-cli sessions revoke --user <email> --app lumen-admin to pick up the new roles right away, and ask the user to sign in again.

learnings.title: Production DB read access requires a ticket in the INC-#### format
learnings.body: The access request form for prod-replica-readonly rejects any ticket reference that does not match INC- followed by four digits. Jira keys like OPS-1234 or SEC-88 get bounced with a validation error that does not say why. Create or link an INC ticket first, then paste its key into the 'Ticket' field exactly as shown in the header.

learnings.title: Service accounts cannot use SSO, so request them through the svc-credential form
learnings.body: Non-human accounts must be created through the svc-credential form in AccessDesk, not through the normal SSO request flow. Each credential rotates every 30 days, and the rotation job posts the new secret into the owning team's vault path. If a service account is needed for a scheduled job, name it svc-<team>-<purpose> or the naming linter will block the request.

learnings.title: iOS sign-in redirect fails when the custom URL scheme contains uppercase letters
learnings.body: The mobile app's SSO redirect uses a custom URL scheme, and iOS 17 builds fail to return to the app if the scheme contains uppercase letters, such as HalyardAuth. The browser sheet closes and the user lands on a blank screen with no error. Use the all-lowercase scheme halyardauth in the Info.plist and in the Halyard client registration, both of which must match exactly.

learnings.title: Nested IdP groups do not flatten into AccessDesk entitlements
learnings.body: AccessDesk only reads direct group membership when evaluating an entitlement, so a user who is a member of a subgroup inside finance-all does not automatically get finance-all's roles. This is a common cause of 'I should have access but I do not' tickets. Either add the user directly to the group that carries the entitlement, or ask identity-eng to add the parent group to the ROLEMAP entry.

learnings.title: Approval SLAs: security-owned apps take two business days, others escalate at 24h
learnings.body: Requests for apps tagged security-owned go to the security review queue and have a two business day SLA. Everything else goes to the app owner, and if they do not act within 24 hours, AccessDesk escalates to their director automatically. The escalation shows up in the request timeline as 'auto-escalated', so you can tell requesters why it took longer than expected.

learnings.title: Login loops in the embedded admin console when third-party cookies are blocked
learnings.body: The admin console is embedded in an iframe on the internal portal, and the SSO handshake depends on third-party cookies being allowed for the Halyard domain. With cookies blocked, the page cycles between the login screen and the console with no error. Ask the user to open the console in a top-level tab, or add halyard.internal to the browser's cookie allowlist, which is the fix that works in every case we have seen.

learnings.title: sigil-cli device login fails behind the proxy unless NO_PROXY includes the IdP host
learnings.body: Running sigil-cli login --device from a laptop on the corporate VPN hangs at 'waiting for authorization' when the proxy intercepts idp.halyard.internal. Add idp.halyard.internal and sigil.internal to the NO_PROXY variable in your shell profile. Verify with curl -I https://idp.halyard.internal/.well-known/openid-configuration, which should return 200 without going through the proxy.

learnings.title: Revoking a laptop certificate does not end the SSO session
learnings.body: When a device is reported lost, revoking its client certificate in the MDM blocks new device-bound logins but leaves the existing browser session valid. The attacker can keep working until the session expires. Use the kill switch in the security console, which revokes all sessions for the user and forces re-enrollment, and only then revoke the certificate.
