learnings.title: Access expiry reminders go only to the manager, not the requester
learnings.body: AccessDesk sends the 14-day expiry reminder to the approving manager only, so the person who actually needs the access often never sees it. When access lapses, the requester gets a generic 'access denied' page with no link to renew. Tell requesters to set a calendar reminder for the expiry date shown on their request, or to ask their manager to forward the reminder.

learnings.title: Bulk access CSV: 200 rows max, header must be exactly email,app,role
learnings.body: The bulk import in AccessDesk rejects files with more than 200 rows and fails silently on headers that differ in case or spacing. The only accepted header is email,app,role with no spaces. Split larger lists into batches and run a dry run first with --validate-only, which prints the rows that would be rejected and why.

learnings.title: Dormant accounts are disabled after 60 days without login
learnings.body: A nightly job at 02:15 UTC disables any account that has not signed in to Halyard for 60 days. The account is not deleted, and re-enabling it takes about 10 minutes through the helpdesk form. People returning from parental leave or long sabbaticals hit this often, so ask managers to flag planned absences in the HR system so the job skips them.

learnings.title: Billing admin console access requires finance-approver group membership
learnings.body: The billing admin console checks for membership in finance-approver at login time, not only at entitlement grant time. Someone who was added to the group but has not signed in since will see an empty console until their next session starts. Add the user to finance-approver and have them sign out fully, not just close the tab, before they test.

learnings.title: Personal email domains are blocked for SSO by default
learnings.body: Accounts with an email domain outside the approved domain allowlist cannot complete SSO sign-in, even when they have an approved access request. Contractors who were given personal addresses will see 'domain not permitted' at the IdP. Request a domain exception through the identity-eng queue, which requires a named sponsor and an end date no more than 90 days out.

learnings.title: Role names longer than 32 characters are truncated in SAML assertions
learnings.body: Halyard truncates role names to 32 characters when building the SAML attribute statement, and the truncation is silent. A role named ANALYTICS_WAREHOUSE_PII_READONLY_EU arrives at the app as ANALYTICS_WAREHOUSE_PII_READONL, which matches nothing. Keep role names at 32 characters or fewer, and check the length in rolemap-lint before adding a new role.

learnings.title: CI runners must use workload identity, not a developer's SSO token
learnings.body: Pipelines that deploy to production were using personal SSO tokens copied into CI variables, which broke every time the developer changed roles. Use the ci-runner-prod workload identity instead, which is bound to the repository and branch in the runner config. Any pipeline still referencing SSO_TOKEN will fail the security gate with a clear message after the next policy update.

learnings.title: Quarterly access review: 10 business days, export from lumen-admin
learnings.body: Each quarter, lumen-admin generates the access review export on the first business day, and reviewers have 10 business days to certify or revoke each entitlement. Reviewers who miss the deadline have their entitlements suspended automatically, which generates a surge of tickets in the second week. Send the export to reviewers yourself on day one, because the built-in email goes to a shared mailbox that often gets missed.

learnings.title: orders_fact late-arriving rows: use the 72h backfill window, not a full rebuild
learnings.body: Source systems in the orders feed can deliver rows up to three days late, so the nightly job only reprocesses the last 1 day by default. If you see counts drifting for a past date, run `keel backfill --table orders_fact --window 3d --dry-run` first and check the diff. A full rebuild takes about 6 hours and locks the BI cache, so avoid it unless the dry run shows more than 3 days of drift.

learnings.title: Q: why does my dbt incremental model have duplicate keys?
learnings.body: Q: My incremental model in tessera/models/marts shows duplicates after a rerun. A: The unique_key was set to order_id alone, but the upstream table is keyed on (order_id, line_no). Change it to a list in the model config, `unique_key=['order_id','line_no']`, then run `tessera run -s fct_order_lines --full-refresh` once to clean the table.

learnings.title: Dedupe on event_id keeps earliest ingested_at, not earliest event_time
learnings.body: The staging dedupe in stg_events uses `qualify row_number() over (partition by event_id order by ingested_at)`. That means a re-sent event from a retry wins over the original if the retry was ingested first, which is rare but happens. If you need the original event timestamp, join back to raw.events_archive on event_id and use the min event_time there.

learnings.title: Dashboard warehouse: keep XS, auto-suspend 300s, never LARGE for BI service account
learnings.body: The BI service account is pinned to the WH_BI_XS warehouse with auto-suspend at 300 seconds. Someone bumped it to LARGE during a Q3 incident and the monthly bill jumped about 40 percent in a week. If a dashboard is slow, add a summary table instead of resizing; ask in #wh-costs before changing sizes.

learnings.title: Deploy checklist for warehouse migrations (prod)
learnings.body:
1. Run `make wh-migrate ENV=stage` and confirm the migration log shows no DROP statements on tables tagged `pii`.
2. Create a zero-copy clone: `CREATE TABLE ... CLONE` on any table being altered, retention 1 day.
3. Open a deploy PR with the label `wh-prod-approved`; the pipeline will refuse to run `make wh-migrate ENV=prod` without it.
4. After deploy, run `recon-check --suite core` and post the output in the deploy thread.

learnings.title: SCD2 joins on dim_customer need strict less-than on valid_to
learnings.body: dim_customer uses '9999-12-31' as the open valid_to, and the valid_to of a closed row equals the valid_from of the next version. Joining with `valid_to >= event_ts` double-counts events that land exactly on a change boundary. Use `event_ts >= valid_from and event_ts < valid_to` in every join, the helper macro `scd_join()` does this for you.

learnings.title: Fiscal weeks start Monday; dim_date.week_start_mon is the one to use
learnings.body: dim_date has two week columns: `iso_week` (ISO, Monday start) and `fiscal_week` (Sunday start, used by Finance for the board pack). Several dashboards silently used iso_week when they should have used fiscal_week, which shifted totals by one day around year-end. Metrics in the `finance_` namespace must reference `fiscal_week` and `week_start_sun`.

learnings.title: Ingest schema drift: raw.events evolves, curated models do not
learnings.body: Keel is set to `schema_policy=evolve` on the raw.events landing zone, so new fields appear automatically in the VARIANT column. Curated models only pick up fields listed in `sources.yml`, so a new field will not show up in dashboards until someone adds it. Run `keel schema diff --source events --since 7d` each Monday to see what is new.

learnings.title: Warehouse timezone rule: store UTC, derive local in one place
learnings.body: All timestamp columns in the warehouse are TIMESTAMP_NTZ in UTC, and the column names end in `_utc`. Local times are only computed in `dim_tz_local`, which maps account_id to an IANA zone. Do not call CONVERT_TIMEZONE in ad hoc SQL; two analysts got different daily totals last quarter because one used the account zone and one used the warehouse session zone.

learnings.title: Row count reconciliation threshold is 0.5 percent against source
learnings.body: The `recon-check` job compares daily row counts for the core tables against the source databases. A difference under 0.5 percent is logged as a warning and does not page anyone. Anything above that opens a PagerDuty incident for data-platform, so check the source job logs before rerunning the load.

learnings.title: Null vs empty string in session referrer: pipeline coerces to NULL
learnings.body: Since the March refactor, stg_sessions turns empty-string referrers into NULL, so `where referrer = ''` returns nothing. Use `where referrer is null` for direct traffic. The old dashboards still count '' as direct, which is why direct traffic appeared to drop about 8 percent in April.

learnings.title: Join fan-out trap: sessions joined to events multiplies revenue
learnings.body: Joining fct_sessions to fct_events and then summing order_value counts each order once per event in the session. Pre-aggregate the events to one row per session_id in `int_session_events_agg` before joining. The fan-out check in the CI lint will flag joins where the row count grows more than 1.1x.

learnings.title: Metric definitions live in the metrics repo; do not redefine active_user in dashboards
learnings.body: The canonical active_user metric is defined in `metrics/active_user.yml` as users with at least one qualifying event in a rolling 28-day window. Several dashboards had their own definition using 30 days, which made the executive numbers disagree with the product numbers. If you need a new variant, add a new metric name with a suffix and get sign-off in #metrics-council.

learnings.title: Nightly DAG wh_nightly waits for source dumps; do not trigger it manually before 02:15 UTC
learnings.body: The wh_nightly DAG starts at 02:15 UTC and has a sensor on the `_SUCCESS` marker from each source dump. Triggering it by hand before the markers exist produces partial loads that look complete, because the sensor only checks for the marker's presence from the previous run. If you must rerun, use `airflowctl dags backfill wh_nightly --start <date>` which clears the sensor state.

learnings.title: VARIANT keys are case-sensitive; payload:userId is not payload:userid
learnings.body: Fields in raw.events.payload are stored with the casing the producer used, and the producer changed from userid to userId in January. Queries written against the old casing return NULL for events after that date without any error. Use the helper `coalesce(payload:userId, payload:userid)` until the backfill finishes in Q3.

learnings.title: Partition pruning fails when you filter on a cast of event_ts
learnings.body: raw.events is clustered on event_date, a DATE column, not on event_ts. Writing `where to_date(event_ts) = '2024-05-01'` scans the full table because the function wraps the cluster key. Filter on `event_date = '2024-05-01'` directly; a 30-day query dropped from 11 minutes to 40 seconds after this change.

learnings.title: Materialized summary agg_daily_sessions is the default for dashboards over 90 days
learnings.body: Dashboards that look back more than 90 days should read from `agg_daily_sessions` rather than the raw sessions table. The summary is rebuilt at 04:00 UTC and is grouped by date, country, channel, and device class. If you need a dimension that is not in the summary, open a request in #wh-requests and do not join the raw table into a dashboard.

learnings.title: Statement timeout for BI is 900 seconds; longer queries get killed silently
learnings.body: The BI role has STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS set to 900, and the dashboard tool shows a generic 'query failed' message when it hits the limit. Several people assumed a bug in the tool. For long jobs, run them as a scheduled task in tessera with the `long_running` tag, which allows 3600 seconds.

learnings.title: Access requests: analysts get ANALYST_RO through the okta group, not direct grants
learnings.body: New analysts are added to the okta group `wh-analyst-ro`, which syncs to the ANALYST_RO role every hour. Do not run GRANT statements by hand because the sync will remove them and the audit log will show a mismatch. Contractors use `wh-contractor-ro`, which excludes any table tagged `pii` and the finance schema.

learnings.title: PII masking policy on email columns applies to all non-admin roles
learnings.body: The masking policy `mask_email` is attached to every column tagged `pii_email` in the core schemas, and it returns the domain only for analysts. If you need an unmasked export for a support investigation, file a ticket in the SEC queue with the customer account id and the business reason. Exports are logged and reviewed monthly.

learnings.title: Zero-copy clones for testing expire after one day; re-clone before each test run
learnings.body: The `CLONE` statements in our test harness use a retention of 1 day, so a clone created last Thursday will be missing data changes from the weekend. The test script `scripts/clone_for_test.sh` always recreates the clone from the current prod snapshot. Do not point tests at a clone you created more than 24 hours ago.

learnings.title: Weekly compaction runs Sunday 03:00 UTC and locks raw.events for about 20 minutes
learnings.body: The compaction job merges small files in raw.events every Sunday starting at 03:00 UTC. Writes queue during the lock and are replayed, so the ingestion lag will look like 15 to 25 minutes on Monday morning. Do not interpret that as an outage; check `keel status --lag` before opening an incident.

learnings.title: Unknown dimension member is id -1; always LEFT JOIN and coalesce to 'Unknown'
learnings.body: Every dimension table has a row with surrogate key -1 labeled 'Unknown' for facts that fail the lookup. Inner joins on dimensions silently drop these facts, which hid about 2 percent of signups in one report. Use LEFT JOIN and coalesce the label, and the `dim_unknown_check` test will fail if the Unknown share exceeds 1 percent.

learnings.title: Sampling for exploration: use SAMPLE (1), not LIMIT, on large tables
learnings.body: LIMIT 1000 on raw.events still reads from the beginning of the cluster and returns a skewed sample toward the oldest partition. Use `select * from raw.events sample (1) where event_date between ...` to get a random one percent sample across the range. Results are not exact, so do not use sampled numbers in anything shared with finance.

learnings.title: Looker-style BI explores break on column renames; run meridian lint first
learnings.body: The BI layer (Meridian) binds explores to physical column names, so a rename in dbt breaks dashboards without any warning in dbt tests. Before merging a rename, run `meridian lint --changed` in the models repo, which lists every explore that references the old name. Add the old name as a `meta.aliases` entry for at least two weeks.

learnings.title: Currency conversion tables are dated; join on rate_date, not on the transaction date
learnings.body: fx_rates_daily stores the end-of-day rate for each date, and transactions made after the close use the next day's rate in finance reporting. If you join on the transaction date directly, the numbers will not match the finance close. Use the macro `fx_at_close(txn_date)` which applies the rule centrally.

learnings.title: Snapshots of stage exports: name paths by run date, not by export time
learnings.body: Exports written to the stage path `@exports/core/` must use the pattern `run_date=YYYY-MM-DD/` so downstream loaders can find them. Writing with the wall-clock time in the path caused two loaders to skip files when a rerun happened on the same day. The loader `load_export` expects exactly one directory per run date.

learnings.title: Cost attribution: set QUERY_TAG on every scheduled job or the spend shows as unattributed
learnings.body: The monthly cost report groups spend by QUERY_TAG, and anything without a tag lands in the unattributed bucket, which was 31 percent of spend in February. Set the tag at the top of each job with `ALTER SESSION SET QUERY_TAG = 'team:<name>;job:<name>'`. The tessera runner does this automatically if the job has an owner field in its YAML.

learnings.title: Idempotent backfill rule: rerunning a load must not change row counts
learnings.body: All loaders in keel are required to pass the idempotency test, which runs the load twice against a clone and compares counts and checksums. If a new loader fails that test, it cannot be merged. The usual cause is an append without a merge key, so use the `merge_on` option in the loader config.

learnings.title: Incremental fct_sessions lookback set to 3 days for late mobile pings
learnings.body: The mobile SDK v4.x batches pings and can deliver events up to 72 hours late, so fct_sessions uses a 3-day lookback in its incremental filter. We measured this against the ingest_lag_audit table in March and nothing arrived later than 71 hours. Don't drop it to 1 day or late sessions will silently stay wrong.

learnings.title: Deploy: nightly prod dbt build is triggered by `make ship-dbt`
learnings.body: To ship model changes to prod, run `make ship-dbt ENV=prod` from the analytics-core repo, which wraps `dbt build --select state:modified+ --defer --state prod_artifacts/`. Do not run plain `dbt run` against prod by hand, because it skips tests on downstream models. The target is the same as the 03:15 UTC nightly job.

learnings.title: Source freshness on raw_orders warns at 6h and errors at 12h
learnings.body: The freshness block in sources/raw_orders.yml uses loaded_at_field _fivetran_synced with warn_after count 6 and error_after count 12, period hour. Fivetran's connector for the orders DB syncs every 4 hours, so a 6h warning is normal on weekends when the connector is paused for maintenance. If you see an error, check the Fivetran dashboard before paging anyone.

learnings.title: Q: why does relationships test fail on fct_sessions.user_id?
learnings.body: Q: relationships test from fct_sessions.user_id to dim_users fails with about 9% orphans. A: anonymous sessions have null user_id and the test treats null as a failure. Add where: 'user_id is not null' to the test config, which is what we use in the warehouse_tests package.

learnings.title: Staging model naming: stg_<source>__<entity> with double underscore
learnings.body: House rule: staging models are named stg_<source>__<entity>, with two underscores between source and entity, e.g. stg_stripe_billing__invoices. The sqlfluff custom rule RB02 in the CI linter enforces this and will fail the PR. Single underscore names got us a broken lineage view in Lighthouse last year.

learnings.title: Lighthouse lineage graph goes stale until manifest is re-synced
learnings.body: Lighthouse, our internal lineage viewer, reads a cached copy of target/manifest.json and does not auto-refresh after a merge. After a deploy run `lh sync --manifest target/manifest.json --project analytics-core` to push the new graph. If new models are missing from the graph, this is almost always the reason.

learnings.title: Snapshot on subscriptions uses check strategy, not timestamp
learnings.body: The snap_subscriptions snapshot uses strategy: check with check_cols [status, plan_tier], because the source table has no reliable updated_at column. The run takes about 11 minutes over roughly 4.2M rows. If you change check_cols, you must run with --full-refresh only after asking billing-data, since history will reset.

learnings.title: Warehouse sizing: only int_event_sessionize runs on XL
learnings.body: Marts run on TRANSFORM_M by default, set via +snowflake_warehouse in dbt_project.yml. The only model on TRANSFORM_XL is int_event_sessionize, which peaks around 40 minutes at M and about 14 at XL. Please don't add other models to XL without checking the warehouse credit dashboard first.

learnings.title: fct_ledger_daily full refresh needs the confirm_refresh var
learnings.body: fct_ledger_daily is protected by a macro guard that aborts --full-refresh unless you pass the var explicitly. Run `dbt run --select fct_ledger_daily --full-refresh --vars 'confirm_refresh: true'`. The guard exists because a full refresh in 2023 wiped four months of restated history.

learnings.title: Seeds: cast sku codes to varchar or leading zeros disappear
learnings.body: When dbt loads ref_skus.csv as a seed, codes like 0042117 are inferred as integers and become 42117. Set column_types: {sku: varchar} under the seed's config block in seeds/schema.yml. We found this after the warehouse reconciliation showed 312 missing SKUs.

learnings.title: Unit tests with more than 50 fixture rows: switch to CSV format
learnings.body: Unit test fixtures written as inline dicts get slow past about 50 rows and the dbt parser becomes the bottleneck. Move them to tests/unit/fixtures/*.csv and reference them with format: csv in the test definition. Run only unit tests with `dbt test --select test_type:unit` during local development.

learnings.title: Warden stores dbt prod credentials, profiles.yml reads them at runtime
learnings.body: The dbt prod profile does not contain a password. It calls `warden get dbt-svc-prod` through the password field, and you need the analytics-core role in Warden to fetch it. Locally you can use the dev profile with your own SSO token instead.

learnings.title: Model contracts on dim_customers caught a dropped column
learnings.body: We turned on contract: enforced: true for dim_customers in February. The first week it blocked a PR that dropped account_region, which the Looker explore customer_360 depends on. Turn contracts on for any mart that has an exposure, since the build fails before the BI layer breaks.

learnings.title: Schema override macro needed for package sources to resolve
learnings.body: When a dbt package calls source() the default generate_schema_name can point at the wrong schema for our staging layer. We override it in macros/schema.sql so custom schemas get appended to target.schema only in the dev target. If sources in the vendored package return zero rows, check that override first.

learnings.title: Accepted_values on plan_tier missed enterprise_trial
learnings.body: The accepted_values test on dim_accounts.plan_tier started failing in March because the product team added enterprise_trial without telling us. The fix was to add the value to ref_plan_tiers seed and have the test reference that seed via relationships. Ping #product-data before any new tier ships so the seed gets updated first.

learnings.title: Ephemeral models cannot carry tests, so test their parents
learnings.body: Do not attach data tests to ephemeral models because dbt compiles them inline and the test has nothing to query. Instead put the test on the nearest materialized parent or on the first downstream table. This came up repeatedly in the int_ layer review and is now a comment in the PR template.

learnings.title: Metabase syncs lag a full build, schedule the refresh after dbt
learnings.body: Metabase caches table metadata and will show old column types until its sync runs, which we set to 04:30 UTC after the nightly dbt build. If an analyst reports a missing column right after a deploy, click Sync now on the database in Metabase admin before debugging the model. Forcing a manual sync usually fixes it in under a minute.

learnings.title: Rollback a bad mart: git revert, then defer-build the prior state
learnings.body: To roll back fct_orders after a bad deploy, git revert the offending merge commit and then run `dbt run --select fct_orders+ --defer --state prod_artifacts/`, pointing state at the last good artifact bundle. The artifact bundles are kept for 14 days in the s3 bucket dbt-artifacts-prod. Announce the rollback in #data-incidents so downstream owners know.

learnings.title: dbt-guard pre-commit hook rejects models without meta.owner
learnings.body: Our dbt-guard hook fails any model in models/marts/ whose YAML lacks a meta.owner key. Add meta: {owner: your-team-slug} under the model's config, using a slug from the team registry. The hook runs on commit and also in CI, so skipping it locally just moves the failure to the PR.

learnings.title: Exposures for dashboards must be declared or dbt docs show orphans
learnings.body: Every Looker dashboard fed by a mart should have an exposure file in models/exposures/. Without it the docs site at docs.internal.example shows the mart as unused and people delete it. The publish job runs at 02:00 and regenerates the exposure graph.

learnings.title: Q: why is dbt build slower after adding dbt_utils.star?
learnings.body: Q: after switching a staging model to dbt_utils.star the build time doubled. A: star expands into the full column list at compile time, which bloats the SQL for wide sources like the 240-column events table. Use an explicit column list for any source over about 60 columns.

learnings.title: Heads up: dbt_utils pinned to 1.1.1, do not bump without re-keying
learnings.body: We pinned dbt_utils to 1.1.1 in packages.yml because 1.2 changed the output of generate_surrogate_key, which would change every surrogate key in dim_ and fct_ tables. If you need to upgrade, plan a full refresh of the affected marts and tell the BI team first. The pin is documented in the packages file itself.

learnings.title: Ops note: the 03:15 UTC nightly job is capped at one run per warehouse
learnings.body: The dbt Cloud job nightly-core has concurrency set to 1 per warehouse, so a manual trigger during the nightly window will queue behind it. If you need an out-of-cycle build before 06:00 UTC, use the hotfix job instead, which runs on a separate warehouse. Queued runs over 45 minutes get auto-cancelled by the scheduler.

learnings.title: Pivot macro output column names are truncated past 63 characters
learnings.body: The pivot macro in our utils package generates column names from category values, and Postgres-backed reporting truncates anything over 63 characters. Long values like enterprise_annual_prepaid_addon silently collide. Shorten the category labels upstream in the seed mapping rather than patching the macro.

learnings.title: Team agreement: marts must not reference other marts directly
learnings.body: Agreed in the Q2 architecture review that marts reference only intermediate and staging models, never other marts. This keeps the fan-out in the lineage graph readable and stops cascading full refreshes. The exception list lives in the ARCHITECTURE.md file at the repo root, and anything not on it needs a sign-off from the analytics lead.

learnings.title: Set catchup=False on every new warehouse DAG
learnings.body: Any DAG added to the warehouse-dags repo must pass catchup=False in its constructor unless someone has approved a backfill in #data-platform. Without it, the first deploy of a daily DAG with a start_date of last spring will queue about 300 runs and swamp the heavy pool. Reviewers in the repo's PR template check this box.

learnings.title: XCom payloads over 48KB fail silently in our setup
learnings.body: Our metadata DB column truncates XCom values beyond 48KB, and the task still shows success, so downstream tasks read partial JSON. Push anything large to object storage with the stashkit helper (stashkit.put(df) returns a URI) and pass only the URI through XCom. The helper is in the common-airflow package v2.3 or later.

learnings.title: Heavy dbt runs must use the warehouse_heavy pool
learnings.body: The warehouse_heavy pool has 4 slots shared across all teams, so dbt build tasks that run without it can starve the finance reconciliations. Set pool='warehouse_heavy' and pool_slots=2 for any dbt selector that touches more than 50 models. Check current usage at the Pools page before adding new heavy jobs.

learnings.title: Scheduler timezone is UTC, but our cron strings are written in Chicago time
learnings.body: Airflow evaluates schedule expressions in UTC in this deployment, which bit us when the 02:00 cron on the finance export ran at 20:00 local. Use pendulum-aware start_date with tz="America/Chicago" when a job has to hit a local business window. Keep the cron comment in the DAG file stating which zone it means.

learnings.title: Interpreting logical_date vs data_interval_start in ad-hoc questions
learnings.body: Q (from Dana, asked in #analytics-eng): why does the run labeled 2024-03-10 process March 9 data? A: logical_date is the start of the data interval, not the time the run happens, so a daily DAG labeled March 10 runs on March 11 and loads March 10 partitions. Use data_interval_start and data_interval_end in templates rather than ds when writing new code.

learnings.title: DAG file import timeout is 30s; slow top-level code breaks parsing
learnings.body: The scheduler's dagbag_import_timeout is 30 seconds, and a DAG file that exceeds it disappears from the UI with no error banner. The usual culprit is an HTTP call to the catalog API at module level. Move that call into a task or wrap it with the module-level cache in dagutils.cached_catalog() so parsing stays under 2 seconds.

learnings.title: Deploy path for DAG changes: merge to main, wait for Brindle sync
learnings.body: Merging to main triggers Brindle CI, which copies the dags/ folder to the gs://ac-airflow-dags bucket, and the scheduler picks it up within about 5 minutes. There is no manual restart step. If you need to hotfix a running DAG, pause it first with `airctl dags pause <dag_id> --reason "hotfix PR-1182"` so an in-flight run does not pick up half-updated code.

learnings.title: Clearing failed tasks without re-running successes
learnings.body: To rerun only the failed tasks in a DAG run, use `airctl tasks clear -d <dag_id> -r <run_id> --only-failed`. Without --only-failed the command clears every task, including successful loads, and those will re-insert rows into the fact tables. Always do a dry run first with --dry-run, which prints the task list without changing state.

learnings.title: Use reschedule mode for ExternalTaskSensor
learnings.body: Sensors in poke mode hold a worker slot for their entire wait, and during the Monday ingest we once had 40 sensors blocking the light queue. Set mode="reschedule" with poke_interval=300 and a timeout of 6 hours on every ExternalTaskSensor. The sensor releases its slot between checks, which the light queue needs during peak hours.

learnings.title: Finance DAGs: max_active_runs must be 1
learnings.body: The finance ledger DAGs assume that day N finishes before day N+1 starts, so max_active_runs=1 is required in their constructor. The CI linter named finance-dag-lint will fail a PR that omits it or sets a higher value. If you need to catch up after an outage, run the backfill in a separate DAG copy with a suffix like _backfill_2024q1.

learnings.title: Cleanup tasks should use trigger_rule all_done
learnings.body: A cleanup task that uses the default all_success trigger rule gets skipped whenever an upstream extract fails, which leaves staging tables behind and fills the scratch bucket. Set trigger_rule="all_done" on drop_staging and delete_tmp_files tasks. Verify in the graph view that the task runs after a forced failure of its upstream in the sandbox environment.

learnings.title: Connections live in Vault, never in the Airflow UI
learnings.body: All Airflow connections are read from Vault at secret/airflow/conn/<conn_id>, and the UI connection editor is read-only for most people. To add a connection, open a ticket to the platform queue with the conn_id and the owning team, and they will write the secret. Creating one through the UI will be overwritten by the next Vault sync within 15 minutes.

learnings.title: Do not call Variable.get at module level
learnings.body: Every Variable.get in top-level DAG code is a metadata DB query each time the scheduler parses the file, which adds up fast with 200 DAGs. Wrap the lookup inside a task callable or use a Jinja template like {{ var.value.load_window_days }}. The scheduler dashboard shows parse time per file; anything over 3 seconds should be reviewed.

learnings.title: Default retries and backoff for lakehouse API operators
learnings.body: The house default is retries=2 with retry_delay=5 minutes and retry_exponential_backoff=True, set in the shared default_args dictionary in common-airflow. Lakehouse API calls that return 503 during the nightly compaction window usually succeed on the second retry. Do not raise retries above 4 without talking to the lakehouse on-call, since it keeps the pool slot occupied.

learnings.title: Backfill command and the reset flag
learnings.body: To backfill a DAG for a date range, run `airctl backfill --dag <dag_id> --start 2024-02-01 --end 2024-02-07 --max-active 2 --reset-dagruns`. The --reset-dagruns flag clears existing runs in that range before queuing new ones, which is required when the source table was corrected. Without it, the backfill silently skips dates that already have a success state.

learnings.title: SLA misses go to #data-alerts, and paused DAGs don't count
learnings.body: SLA miss callbacks post to #data-alerts with the DAG id and the expected completion time. A DAG that is paused will not generate SLA misses, so a silent pause can hide a broken pipeline for days. The weekly pipeline health report counts paused DAGs separately, so check it if a dashboard looks stale.

learnings.title: Pin KubernetesPodOperator images by digest
learnings.body: Tags like :latest and :v2 get re-pushed by the build pipeline, and we had one DAG silently pick up a broken pandas version that way. Reference images as registry.acme.internal/etl/base@sha256:<digest> in the image parameter. The current digests for the shared base images are listed in the etl-base README under 'Pinned images'.

learnings.title: Log retention for task logs is 14 days
learnings.body: Task logs are copied from the workers to the gs://ac-airflow-logs bucket and deleted after 14 days by a lifecycle rule. If you need a failure from three weeks ago, export it before it expires or check the incident doc that usually links to the log path. Use `airctl logs fetch <dag_id> <task_id> <run_id>` to pull them to your laptop without console access.

learnings.title: Zombie tasks after a scheduler restart
learnings.body: When the scheduler restarts during a run, tasks sometimes stay in the running state with no worker attached, and new runs for that DAG will queue behind them. Run `airctl tasks clear -d <dag_id> --state running --only-failed` after confirming in the worker dashboard that no pod is alive for that task. The restart checklist in the on-call runbook lists this as step 4.

learnings.title: Task ids: lowercase snake_case, under 200 characters
learnings.body: Task ids longer than about 200 characters break the lineage ingestion job in Marquez, which then drops the whole DAG from the lineage graph. Stick to lowercase snake_case, and put the table name in the id (load_orders_daily, not step_3). The lint rule task-id-format in the CI config enforces this.

learnings.title: Prefer data_interval templates over the ds macro
learnings.body: The ds macro still works, but our internal template helper expects data_interval_start, and mixing the two in one DAG caused an off-by-one in the June retention job. Use {{ data_interval_start | ds }} for the partition date and {{ data_interval_start | ds_nodash }} for file names. New DAGs using bare {{ ds }} will be flagged by the Airflow lint pass.

learnings.title: Failure email goes to the oncall alias, not per-task emails
learnings.body: Do not set email_on_failure or an email list on individual tasks. Failures route through the shared default_args to the data-oncall-fyi alias, which pages the on-call rotation after two consecutive failures. Per-task emails are duplicated and have caused alert fatigue in the past.

learnings.title: Celery queue split: light vs heavy
learnings.body: Tasks run on the light queue by default, which has 24 workers sized for API calls and small SQL. Anything that loads more than 1 GB into memory or runs a Spark submit goes on the heavy queue via queue="heavy". Using the wrong queue is the most common cause of the nightly scheduler lag we saw in May.

learnings.title: Testing DAGs locally with make dag-test
learnings.body: Run `make dag-test DAG=<dag_id>` inside the warehouse-dags repo to load the DAG into a DagBag and execute it against the sandbox warehouse. The target fails if the DAG has import errors, which catches most parse problems before CI does. Use DATE=2024-01-15 to pin the logical date for reproducible output.

learnings.title: owner field must match a team slug in the directory
learnings.body: The owner argument in default_args must be a team slug from the org directory, such as fin-recon or growth-data, because the on-call routing and cost reports use it to assign the DAG. Individual names are rejected by the DAG validator. If you transferred a DAG to another team, update owner in the same PR that moves the file.

learnings.title: Dynamic task mapping is capped at 128 items
learnings.body: Mapping over a list longer than 128 produces a 'map length exceeded' error at run time, not at parse time, so the failure shows up after the upstream task has already run. Chunk large lists with the chunked() helper in dagutils so each mapped task gets a batch of up to 100 items. The cap is set by max_map_length in our Airflow config and is not overridable per DAG.

learnings.title: Pausing a DAG when the source is late
learnings.body: If an upstream feed is late by more than the SLA window, pause the downstream DAG with a reason so the on-call knows it was deliberate, not a broken scheduler. The command is `airctl dags pause <dag_id> --reason "vendor feed late, ticket OPS-889"`. Unpause it once the feed lands, and then clear the sensor task so the run continues from where it stopped.

learnings.title: Deferrable operators for long warehouse waits
learnings.body: The warehouse load operator supports deferrable=True, which hands the wait off to the triggerer instead of holding a worker. Turn it on for any load that is expected to take more than 20 minutes, such as the full-refresh of the orders history table. The triggerer runs in its own deployment called airflow-triggerer, so check that it is healthy if deferred tasks stay in the deferred state.

learnings.title: Q&A: why does my DAG show two runs for the same day?
learnings.body: Q (Priya, #growth-data): I see two runs with the same logical date, one manual and one scheduled. A: Manual triggers in the UI create a run with a run_id starting with manual__ and the same logical date as the scheduled run if you don't change it. Use the run_id column to tell them apart, and delete the manual one with `airctl runs delete` if it was a mistake.

learnings.title: Backfills need a separate pool or they starve production
learnings.body: A backfill that runs in the default pool will take every slot and push the 6 AM production loads into a queue that can take hours to drain. Launch backfills with --pool backfill_pool, which has 3 slots, and check the pool size before starting a wide date range. The pool is managed by the platform team, so request changes in #platform-requests.

learnings.title: Resuming from checkpoint resets LR warmup in forge-trainer
learnings.body: If you resume a run with --resume-from, forge-trainer 3.x restarts the LR warmup schedule from step 0 instead of continuing from the saved step. This caused a noticeable loss spike in the ranker run on Tuesday. Pass --keep-schedule-state to preserve the scheduler position, which has been the default in forge-trainer 3.4 and later.

learnings.title: Nightly retrain diffs: always pin --seed-mode=fixed
learnings.body: Use --seed-mode=fixed for any retrain you plan to compare against last week's model, otherwise weight diffs are dominated by init noise. Our rule is that the seed for a retrain is derived from the dataset snapshot ID, so reruns on the same snapshot are bit-identical on the same GPU type. Mixed GPU types still differ in the last few decimal places, so note the hardware in the run card.

learnings.title: Stratify holdout splits on customer_tier, not on region
learnings.body: We got burned when the holdout split was stratified on region because enterprise tier was badly underrepresented, and the offline AUC looked great while enterprise lift was flat. The current split helper in splitkit uses stratify_cols=['customer_tier', 'label'] by default. If you need a different stratification, set it explicitly in the experiment YAML rather than relying on the default.

learnings.title: forge-gpu queue preempts jobs tagged priority=low after 6h
learnings.body: Jobs in the shared forge-gpu queue with priority=low are preempted once they've run for six hours if any priority=normal job is waiting. Preempted jobs are restarted from the last checkpoint, but only if you set checkpoint_interval in the job spec. Jobs without checkpointing simply lose all progress, so please don't submit long runs as low priority without it.

learnings.title: Label leakage from joining on updated_at
learnings.body: Joining the orders table to the labels table on updated_at leaked post-outcome information into the training set, inflating validation metrics by roughly 4 AUC points. Use the point-in-time join in featurelake with as_of=label_event_time instead. The old ad-hoc SQL in the notebook templates has been removed from the shared folder.

learnings.title: bf16 mixed precision gave NaN loss until we raised eps
learnings.body: Training the fraud embedding model under bf16 autocast produced NaN losses after about 2k steps when the LayerNorm eps was left at 1e-12. Setting eps to 1e-5 in the model config fixed it, and the final AUC matched the fp32 baseline within noise. Keep loss scaling enabled even under bf16 unless you have a specific reason to disable it.

learnings.title: Run holdout evaluation with evalctl, not notebooks
learnings.body: The canonical way to score a candidate against the holdout is evalctl run --holdout v3 --model <registry-uri>, which writes the metrics table and the calibration plot to the experiment page. Notebook evaluations have drifted from this in the past, with different thresholds for the same metric. If evalctl is missing a metric you need, file a ticket against eval-tools rather than computing it by hand.

learnings.title: pitjoin lookback window defaults to 30 days
learnings.body: When you call pitjoin for point-in-time feature retrieval, the lookback window defaults to 30 days, which silently drops features older than that for slow-moving entities like merchants. For the merchant risk features you typically need --lookback 180d. The join returns null rather than erroring when the window is too short, so check the null rate in the feature report before training.

learnings.title: Experiment naming convention: team-model-YYYYMMDD-tag
learnings.body: All experiments in the tracking server should follow team-model-YYYYMMDD-tag, for example search-ranker-20240611-dropout03. The tracking server rejects names with uppercase letters or spaces, but it does accept them silently in the UI title field, which causes confusion later. Runs with nonconforming names get auto-archived after 60 days.

learnings.title: Early stopping patience is counted in eval intervals
learnings.body: The patience parameter in our training config counts evaluation intervals, not epochs and not steps. If you set eval_every_steps=500 and patience=10, the run stops after 5000 steps without improvement. Several people assumed patience meant epochs and were surprised by runs ending early on large datasets.

learnings.title: Shared nodes cap dataloader workers at 8
learnings.body: On the shared training nodes, the dataloader is limited to 8 worker processes by a cgroup setting, and anything higher causes the job to be throttled without a clear error. If you set num_workers above 8 you will see GPU utilization drop to around 30 percent while the job appears healthy. Use num_workers=8 and enable prefetch_factor=4 for most image and text pipelines.

learnings.title: Model registry promotion requires a lineage tag
learnings.body: A model version cannot be promoted from staging to production in the registry unless it has a lineage tag pointing at the dataset snapshot and the training commit. Add these with registry tag set --lineage-dataset <snap> --lineage-commit <sha> before running promote. The promote command's error message just says precondition failed, which is not very helpful, so check the tags first.

learnings.title: Class weights applied twice in the ranker wrapper
learnings.body: The ranker wrapper in rankkit applies class weights in the loss function and again in the sampler when balanced_sampling is on, so the minority class effectively gets weighted squared. We found this when calibration plots showed systematic overprediction for the rare category. Turn off class_weights in the loss config whenever balanced_sampling is enabled, or disable the sampler instead.

learnings.title: House default for gradient clipping is global norm 1.0
learnings.body: Unless a model card says otherwise, every training config should set clip_grad_norm to 1.0 using the global norm variant, not per-parameter clipping. This was agreed after the transformer runs in March diverged on two separate occasions. If you need to change it, note the reason in the experiment description so reviewers can see it.

learnings.title: Spot instance runs: checkpoint every 500 steps minimum
learnings.body: When training on spot capacity, set checkpoint_every_steps to no more than 500, because preemption notices give only about 90 seconds and the sync to object storage can take 40 of those seconds. Runs that checkpointed every 2000 steps lost up to an hour of work in the last preemption wave. The spot flag is spot=true in the job spec and is off by default.

learnings.title: Lumen dashboards smooth loss curves by 0.6 by default
learnings.body: The loss panels in the lumen dashboard apply exponential smoothing at 0.6 by default, which can hide a divergence that is happening in the last few hundred steps. Before calling a run stable, switch the smoothing slider to 0 or check the raw series in the export. The smoothing setting is per-user and does not persist across browsers.

learnings.title: Dataset snapshots are identified by manifest content hash
learnings.body: Each dataset snapshot is identified by the SHA-256 of its manifest file, which lists the sorted parquet partitions and their row counts. If you rebuild a snapshot with the same data but a different partition layout, the ID changes, and downstream comparisons will look like they used different data. Use snapctl verify to check whether two snapshot IDs have identical contents before comparing metrics.

learnings.title: Scale learning rate linearly with batch size up to 4096
learnings.body: Our rule of thumb is to scale the learning rate linearly with batch size up to a global batch of 4096, and beyond that switch to the sqrt rule. The scaling helper lives in trainkit as scale_lr(base_lr, base_bs, new_bs, rule='linear'). The rule was validated on the ads CTR model but not on the sequence models, so treat it as a starting point for those.

learnings.title: Grouped AUC must be computed on sorted group keys
learnings.body: The grouped AUC helper in metricslib assumes the input is sorted by group key, and silently returns values that look plausible when it is not. We discovered this when per-merchant AUC on the validation set disagreed with the same computation done in SQL by about 0.02. Call sort_by_group() before passing data in, or use grouped_auc(..., presorted=False), which is slower but safe.

learnings.title: Weekly retrain runs Sunday 02:00 UTC via kiln scheduler
learnings.body: The production ranker retrain is scheduled in kiln for Sundays at 02:00 UTC and takes about four hours on a full allocation. If you need to pause it during a freeze, use kiln pause ranker-weekly and remember to resume it, since kiln does not auto-resume. The scheduler posts a summary to the ml-alerts channel when the job finishes.

learnings.title: Feature drift alert threshold is PSI 0.2
learnings.body: The drift monitor flags a feature when its population stability index against the training baseline exceeds 0.2, and it pages on-call only if three or more features breach together. Single-feature alerts go to the weekly drift digest instead. If you add a new feature, set its baseline window explicitly in drift.yaml, because the default baseline is the first 14 days after launch.

learnings.title: New models run in shadow mode for 72 hours before rollout
learnings.body: Our deployment checklist requires 72 hours of shadow traffic before any new model replaces the production version, with at least 5 percent of requests mirrored. Shadow results are reviewed in the shadow dashboard, and the promotion gate checks that p95 latency is within 10 percent of the incumbent. Skipping shadow requires sign-off from the ML platform lead.

learnings.title: Do not load pickled models; use safetensors
learnings.body: The inference sandbox blocks unpickling of arbitrary objects, so any model saved with pickle will fail to load in production with a cryptic SandboxViolation error. Save weights with safetensors and store the architecture config as JSON alongside it. Legacy .pkl models were migrated last quarter, but a few notebooks still write pickles by default.

learnings.title: Always pass random_state when sampling training rows
learnings.body: When sampling rows with pandas for quick experiments, always pass random_state, because without it the subsample changes on every run and your comparisons become meaningless. The team lint rule flags df.sample() calls without random_state, but the rule only runs on files under src/, not in notebooks. Pick 42 if you have no other preference, to match the rest of the team.

learnings.title: Eval OOM came from accumulating logits on GPU
learnings.body: The evaluation job was running out of GPU memory on the 80k-row validation set because it concatenated all logits on device before computing metrics. Switching to the streaming metric accumulators in evalkit, which move partial sums to CPU per batch, dropped peak memory from 31 GB to under 4 GB. Use accumulate='streaming' in the eval config for any dataset larger than about 20k rows.

learnings.title: Sessionizer uses 30-minute inactivity gap, not 30 minutes from session start
learnings.body: The `sessionize_events` macro in dbt closes a session after 1800 seconds of inactivity measured from the last event, not from the session's first event. If you need fixed-length windows for a funnel report, use `session_window_fixed` instead, which bins by `floor(ts / 1800)`. Mixing the two in one dashboard produced a 12% mismatch in Q2 session counts before we caught it.

learnings.title: Late-arriving mobile events: wait 36 hours before finalizing daily metrics
learnings.body: Mobile SDK batches flush when the device regains connectivity, so about 3% of events for a given day arrive more than 24 hours late. The `daily_active_users` table is marked final only after the `lag_guard` check passes at T+36h. Do not quote DAU numbers from the previous day in Monday stakeholder decks; use the `provisional` flag column instead.

learnings.title: Experiment exposure logging must fire before the variant render
learnings.body: Our experimentation SDK logs an exposure event through `exp.expose(name)` and the assignment is only valid for analysis if that call precedes the UI render. Several teams called it in the `componentDidMount` hook, which fired after the first paint and created a ~6% exposure dilution in the checkout test. Move the call into the route loader, then re-run `exp-audit --test checkout_v3` to confirm the sample ratio matches the 50/50 allocation.

learnings.title: Looker-style explore 'Retention Curve' needs cohort_week filter set explicitly
learnings.body: The Retention Curve explore in our BI tool defaults to a 90-day lookback, which silently drops cohorts older than that and makes long-term retention look artificially flat. Set `cohort_week` to a range in the filter panel or use the saved view `retention_full_history`. Analysts reported this in March when a board slide showed 180-day retention higher than 90-day retention, which is impossible.

learnings.title: Warehouse query cost cap: 2 TB per interactive query on analytics_xs warehouse
learnings.body: The `analytics_xs` warehouse has a per-query scan limit of 2 TB; queries exceeding it fail with `QUOTA_SCAN_EXCEEDED` after about 40 seconds. Filter `events_raw` on `event_date` first, because the table is partitioned by date and clustered on `user_id`. For exploratory work over multiple months, use `events_daily_rollup` which is roughly 300x smaller.

learnings.title: Funnel step ordering in Mixpanel-style tool ignores events with identical timestamps
learnings.body: When two funnel events share the exact same millisecond timestamp, the funnel engine treats the later-listed step as occurring first and drops the conversion. This happens often with `signup_started` and `signup_form_submitted` because the client fires both in one tick. Add a sub-millisecond `seq` property in the SDK, or define the funnel with `allow_same_ts: true` in the funnel config YAML.

learnings.title: Identity stitching: anonymous_id merges into user_id only on login, never backward
learnings.body: Our identity graph in `identity_map` links anonymous IDs to a known user when the `identify` call fires, but it does not retroactively reassign pre-login events in the raw table. Those events remain under the anonymous ID and show up as separate users in unique-user counts. The `stitched_events` view applies the merge at query time and should be used for any user-level question about onboarding.

learnings.title: Q3 north star metric definition: weekly active teams with 3+ members invited
learnings.body: Product agreed in the August planning doc that the north star is weekly active teams that have at least three active members, not raw WAU. The canonical definition lives in the metrics catalog under `nsm_weekly_active_teams` and the dashboard tile must reference that ID rather than a local copy. If you need a variant for a single feature, label it explicitly as a sub-metric so it doesn't get confused with the NSM.

learnings.title: Sample ratio mismatch alert threshold is p < 0.001 with chi-square
learnings.body: The experiment platform runs a chi-square SRM check on every test once it reaches 1,000 exposures per arm, and raises an alert when p falls below 0.001. Earlier we used 0.05 and got flooded with false alarms from bot traffic. A flagged test should not be read out until the SRM cause is documented in the test's `notes` field.

learnings.title: Dashboard 'Activation Overview' refreshes at 06:00 UTC, not local time
learnings.body: The scheduled refresh for the Activation Overview dashboard runs at 06:00 UTC via the `bi-scheduler` job, which means APAC and US Pacific viewers see different 'today' numbers depending on when they open it. Add a note to any exec-facing export stating the reference timezone. We considered moving the job but the warehouse maintenance window makes 06:00 UTC the only safe slot.

learnings.title: Event naming convention: object_action in snake_case, past tense for completed actions
learnings.body: All new tracking events must follow `<object>_<past_tense_verb>`, for example `invoice_created` or `report_exported`, and present-tense names like `create_invoice` will be rejected by the schema linter. The linter runs as a pre-merge check in the `tracking-plans` repo and reads `plan/events.yaml`. Exceptions need a sign-off from the analytics lead and are recorded in the `legacy_names` list.

learnings.title: Duplicate page_view events from SPA route changes: dedupe on route_id plus 2s window
learnings.body: Our single-page app fires `page_view` twice on hash-based navigation because the router emits both a pushState and a hashchange event. The `page_views_clean` model dedupes on `(session_id, route_id)` within a two-second window and keeps the first occurrence. Raw counts from `page_views_raw` overstate pageviews by roughly 18% on the settings section and should not be used for engagement benchmarks.

learnings.title: Holdout group for lifecycle messaging is fixed at 5% and must not be reassigned
learnings.body: The global holdout for lifecycle campaigns uses the `holdout_global_v2` bucket, which assigns 5% of users by hashing the user ID with salt `lc-2024`. Changing the salt or the percentage invalidates all cross-quarter comparisons, so the config is locked in the feature flag service. To exclude users from an individual campaign, use the campaign-level suppression list instead.

learnings.title: Cohort analysis: use signup_date from accounts table, not first_seen from events
learnings.body: The `first_seen` column in `user_events_summary` reflects the first tracked event, which can be days after account creation if the SDK wasn't loaded during signup. For cohort reporting by signup week, join to `accounts.created_at` instead. Using first_seen moved about 4% of users into the wrong monthly cohort in last quarter's board pack.

learnings.title: Quick answer: why does the revenue dashboard show fewer rows than the events table?
learnings.body: The revenue dashboard joins to `subscriptions_current`, which only keeps one row per active subscription, while the events table has a row per billing event. Trials that were converted and cancelled within the same day collapse into a single row. This is intended behavior, and the `subscription_history` table should be used for any question about intra-day transitions.

learnings.title: Tableau-style extract refresh fails if the source view has a trailing space in column names
learnings.body: The nightly extract job for the Product Health workbook failed three nights in a row with a 'column not found' error. The cause was a column named `active_users ` (trailing space) introduced in a dbt model change. Fix the alias in the model, then force a full refresh with `bi-extract refresh --workbook product_health --full`.

learnings.title: Looker-equivalent measure 'Conversion Rate' is defined as orders over sessions, not users
learnings.body: The shared `conversion_rate` measure divides `orders` by `sessions`, so a user with three sessions and one order contributes to the denominator three times. Product PMs often expect a user-level rate, which is available as `user_conversion_rate`. Make sure the label on any slide says which one you are showing.

learnings.title: Segment size estimates in the audience builder are approximate within 2% above 10k users
learnings.body: The audience builder uses HyperLogLog sketches for counts, so reported segment sizes above 10,000 users can differ from exact counts by up to about 2%. Below that threshold it runs an exact count. If you are sizing a campaign that must hit a specific number, request an exact count with the `exact: true` flag in the API call, which takes roughly 90 seconds.

learnings.title: Notebook kernel memory: analytics-jupyter pods are capped at 8 GB
learnings.body: Jupyter pods in the analytics namespace are limited to 8 GB RAM, and loading a full `events_raw` month into pandas will kill the kernel without a clear error. Use the Spark connector via `from lib.spark import session` and aggregate before converting to pandas. The kernel restart message 'Dead kernel' in this environment almost always means OOM.

learnings.title: Experiment metric guardrails: revenue per user requires minimum 14-day runtime
learnings.body: Our experiment platform blocks readout for revenue-per-user guardrails until a test has run for at least 14 full days, because weekly purchase cycles produce large early variance. The override requires a comment in the test's `decision_log` and approval from the analytics lead. Retention guardrails have a 21-day minimum for the same reason.

learnings.title: Event property 'plan_tier' values changed in July: free_v1 replaced by starter
learnings.body: On July 9 the billing service renamed the plan tier `free_v1` to `starter` in the SDK payload, and both values appear in data from that date forward. Use the `plan_tier_normalized` column in `events_enriched`, which maps both to `starter` and includes a `legacy_plan` flag. Comparisons across the boundary should go through that normalized column only.

learnings.title: Onboarding funnel dropped 22% after the telemetry SDK bump; check sdk_version before blaming UX
learnings.body: When the onboarding conversion chart fell sharply in mid-May, the cause was a telemetry SDK upgrade that stopped sending `step_viewed` on web for Safari 16 and below. Before investigating product changes, group the funnel by `sdk_version` and browser in `funnel_debug`. Filing the tracking ticket under the `instrumentation` label speeds up the fix since the SDK team triages that queue first.

learnings.title: Retention definition: 'returned' means any event in product_core category on day N
learnings.body: The official D7 and D30 retention metrics count a user as retained if they fired any event tagged `category = product_core` on that day, not just a login. Marketing pings and background sync events are excluded via the `is_engagement` flag. If you're comparing to the pre-2023 deck, expect numbers about 6 points lower under the old login-based definition.

learnings.title: Backfill procedure for missing event days: run backfill_events with --dry-run first
learnings.body: To backfill a missing day of events from the raw S3 landing zone, run `backfill_events --date 2024-06-14 --dry-run` and check the row count against the expected range in `expected_volume`. Then run it without the flag, which will overwrite partitions in `events_raw` for that date. Never backfill more than seven days at once because the job holds a table-level lock that blocks the nightly rollups.

learnings.title: Attribution window for paid campaign reports is 7-day click, 1-day view
learnings.body: Paid acquisition dashboards use a 7-day click and 1-day view attribution window, configured in `attribution_config.yaml` under `paid_default`. Organic and referral channels are not attributed using these windows and instead use last-touch with no lookback limit. Changing the window requires a review from both marketing ops and finance because it moves reported CAC.

learnings.title: Power calculator: use MDE of 2% relative for checkout tests, otherwise tests run too long
learnings.body: The power calculator in the experiment hub defaults to a 5% minimum detectable effect, which is too coarse for checkout where typical lifts are 1 to 2%. Set `mde_relative = 0.02`, `alpha = 0.05`, and `power = 0.8` for checkout tests, which yields roughly 210,000 users per arm at baseline 3.1% conversion. Document the MDE choice in the test brief so the readout criteria match.

learnings.title: Event ingestion latency SLA: 95th percentile under 90 seconds from client to warehouse
learnings.body: The ingestion pipeline is held to a p95 latency of 90 seconds from client send to availability in `events_raw`, measured by the `ingest_lag_seconds` metric. If the dashboard `ingest-health` shows p95 above 180 seconds for more than ten minutes, page the data-platform on-call through the `#data-oncall` escalation. Analysts should not report real-time metrics that depend on events newer than five minutes without this caveat.

learnings.title: Product tour completion events are logged only on desktop, mobile is still open ticket
learnings.body: The `tour_completed` event is fired by the desktop web client only, and the mobile apps do not emit it because the tour component was never ported. Any completion-rate calculation including mobile users will undercount by roughly the mobile share of tour starts. Ticket PA-1182 tracks the port and is targeted for the next mobile release train.

learnings.title: Looker-style 'Explore' default timezone is account-level, set in admin settings
learnings.body: When a viewer opens an Explore, timestamps display in the account's configured timezone under Admin > Display > Default Timezone, which for our workspace is America/New_York. Schedules and exports, however, use UTC unless the schedule explicitly sets `timezone`. Mismatches here caused two separate off-by-one-day discrepancies in weekly ops reports last quarter.

learnings.title: Survey response analytics: exclude responses under 15 seconds from NPS calculations
learnings.body: The in-app NPS survey logs `completion_seconds` for every response, and responses completed in under 15 seconds are almost always accidental or speeders. The `nps_clean` view excludes them by default, which removes about 4 to 6% of responses each month. If you need the raw distribution for a quality audit, query `nps_raw` directly and state that the numbers include speeders.

learnings.title: Feature adoption dashboard needs feature_flag exposure join or it overcounts
learnings.body: Feature adoption metrics that count `feature_used` events without joining to exposure logs will overcount for features rolled out gradually, because users who never saw the feature can still trigger events from shared components. Use the `adoption_exposed` model, which joins to `flag_exposures` on user and flag key within the rollout window. Expect adoption rates to drop 10 to 30 points versus the naive count for features in staged rollout.

learnings.title: Lantern UTM medium values are case-sensitive in Foghorn reports
learnings.body: Lantern writes UTM parameters exactly as entered, and Foghorn groups 'Paid_Social' and 'paid_social' as separate rows. Use only the lowercase values listed in the taxonomy sheet. Run `lantern lint --campaign <id>` before publishing to catch mixed-case values.

learnings.title: Harbor CRM routing sends blank-Region leads to the default queue
learnings.body: Harbor evaluates the Region field before Territory, and a blank Region silently falls through to the default SDR queue. The nightly region_from_zip job at 02:10 UTC backfills most of these. If a lead still has no region the next morning, assign it by hand in Harbor rather than leaving it for the job.

learnings.title: Kiln preview links die after 24 hours with a 403
learnings.body: Reviewers who open a Kiln preview link after 24 hours see a 403 with the error preview_expired. Rotate the link from Kiln > Share > Rotate preview, then send the new URL. Do not forward the old link in Slack threads, because it will look like a broken page to the reviewer.

learnings.title: Keystone offline conversions need click IDs younger than 90 days
learnings.body: Keystone Ads rejects offline conversion uploads when the gclid or msclkid is older than 90 days, and it reports the failure as a generic partial import. Export conversions from Harbor weekly so the click IDs are still in the window. Check the rejected-rows CSV in Keystone under Imports > History.

learnings.title: Quarry asset library: filenames with spaces break CDN paths
learnings.body: Assets uploaded to Quarry with spaces in the filename get a URL-encoded path that the brand CDN caches under a different key, so the old version keeps serving for hours. Rename files to kebab-case before upload. If you have already uploaded one, run `quarry purge --path /assets/<name>` to clear it.

learnings.title: Mosaic A/B tests need at least 400 visitors per arm to call a winner
learnings.body: The Mosaic dashboard shows a winner badge as soon as one arm leads, even with very few visitors. Our team rule is at least 400 unique visitors per arm and two full business weeks before anyone declares a result. Anything earlier goes in the test notes as 'inconclusive' so it doesn't get rolled out by accident.

learnings.title: Campaign naming convention for the ad managers
learnings.body: Every paid campaign name follows the pattern region-channel-objective-yyyymm-variant, for example emea-search-demo-202409-a. The naming check in Foghorn rejects names that don't match, but it only runs on the campaign level, not ad sets. Ad set names should follow the same pattern with the audience segment appended.

learnings.title: Beacon sync drops contacts that have no company domain
learnings.body: Beacon's contact sync to Harbor skips any contact whose company domain is empty, and it logs this as a skipped_no_domain event instead of an error. Webinar registrants who sign up with personal addresses are the usual cause. Use the enrichment fallback in Beacon settings to infer the domain from the form's company name field.

learnings.title: Webinar registration caps are enforced per session, not per series
learnings.body: On the Tallyburst event platform, the seat cap belongs to each session in a series. A 100-seat cap on a four-part series means up to 400 total registrations, which surprised the Q3 team. Set the cap on each session individually and check the waitlist settings for the series page.

learnings.title: Press kit PDFs regenerate only when the source deck is re-exported
learnings.body: The press kit generator pulls from the Quarry deck snapshot, not from the live slides. If you update the logo or the boilerplate paragraph, you need to re-export the source deck from Quarry first, then click Regenerate in PressDesk. Otherwise the old boilerplate stays in the PDF even though the page looks correct.

learnings.title: SparkRoute social scheduler ignores posts queued during maintenance
learnings.body: Posts scheduled inside SparkRoute's Tuesday 01:00 to 01:30 UTC maintenance window are marked 'published' but never actually go out. This has happened twice and was only caught when engagement stayed at zero. Schedule around that window and check the outbound log the next morning for any post stuck in 'queued'.

learnings.title: Lead score decay runs on the first of each month
learnings.body: The Harbor lead score decay job subtracts 10 percent from any score older than 60 days on the first day of the month. Sales has complained about hot leads cooling off suddenly, so marketing exempts anyone with a demo request in the last 90 days. Do not change the decay rate without a note in the #revops-changes channel.

learnings.title: Form field 'Company Size' must use the picklist values, not free text
learnings.body: Forms built in Kiln send Company Size as a free-text string if the picklist is not linked, and Harbor then maps everything to 'Unknown' during import. Always pick the field from the Harbor object list when adding it. The valid values are 1-49, 50-249, 250-999, and 1000+, and nothing else maps.

learnings.title: Brand guidelines: the approved blue is #1F4E9C, not the old #2255AA
learnings.body: The rebrand replaced #2255AA with #1F4E9C across all templates, but a few legacy banners in Quarry still use the old value. Designers have been pulling colors from those files by eye. Use the brand token picker in Kiln, which only offers the new palette, and treat any other blue as a bug to report.

learnings.title: Survey responses from the Tallyburst NPS form exclude partial submits
learnings.body: Tallyburst only exports completed NPS responses to the analytics warehouse, so the dashboards undercount detractors who abandon after the score question. To include partials, use the raw_responses export from Tallyburst's API rather than the scheduled report. Partial rows have a null comment field, which is expected.

learnings.title: Redirect rules for retired product pages live in Kiln, not the CDN
learnings.body: When a product page is retired, add the redirect in Kiln under Site > Redirects, because CDN-level rules are overwritten by each Kiln deploy. Add the rule with a 301 status and point it at the closest live category page. Check the rule count in Kiln before the quarterly SEO audit, which caps at 2,000 rules.

learnings.title: Paid social audiences from Harbor refresh at 06:00 local time
learnings.body: Custom audience syncs from Harbor to the social ad platforms run at 06:00 in each account's configured timezone, not in UTC. A list uploaded at 05:45 Pacific will not reach the platform until the next day. If a launch depends on a fresh list, upload the audience by 05:00 in that timezone.

learnings.title: Intent data scores are per-account, so don't assign them to contacts
learnings.body: The Glimmer intent feed only scores company accounts, and our Harbor import mapped scores to contacts for two weeks in March. Those contact-level intent fields are now deprecated, and reports built on them show inflated numbers. Use the account-level field intent_score_30d for all segmentation.

learnings.title: Event badge printing needs the 3x2 template, not the default
learnings.body: The badge printer at the Denver booth jams if you send the default Tallyburst badge template, which is 4x6. Use the 3x2 template named badge_compact in the export settings. Print a single test badge first, because the printer driver resets to 4x6 after every power cycle.

learnings.title: Landing page A/B variants inherit the control's analytics tags
learnings.body: When you duplicate a Kiln page to make a variant, the analytics tag manager container ID is copied, but the page_variant parameter is not updated automatically. Both variants then report under the control's name in Foghorn. Set page_variant manually in the page's custom head section before you start the test.

learnings.title: Content calendar: blog posts need a legal review tag before scheduling
learnings.body: Kiln will schedule any blog post, but the content calendar in Quarry only moves an item to 'ready' when the legal-review tag is present. Posts that mention pricing, benchmarks, or customer names need that tag or they get pulled by the compliance bot. Ask the legal queue for a review at least three business days before the planned publish date.

learnings.title: Search ad keyword imports cap at 5,000 rows per file
learnings.body: Keystone Ads silently truncates keyword CSVs above 5,000 rows, and the import still reports success with a green check. Split large keyword lists into batches of 4,500 to leave margin for header rows. Compare the row count in Keystone's imported keywords view against your source file after each upload.

learnings.title: Link shortener domains expire if no click occurs for 180 days
learnings.body: Lantern deactivates short links that receive no clicks for 180 days, and it returns a plain 410 page with no redirect. Printed materials and QR codes at trade shows have broken this way. Before a campaign ends, run `lantern report --idle 150d` to list links approaching the cutoff and extend them.

learnings.title: Harbor campaign influence reports use the first-touch window of 30 days
learnings.body: The default influence window in Harbor is 30 days from first touch, and it does not reset on later touches. Pipeline reviews often assume a 90-day window, which makes paid programs look much weaker than they are. Ask RevOps to change the window in the Influence settings if the program needs a longer view, and note the change in the team wiki.

learnings.title: Email preheader text longer than 90 characters gets cut off on mobile
learnings.body: Preheader text in our Kiln template editor shows a counter, but the mobile preview clips at about 90 characters. Keep preheaders under 90 characters and put the key offer in the first 40. Check the mobile preview in the template editor under the phone icon, since the desktop preview is not representative.

learnings.title: Q3 campaign budget approvals route to the finance lead after 4,000 dollars
learnings.body: Campaign budget requests in Foghorn route to the marketing director for amounts under 4,000 and to the finance lead above that. Requests split into multiple lines to stay under the threshold are flagged automatically in the weekly audit. Plan the full program as a single request, even if it spans multiple channels.

learnings.title: Merging duplicate contacts: check open opps owned by different AEs first
learnings.body: Run `crmctl merge --keep-oldest --dry-run` before any real merge, because the tool keeps the oldest CreatedDate record and reparents activities onto it. If either contact has an open opportunity owned by a different AE, the merge will hand that opp to whoever owns the surviving record. Ask the AE managers to confirm ownership in #revops-merges before running it without the dry-run flag.

learnings.title: LeadRouter skips OOO reps and dumps leftovers into unassigned-smb
learnings.body: LeadRouter round-robins inbound leads across the SMB pool, but it skips any rep whose Presence_Status is OOO. If the whole pool is OOO at once, leads land in the queue 'unassigned-smb' instead of erroring. That queue is reviewed Mondays at 9am Pacific by whoever is on the routing rota.

learnings.title: Closed Won needs Contract_Signed_Date or validation rule OPP-V14 fires
learnings.body: Opportunities cannot move to Closed Won without a populated Contract_Signed_Date__c. Users often see the generic error 'OPP-V14' and assume the stage picklist is broken. Fill in the signed date first, then change the stage.

learnings.title: Industry picklist has both Fintech and FinTech; canonical value is Fintech
learnings.body: The Industry picklist ended up with two values that differ only in capitalization, and the dashboards split the counts between them. Canonical value is 'Fintech'. The picklist-normalize job runs weekly and remaps 'FinTech' to 'Fintech' on Account records, but it does not touch Lead records yet.

learnings.title: Territory rebalance runs 02:00 UTC on the 1st; manual edits get overwritten
learnings.body: The terr-rebalance batch reassigns accounts to AEs on the first of each month at 02:00 UTC. Any manual owner change made between roughly 01:30 and 02:30 UTC on that day is overwritten. If you need a change to survive, submit it through the territory-map request form before the 25th.

learnings.title: Board Forecast tile excludes Best Case; Commit needs a close date this quarter
learnings.body: The Board Forecast tile in the revenue dashboard sums Commit and Closed Won only, so Best Case deals do not appear in it. An opportunity can only be set to Commit if its close date falls inside the current fiscal quarter, otherwise the save is blocked. Pipeline reviews should use the 'Full Pipe' tile if you need Best Case visibility.

learnings.title: Account hierarchy: never set ParentId to the record itself
learnings.body: The account importer loops forever if an Account's ParentId points to itself, and it does not fail loudly. The symptom is a stuck import job with the status 'running' for hours. Before loading hierarchy data, run the parent-check script in the crm-tools repo to catch self-references and cycles.

learnings.title: pipeline-snap freezes Friday 23:59 Pacific; use the Q-Snap tile for weekly numbers
learnings.body: The pipeline-snap job takes a frozen copy of the pipeline every Friday at 23:59 Pacific. Numbers in the live pipeline view on Monday morning will differ from the prior Friday's, so do not compare them directly. For week-over-week reporting, use the Q-Snap tile in Looker, which reads only from the frozen copies.

learnings.title: Phone numbers must be E.164 or the dialer silently drops them
learnings.body: The dialer integration rejects any phone number with spaces, parentheses, or dashes, and it does not show an error in the UI. Store numbers in E.164 format such as +14155550123. The normalize-phone task runs nightly on Contact and Lead records and logs failures to the #data-quality channel.

learnings.title: Discounts above 25% need deal desk approval via /dd approve in Slack
learnings.body: Any opportunity where the discount exceeds 25% of list price is locked until deal desk approves it.
