Request approval by posting in #deal-desk with the opp ID, then the approver runs `/dd approve OPP-id` in Slack. Approvals older than 5 business days expire automatically and must be re-requested.

learnings.title: Sandbox refresh happens every second Tuesday; emails are scrambled
learnings.body: The CRM sandbox is refreshed from production on alternating Tuesdays, and the refresh wipes any changes made in the sandbox since the last refresh. Contact emails are scrambled during the copy, so do not use the sandbox to test email-based matching. Ask #sales-ops-eng before scheduling tests that depend on specific records.

learnings.title: Bulk Owner updates fail silently for inactive users; check IsActive first
learnings.body: When you bulk update the OwnerId field through the API, records assigned to an inactive user are skipped without an error in the job result. The job still reports success with a processed count that looks right. Query the User object for IsActive = true before building the batch file.

learnings.title: Lead Match Email duplicate rule blocks saves; integrations user can override
learnings.body: The standard duplicate rule 'Lead Match Email' blocks any new Lead whose email matches an existing record. Only the integrations user with the allow_dedupe_override flag can bypass it, by sending the header X-Dedupe-Override: true. Do not give that flag to individual sales users, since they will start creating duplicates again.

learnings.title: Lead status Working reverts to New after 30 days of inactivity
learnings.body: The lead-decay job sweeps Leads every night and moves any with status Working and no activity in 30 days back to New. Reps often see leads they were actively working reappear in the New queue and get reassigned. Log at least one activity per month on Working leads to keep them out of the sweep.

learnings.title: Closed Lost requires a reason code from LR-01 to LR-07
learnings.body: Closed Lost opportunities must include Loss_Reason_Code__c. The valid codes are LR-01 Price, LR-02 Timing, LR-03 Competitor, LR-04 No budget, LR-05 No decision, LR-06 Champion left, and LR-07 Other. Win/loss reporting excludes LR-07 from the top-reasons chart, so use it only when nothing else fits.

learnings.title: Field history retention is 18 months; audit reports come from crm-audit dataset
learnings.body: Field history tracking for Opportunity and Account is retained for 18 months and then purged. For audit questions older than that, the crm-audit BigQuery dataset holds a nightly export back to the start of 2021. Query the dataset rather than the CRM UI when you need stage change history beyond the retention window.

learnings.title: renewal-spawner creates renewal opps 90 days out; check for manual duplicates
learnings.body: The renewal-spawner job creates a renewal opportunity 90 days before each subscription end date. Reps who create their own renewal opp manually end up with two open records for the same contract. Before creating one by hand, search for an existing opp with the Renewal record type on that account.

learnings.title: Opportunity amounts are stored in USD; use CAD_Converted for Canadian reporting
learnings.body: All Opportunity Amount values are stored in USD, and the CAD_Converted__c field holds the amount converted at the fx-table rate. The fx-table is refreshed on the 3rd of each month, so CAD figures for the first two days use the prior month's rate. Use the converted field in board decks and the raw Amount field everywhere else.

learnings.title: Partner_Ref must match the partner registry ID exactly or the lead orphans
learnings.body: The Partner_Ref__c field on Lead must match an ID in the partner registry exactly, including case. A typo does not block the save; it just means the partner commission job never picks up the lead. Use the lookup picker in the Lead form rather than typing the reference by hand.

learnings.title: crm-sync-gw resolves conflicts last-write-wins, except Owner where the CRM wins
learnings.body: When the warehouse sync and the CRM both edit the same Account, crm-sync-gw keeps the most recent write for most fields. For OwnerId, the CRM value always wins, regardless of timestamp. If you need to change an owner, make the change in the CRM rather than in the source table.

learnings.title: Unmerge is possible for 72 hours with crmctl unmerge <job-id>
learnings.body: After a merge, the original records can be restored with `crmctl unmerge <job-id>` for 72 hours. The job ID is printed at the end of the merge output and is also in the merge-log channel. After 72 hours the original records are purged and the only recovery path is a restore from the nightly backup, which takes about two business days.

learnings.title: Stale-opp flag: no activity in 45 days sets Stale_Flag and sends a Monday digest
learnings.body: Opportunities with no logged activity for 45 days get Stale_Flag__c set to true, and the owning rep gets a digest every Monday. Stale opps are excluded from the forecast, which surprises people the first time it happens. Log a call, meeting, or task to clear the flag.

learnings.title: Opp naming: Account - Product - QQ-YY, trailing spaces break the pivot
learnings.body: Team convention for Opportunity Name is 'Account - Product - QQ-YY', for example 'Northwind - Analytics - Q3-24'. A trailing space after the product name splits one deal into two rows in the partner pivot. Run the name-trim cleanup in the opp-hygiene report monthly to catch these.

learnings.title: Excel export from list views caps at 50,000 rows; use snapshot export instead
learnings.body: List view exports from the CRM stop silently at 50,000 rows, and the file looks complete. For larger extracts, use the snapshot export job, which writes to the shared drive folder 'CRM Exports' within about 20 minutes. Check the row count against the report total before sharing any extract.

learnings.title: Territory caps at 400 accounts per AE; the rebalance skips anyone over the cap
learnings.body: The territory engine caps each AE at 400 owned accounts. When the monthly rebalance runs and an AE is already at the cap, the job skips the account and leaves it with the previous owner. Check the Territory_Load report before assigning a large batch by hand.

learnings.title: Competitor__c multi-select allows three values maximum
learnings.body: The Competitor__c multi-select on Opportunity accepts at most three values. A fourth selection is rejected with a generic save error. If a deal has more than three competitors, pick the three most relevant and add the rest to the Notes field so they still show up in search.

learnings.title: Q: Why did my lead disappear? A: Check for a Lead Conversion to a Contact
learnings.body: Leads that were converted to Contacts no longer appear in lead views, so they look deleted. Search the Contact object by email instead, and the converted record will show a Converted_From_Lead__c value. The conversion history is also visible in the Activity timeline on the new Contact.

learnings.title: Weekly data steward rota rotates Tuesday standup; claim tickets in the #crm-steward channel
learnings.body: The CRM data steward role rotates each month among the sales ops team, with handoff at the Tuesday standup. The steward owns the weekly data-quality triage queue in Jira project CRMHYG. Post in #crm-steward before taking a ticket so two people do not fix the same records.

learnings.title: ContractVault auto-renewal flags miss 60-day opt-out windows
learnings.body: ContractVault only raises the auto-renewal alert 45 days before term end, which is too late for clauses with a 60-day opt-out notice. For any contract tagged AR-2, set the custom reminder to 75 days using `cv reminder add --contract <id> --days 75`. Legal ops checks the AR-2 list every Monday.

learnings.title: Redline exports drop tracked changes inside footers
learnings.body: When you export a redline from RedlineBot to PDF, changes made in header and footer blocks don't render. Export to DOCX instead, or run the Compare tab with the 'Include headers/footers' box ticked. Counsel has been burned by this twice, so always eyeball footers before sending to the counterparty.

learnings.title: Use clause CL-GOV-07 for governing law, not the 07a variant
learnings.body: CL-GOV-07a was the pre-2023 Delaware wording and it omits the jury waiver. The current library entry is CL-GOV-07, and ClauseIndex will still surface 07a in search results. If you find 07a in an in-flight draft, swap it before the next turn.

learnings.title: Subprocessor additions need 30 days written notice in the DPA
learnings.body: Our standard DPA annex III requires 30 days' notice before any new subprocessor processes customer data. Account teams sometimes add a vendor to the portal the same week it is signed. Post the proposed subprocessor in the #privacy-notices channel first and let the notice clock run before enabling it in production.

learnings.title: DocuSeal DPA envelopes require counsel initials on Annex II
learnings.body: In DocuSeal, the Annex II signature block has a hidden initials field that defaults to unassigned. If counsel doesn't initial it, the envelope completes but the customer's procurement team often rejects it later. Assign the initials field to the legal reviewer role when you create the envelope.

learnings.title: SLA credit cap is 15% of monthly fees under MSA template v4
learnings.body: The v4 MSA caps service credits at 15% of the monthly fees for the affected service, not total contract value. Several sales reps have quoted 25% from an older deck. If a customer asks for more, route to the deal desk instead of editing the cap in the MSA.

learnings.title: Gross negligence carve-out checklist before approving indemnity
learnings.body: Before approving any indemnity language, confirm the carve-out list includes gross negligence and willful misconduct. The most common miss is a customer-drafted paragraph that says 'negligence' without the gross qualifier. Mark it in the Indemnity checklist tab of the review sheet so the approver sees it.

learnings.title: Vendor onboarding is blocked until W-9 and security questionnaire attach
learnings.body: The procurement gate in VendorGate won't release a vendor record to accounts payable until it has a current W-9 and a completed security questionnaire attached. Legal's contract review can start in parallel, but the PO won't generate without both. If a vendor refuses the questionnaire, ask the CISO's office for the exception form SEC-EX-3 rather than skipping the gate.

learnings.title: LexQueue turnaround targets for standard NDAs
learnings.body: Standard mutual NDAs using the approved template go through LexQueue with a one business day target. Anything with a non-template governing law or a residuals clause moves to the three day track automatically. Ask for the 'expedite' label only if a deal is blocked, since it bumps other requests down.

learnings.title: Default liability cap is 12 months of fees
learnings.body: Our default limitation of liability is fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim. Any request for a higher cap, including the super-cap for data breaches at 3x, needs sign-off from the VP of Legal in Approvals. Don't agree to a number on a call and promise paper later.

learnings.title: Pen-test addendum needs the current SOC 2 bridge letter attached
learnings.body: When a customer's security team asks for the pen-test addendum, attach the most recent SOC 2 bridge letter from the Compliance drive folder, path /Compliance/Attestations/current. The bridge letter must cover the date of the customer's requested review. Old bridge letters from last year have caused two escalations this quarter.

learnings.title: Backup data purge in DPA annex is 90 days, not 30
learnings.body: The retention language in the DPA annex II says backup copies are purged within 90 days of deletion, while primary storage is purged within 30 days. Engineering's runbook for the backup-expiry job is set to 90, so don't quote 30 in a customer call. If a customer asks for faster purge, escalate to platform engineering for a feasibility estimate.

learnings.title: ScreenHub export screening before sending to a new country
learnings.body: Before we onboard a customer in a country we haven't served, run the entity name through ScreenHub with `sh screen --entity '<legal name>' --country <ISO2>`. A 'possible match' result isn't a block, but you need to attach the match report to the deal record. Sanctions questions go to the trade compliance mailbox, not the deal channel.

learnings.title: cmp-docs CLI ignores list numbering when comparing versions
learnings.body: Running `cmp-docs --ignore-numbering v3.docx v4.docx` gives a cleaner diff than the default when a clause has been renumbered after a deletion. Without the flag, every subsequent clause shows as changed, which buries the real edits. Paste the output into the review thread as plain text, not as an attachment.

learnings.title: SignPath envelopes expire after 14 days and must be re-sent
learnings.body: SignPath envelopes auto-expire 14 days after sending, and the expiry is not shown in the counterparty email. Several signed-order deals stalled because the signer opened the link after expiry and got a generic error. Set a calendar reminder for day 10 and re-send with `signpath resend --envelope <id>` if still unsigned.

learnings.title: Governing law default is Delaware, Ireland for EU enterprise
learnings.body: Our default governing law is Delaware for US-based customers and Ireland for EU enterprise customers with a data processing role. Customers in the UK are usually fine with Ireland but ask for England and Wales about a third of the time. Any other jurisdiction needs a short memo from outside counsel before it goes into a draft.

learnings.title: Auto-renewal opt-out clause must be 60 days, AR-2 template
learnings.body: The AR-2 renewal clause in the order form template requires customers to give 60 days' written notice to opt out of renewal. Sales sometimes shortens it to 30 days to close a deal, which then creates an unbillable renewal dispute. Changes to AR-2 require a redline approved by legal ops, not a manual edit in the order form.

learnings.title: ContractVault to Salesforce metadata sync runs at 02:15
learnings.body: Contract metadata (term end, renewal date, governing law) syncs from ContractVault to the Salesforce Contract object at 02:15 daily. If you update a term in ContractVault mid-afternoon, Salesforce won't reflect it until the next morning. For urgent changes, use the manual push button on the contract record, which takes about five minutes.

learnings.title: Order form 'Term End' must equal MSA effective date plus term length
learnings.body: The order form validator in ContractVault compares the Term End field against the MSA effective date plus the term length in months. If they disagree, the record is flagged but still saves, so it's easy to miss. Fix it before sending the order form, since the billing system reads Term End directly.

learnings.title: Change-of-control clause triggers mandatory legal review
learnings.body: Any assignment clause that mentions change of control needs legal review before the customer's M&A notice is answered, even if the contract otherwise looks routine. In the last year, two customers were acquired and one tried to assign to a shell entity without notice. Tag the contract with COC in ContractVault so it appears on the weekly watchlist.

learnings.title: Minimum insurance: cyber $5M, E&O $3M for enterprise deals
learnings.body: Enterprise customer contracts require cyber liability coverage of at least $5M and technology E&O coverage of at least $3M. Ask the risk team for the current certificate of insurance rather than sending an old PDF from the shared drive. Certificates must name the customer as additional insured where the MSA says so.

learnings.title: Search ClauseIndex with quoted phrases for exact matches
learnings.body: ClauseIndex treats unquoted search terms as loose keywords, so a search for 'residuals' returns every MSA with the word in any context. Wrap the phrase in double quotes, for example "residuals clause", to match exact wording. Add the field filter `type:indemnity` to narrow results further when looking for precedent.

learnings.title: LicenseGate flags GPL-3.0 dependencies in customer deliverables
learnings.body: LicenseGate blocks any SDK release containing a GPL-3.0 dependency, and a customer's contract may ban copyleft outright. If a build fails on GPL-3.0, check the dependency tree with `lg tree --why <package>` before asking engineering for a swap. Document any approved exception in the OSS register with a link to the legal sign-off.

learnings.title: Quarterly template audit: retire MSA v2 by March 31
learnings.body: All active MSA v2 templates must be retired from the contract library by March 31, since v2 lacks the updated data processing terms. The audit spreadsheet in the Legal Ops folder lists 41 open deals still referencing v2 as of last review. Migrate open deals at renewal rather than amending them mid-term, unless the customer is already asking for changes.

learnings.title: hrsync-pull drops hires whose manager email has uppercase letters
learnings.body: The nightly hrsync-pull job matches manager emails against the Directory table case-sensitively, so a hire whose manager is listed as Jane.Doe@ instead of jane.doe@ gets created with no manager and lands in the unassigned queue. Correct the record in Workday-Lite, then run `hrsync-pull --rerun --normalize-emails` to lowercase before matching.

learnings.title: PTO accrual runs 02:00 UTC on the 1st and credits the prior month
learnings.body: The pto-accrue job fires at 02:00 UTC on the first of each month and credits hours for the previous month. Mid-month hires are prorated by business days using the holidays-us-2024 calendar. If a payslip looks short, check the accrual ledger for a row dated before the start date before recalculating by hand.

learnings.title: Leave requests over 10 consecutive days need a second approver in Tempo
learnings.body: House rule: any leave block longer than 10 consecutive working days requires a second approver from the skip-level chain. Tempo will accept a single approval without complaint, so the check is not automatic. Ask People Ops to confirm the second approval before the leave starts.

learnings.title: Calibration sheets lock at 14:00 on the 14th or the review cycle breaks
learnings.body: Calibration spreadsheets in the perf-cal workspace lock automatically at 14:00 local on the 14th of the review month. Edits after that show as read-only and the lock cannot be lifted by managers. Request an unlock from HR Ops with the sheet ID and a reason, and expect a 24-hour turnaround.

learnings.title: Revoke badge access before the laptop wipe, not after
learnings.body: Offboarding order matters: if the laptop is wiped first, the device-check in Keystone fails because the account still shows as active, and the ticket gets stuck in Pending Device. Run `offboard --step badge-revoke` first, then `offboard --step device-wipe`. Both steps are idempotent, so rerunning is safe.

learnings.title: VerifyPro background checks sit at pending for 72h on international addresses
learnings.body: Background checks for candidates with non-US addresses routinely show 'pending' for three days in the VerifyPro dashboard, even when the vendor has finished. Don't re-submit, since a duplicate order is billed twice. Check the case timeline tab instead, where the real status appears under 'international routing'.

learnings.title: Parental leave uses code PL-2 in Tempo, not PL-1
learnings.body: PL-1 is reserved for medical leave related to pregnancy and recovery, and PL-2 covers bonding and caregiver leave. Selecting the wrong code routes the request to the wrong benefits workflow and delays pay continuation by about a week. If you see a PL-1 request for a newborn, reassign it in Tempo's admin panel.

learnings.title: Comp band lookups: L3 through L7, updated each April from bandlookup
learnings.body: Compensation bands live in bandlookup.internal and cover levels L3 through L7 in each region. The bands are refreshed every April after the market survey, and mid-year edits require a comp committee note. Always check the effective-date column, because the UI shows the latest band even if it hasn't taken effect yet.

learnings.title: Timesheets close Monday 17:00 Pacific for the Friday pay run
learnings.body: Timesheets in Clockwork must be submitted and approved by Monday 17:00 Pacific for the pay run that goes out the following Friday. Anything approved after that is carried to the next run as a manual adjustment. Managers can approve on behalf of their reports with `clockwork approve --bulk --team`.

learnings.title: Relocation to a new state needs a Relocate form before your first day there
learnings.body: If you're moving to a new state for work, file the work-location change in Relocate before your first day in the new location. Payroll uses the form to set state withholding, and a late filing means withholding from the old state for up to two pay periods. Attach your lease or utility bill as proof of address.

learnings.title: Scorecard template eng-panel-v3 auto-hides after five days
learnings.body: Interview scorecards built from eng-panel-v3 automatically move to the archive tab five days after the interview date. Interviewers who submit after that won't see their form in the candidate view, and it looks like nothing was recorded. Unarchive with the 'restore' button on the candidate page, or ask Recruiting Ops to extend the window.

learnings.title: Headcount request IDs are REQ-YYYY-NNNN and sync to the board hourly
learnings.body: Each headcount request gets an ID of the form REQ-YYYY-NNNN, and the Headcount Board pulls changes from the request tracker once an hour on the hour. A request approved at 14:05 won't show as open on the board until 15:00. Don't open a duplicate requisition while you wait, since the finance approval attaches to the original ID.

learnings.title: Open enrollment closes 23:59 local on Nov 15; late changes need reason QLE
learnings.body: Benefits open enrollment closes at 23:59 in your local time zone on November 15. Changes after the window require a qualifying life event, entered in the Benefits Portal with reason code QLE and a supporting document uploaded within 30 days. Requests without a document are auto-rejected overnight.

learnings.title: Sick-day requests auto-approve after two business days of manager silence
learnings.body: The sick-autoapprove script runs every weekday morning and approves any sick-leave request in Tempo that has sat unanswered for two business days. This is intentional so employees aren't penalized for a manager's absence. Managers who want to deny a request must act within that window or ask HR to reopen it.

learnings.title: LearnLoop training completions take about six hours to reach the compliance dashboard
learnings.body: When someone finishes the annual security training in LearnLoop, the completion syncs to the Compliance Dashboard roughly six hours later, not instantly. Re-requesting the course in that window creates a second assignment and sends a false overdue reminder. Check the sync status page before escalating to the security team.

learnings.title: Equity cliff is 12 months from grant date, and grant date is the board approval date
learnings.body: In Capshare, the one-year cliff is measured from the grant date, which is the board approval date rather than the employee's start date. For hires approved before their start, the vesting clock starts earlier than many expect. Confirm the grant date on the award letter before quoting a vesting schedule to a candidate.

learnings.title: Converting a contractor to FTE: new employee ID first, then run convert-contractor
learnings.body: To convert a contractor, create the new employee record in Workday-Lite first, then run `convert-contractor --from VND-id --to EMP-id` so the history carries over. Running the convert before the employee record exists leaves the vendor account active and double-bills the next invoice cycle. Vendor Master needs to be deactivated by Finance afterward.

learnings.title: Legal name changes need a Dossier upload; preferred names only sync display
learnings.body: A legal name change must be supported by a document uploaded to Dossier, such as a court order or marriage certificate. Changing only the preferred name updates display in Slack and the directory but not payroll or tax forms. Payroll changes require the legal name workflow, which takes about two business days.

learnings.title: Reference check form RC-7 in Formly goes only through the recruiter
learnings.body: Hiring managers should not contact candidate references directly. All reference checks are sent through the recruiter using form RC-7 in Formly, which logs the call and the reference's consent. Managers who reach out on their own have caused two candidate complaints this year, so route everything through the recruiter queue.

learnings.title: Exit survey links expire after 14 days, resend with exit-survey --resend
learnings.body: The exit survey link sent after an offboarding expires after 14 days, and the response rate drops sharply after the first week. Run `exit-survey --resend --employee EMP-id` to issue a fresh link to the departed employee's personal email on file. Responses stay anonymous to the manager in the aggregate report.

learnings.title: OrgChart rebuilds Sunday night, so Monday manager changes show a week late
learnings.body: The OrgChart is rebuilt from Workday-Lite every Sunday night, so any manager change entered during the week only appears on the chart the following Monday. Access checks that depend on the chart use the old reporting line until the rebuild finishes. For urgent access changes, use `orgchart patch` to apply the change immediately.

learnings.title: Visa status H1B-pending auto-opens a Legal review ticket in LGL-IMM
learnings.body: Setting a visa status to H1B-pending in Workday-Lite automatically opens a ticket in the LGL-IMM queue for immigration counsel. Start dates should not be confirmed to the candidate until that ticket is closed, which usually takes ten business days. Don't reuse an old ticket, because each filing needs its own record.

learnings.title: Accommodation requests live in the Vault hr-accom folder, never in Jira
learnings.body: Requests for workplace accommodations must be stored only in the Vault folder hr-accom, which restricts access to HR case managers. Jira tickets are visible to the whole engineering org and have leaked sensitive details before. If you receive an accommodation request in a ticket, move it to Vault and delete the original text.

learnings.title: Floating holidays are set per region in holidays-config.yaml
learnings.body: Each region gets its own floating holiday allowance in holidays-config.yaml, currently two days for US, one for UK, and three for India. Changes take effect on the next accrual run, not immediately on the calendar. Employees who joined after January have their allowance prorated by the start month.

learnings.title: Probation reviews at day 90 send a Nudge reminder; reassign it if the manager is out
learnings.body: A probation review reminder goes to the manager through Nudge on day 90 of employment. If the manager is on leave, the reminder keeps going to their inbox and nobody completes the review, which can silently extend probation. Use `nudge reassign --review ID --to backup-manager` so the backup gets the task.

learnings.title: Three-way match tolerance is set per vendor class, not globally
learnings.body: The ap-match service reads tolerances from vendor_classes.yaml, and the default is 2% for services vendors and 0% for goods vendors. If a goods invoice is off by a small amount, check the vendor's class in Vendorvault before assuming the match engine is broken. Changing a class tolerance needs sign-off from the AP controller and a ticket in FIN-OPS.

learnings.title: Duplicate check ignores leading zeros but not suffixes
learnings.body: dupcheck normalizes invoice numbers by stripping leading zeros, so INV-0042 and INV-42 from the same vendor are flagged. It does not strip suffixes, so INV-42A and INV-42 are treated as different invoices. When a vendor reissues a corrected invoice with a suffix, expect it to pass through and reject the original manually.

learnings.title: Bank detail changes: callback first, then 24h hold
learnings.body: Any change to a vendor's remittance bank details in Vendorvault puts the record into a 24-hour hold, and no payments go to the new account during that window. Before you submit the change, call the vendor on the phone number already on file, not one from the change request email. Log the callback in the ticket. Skipping this has been the path for two attempted fraud cases this year.

learnings.title: Invoices arriving before goods receipt sit in 'awaiting receipt'
learnings.body: The WMS goods receipt sync runs nightly at 02:10, so invoices for goods received the same day will show 'awaiting receipt' until morning. Don't reject them. Once the receipt posts, run apctl rematch --po PO-number to force a re-match instead of waiting for the next sweep.

learnings.title: Approval chain escalates after 72 hours to the controller's group
learnings.body: ledgerbot sends approval requests to the budget owner and times out after 72 hours. At that point the invoice is reassigned to the controllership queue, which adds about three days of delay on average. If you know a budget owner is out, reassign the approval yourself in Lakeshore Ledger under Actions > Delegate.

learnings.title: 1099-eligible vendors blocked until W-9 is on file
learnings.body: Vendors flagged 1099_eligible in Vendorvault cannot be included in a payment run until a W-9 is attached to their record. taxprofile blocks the payment and shows the reason as 'TIN_MISSING' in the run preview. Ask the vendor for the form through the supplier portal, not by email, so the attachment lands on the right record.

learnings.title: Manual accruals on the last day double-reverse
learnings.body: The accrue_rev job runs on the first business day of the month and reverses every accrual flagged as auto. If you post a manual accrual on the last day of the period, it will be reversed by the job and also by your own reversing entry. Set manual_accrual=true on the journal header so the job skips it.

learnings.title: Rotated freight PDFs misread totals in OCR
learnings.body: Invoices from the freight vendor with ID VND-4471 often arrive as landscape PDFs with rotated pages, and the ocr-ingest pipeline reads the total from the wrong box. Apply the template override tmpl_freightco_v3 when the header shows 'FRC' in the first line. Always check the extracted total against the PDF before approving.

learnings.title: AP aging dashboard hides credit memos by default
learnings.body: The AP Aging (Lakeshore) dashboard excludes credit memos unless you add include_credits=1 to the URL. Totals without them look higher than what we actually owe, which led to an overpayment question in Q2. Include the parameter any time you're reconciling aging to the GL.

learnings.title: Payment run hold label blocks vendors silently
learnings.body: The pr-hold label in Payhub keeps a vendor out of every payment run until someone removes it. Labels added during a dispute are often forgotten after the dispute closes, which pushes payments late. Run apctl holds list --older-than 30d each Monday and clear any that are stale.

learnings.title: Credit memo auto-apply order differs between prod and sandbox
learnings.body: Under policy LX-7, credit memos should apply to the oldest open invoice first. The autoapply tool does this in production, but the sandbox build applies newest first, which is why test reconciliations look wrong. Verify with a known vendor before trusting any sandbox output for credit application.

learnings.title: FX-denominated invoices use invoice-date rates
learnings.body: Foreign currency vendor invoices are converted using the rate snapshot from FXBoard on the invoice date, not the payment date. Revaluation of open balances happens in the monthly FX job, so an invoice paid after month end will show a gain or loss in the next period. Don't manually override the rate unless treasury approves it in the ticket.

learnings.title: Vendor merges affect 1099 totals based on date
learnings.body: When two vendor records are merged, the surviving record keeps the older vendor ID. The tax-year job sums 1099 payments across both records only if the merge was completed before December 15. Merges after that date need the manual adjustment template TAX-ADJ-2 to avoid under-reporting.

learnings.title: Invoice splitter caps at 12 cost center lines
learnings.body: The splitter UI in Lakeshore Ledger allows up to 12 cost center lines per invoice. For anything over 12, export the allocation template from the Actions menu, fill it in, and attach the CSV to the ticket. ap-platform will load it manually within one business day.

learnings.title: Journal memo needs ref: prefix for reconciliation bot
learnings.body: The recon bot matches reclass journals to their source invoices only when the memo field starts with 'ref:' followed by the invoice ID. Journals without this prefix show up as unmatched in the daily variance report. Copy the invoice ID exactly from Lakeshore, including any dashes.

learnings.title: Supplier portal rejects PDFs over 10 MB
learnings.body: Vendors uploading through the supplier portal get an automatic rejection for any PDF over 10 MB, and the rejection message is unclear. Ask them to split the file or send it to the ap-intake inbox instead. Scanned multi-page invoices from one German vendor hit this limit most often.

learnings.title: ap-intake inbox only processes the first attachment
learnings.body: The ap-intake mailbox parser reads only the first PDF attachment in a message. When a vendor forwards a thread containing several invoices, the others are silently dropped. Scan the whole thread for attachments and forward each invoice separately to ap-intake.

learnings.title: bizcal holiday list lags behind the company calendar
learnings.body: AP due-date calculations use the bizcal service, which reads a holiday list that is updated by hand. In 2023 the list was missing the June observance, so due dates fell one business day early. Check the holiday list each January against the HR calendar and file a ticket to bizcal owners if anything is missing.

learnings.title: Use-tax accrual for out-of-state SaaS vendors
learnings.body: When an out-of-state SaaS vendor doesn't charge sales tax, AP must accrue use tax to account 2210 based on the buyer's location. taxgrid calculates the rate, but it needs the cost center's state code set in Vendorvault. Missing state codes default to zero and understate the accrual.

learnings.title: Retainage release requires a lien waiver first
learnings.body: Construction vendors hold 10% retainage, and releases are entered through the retain-release form. The form rejects the release unless a conditional or unconditional lien waiver is already uploaded to the vendor record, and the waiver date must be on or before the release date. Get the waiver from the project manager before opening the form.

learnings.title: Payment runs need two distinct approvers
learnings.body: Payhub requires two different people to approve each payment run. If the same person approves twice, the second approval is deduplicated silently and the run stays in 'pending approval' with no error. Have the second approver click approve on their own session, and don't try to re-submit.

learnings.title: Early-pay discount calc used received date in v2.1
learnings.body: In discount_calc v2.1, early-pay discounts such as 2/10 net 30 were computed from the date the invoice was received instead of the invoice date. This caused missed discounts on roughly 300 invoices in Q1. The fix shipped in v2.1.4, so check the version in the service header before trusting older discount reports.

learnings.title: Intercompany invoices skip three-way match
learnings.body: Invoices with the ICI prefix come from our own subsidiaries and bypass three-way match entirely. They must carry the ic_settle tag so treasury can net them at month end. Untagged ICI invoices will sit in an exceptions queue that nobody watches, so tag them at entry.

learnings.title: po-janitor closes POs open 180 days on Sunday
learnings.body: The po-janitor job runs Sundays at 03:00 and auto-closes any purchase order that has been open for 180 days with no receipts. Closed POs block new invoices from matching and create a confusing 'PO closed' error. Reopen with apctl po reopen --reason followed by the reason, within 30 days of closure.

learnings.title: Vendors need COI expiry at least 60 days out
learnings.body: During vendor onboarding, Vendorvault checks the certificate of insurance expiry date, and anything under 60 days puts the vendor into on_hold_coi status. Payments to on-hold vendors are blocked until a new certificate is uploaded. Ask vendors for renewed certificates early, before the renewal date approaches.

learnings.title: Corporate card merchants do not belong in AP
learnings.body: Merchants such as CloudMarket and the office supplies portal are paid on corporate cards, and the card feed already creates transactions for them. If you also enter the vendor invoice in AP, the expense shows up twice in the ledger. Check the card feed in Spendlane first and only enter an AP invoice if the card was not used.

learnings.title: Searching invoices by PO needs no space after PO-
learnings.body: In Lakeshore Ledger's search bar, the vendor: prefix filters by vendor name, and PO numbers must be typed without a space after the dash. Searching 'PO 4471' returns nothing, while 'PO-4471' returns the matching invoices. This trips up new hires almost every onboarding cycle.

learnings.title: Vendor name matching fails on punctuation variants
learnings.body: The vmatch tool sometimes fails to link 'Acme Ltd.' and 'ACME LTD' to the same vendor record because punctuation and case are compared differently across sources. Run vmatch --dry-run on the invoice's vendor name before creating a new record to avoid duplicates. If the dry run shows a candidate above 0.9 similarity, use the existing record.

learnings.title: Cairn escalation queue silently drops tickets with more than 40 CC addresses
learnings.body: Cairn's escalation queue rejects any ticket with more than 40 CC'd addresses and does not show an error in the agent UI. The ticket stays in the original queue with no escalation flag, so it looks handled. If a customer reports a CC list that big, strip the extra addresses into an internal note before escalating.

learnings.title: Pigeonhole macro variables don't render in subject lines
learnings.body: Macro placeholders like {{customer.first_name}} work in the body but are left as raw text in the subject field. Hardcode the subject or use the 'Subject template' option, which does support variables. This has bitten a few people during the March macro cleanup.

learnings.title: Rookery SLA clock only pauses on Pending if a reason code is set
learnings.body: Setting a ticket to Pending does not stop the first-response SLA clock unless a Pending reason code is chosen. Rookery defaults to no reason, which means the clock keeps running and breach alerts fire at the manager. Pick one of the reason codes (waiting_customer, waiting_vendor, internal_review) every time.

learnings.title: Lantern sync worker deploy checklist
learnings.body: 1. Drain the worker pool with `lanternctl drain --pool sync` and wait for in-flight count to reach zero. 2. Deploy the new image to staging first and run `lanternctl smoke --env staging`. 3. Only then promote to prod and undrain. Skipping step 1 has caused duplicate ticket creation twice this year.

learnings.title: Tier-2 handoff rule for P1 tickets
learnings.body: House rule: never reassign a P1 ticket to another tier without posting a handoff note in #sev-handoff. The note needs customer impact, current hypothesis, and the next check time. Reassignment without a note will be reverted by the on-call lead.

learnings.title: Quill CSAT survey is suppressed for tickets reopened within 24 hours
learnings.body: If a customer reopens a ticket within 24 hours of closing, Quill will not send a second CSAT survey, and the original score is kept. This is intentional so customers aren't surveyed twice for one issue. Analysts reporting on CSAT response rates should exclude these reopen windows from the denominator.

learnings.title: Hearth portal attachments over 15 MB are truncated without warning
learnings.body: Customers uploading files to Hearth above 15 MB get a success message, but the stored file is cut off at 15 MB. Agents often find corrupted zip files later. Tell customers to share large files via the external transfer link in the help center article instead.

learnings.title: Marlin chat exports cap at 5,000 messages
learnings.body: Exporting a chat transcript from Marlin returns at most the most recent 5,000 messages. Longer conversations are silently truncated at the start. For legal or QA requests, use `marlin export --chat <id> --full`, which pages through the full history and takes a few minutes.

learnings.title: Beacon status updates: post the draft before publishing
learnings.body: Beacon incident updates should be written as drafts first and reviewed in the #status-review thread. Publishing directly sends the update to subscribers immediately and cannot be recalled. Once the draft is approved, use the Publish button rather than editing a live incident.

learnings.title: Auto-tagger misreads 'refund' in shipping complaints
learnings.body: The auto-tagger in the triage pipeline applies the billing/refund tag whenever the word 'refund' appears, even in shipping complaints like 'still waiting for my refund shipment'. Around 18% of tickets in that tag in Q2 were wrong. Until the classifier is retrained, check the first sentence of the ticket before routing to the refunds queue.

learnings.title: Tessel KB search ignores stopwords but needs quotes for phrases
learnings.body: Tessel's knowledge base search drops common words, so searching 'can I change my plan' matches almost everything. For exact phrases wrap the query in double quotes. Agents on the new hire training track kept missing the 'Plan change' article until we added this note to onboarding.

learnings.title: Agent seat reclaim runs Sundays for the EU tenant
learnings.body: Unused agent seats in the EU helpdesk tenant are reclaimed every Sunday at 02:00 local time. An agent who has not logged in for 45 days loses their seat, and their assigned tickets go back to the unassigned pool. Ask the team lead to request a seat exemption in #helpdesk-admin before any extended leave.

learnings.title: Reseller inbox tickets are missing requester ID
learnings.body: Tickets arriving through the reseller inbox come in with a blank requester_id field. Use the reseller_ref value in the custom fields to look up the end customer in the CRM. Merging these tickets with the wrong account has happened, so verify the email domain before merging.

learnings.title: Macro preview shows stale content until hard refresh
learnings.body: The macro preview pane in Pigeonhole caches the last rendered version for the session. If you edit a macro and the preview doesn't change, press Shift+R to force a reload. Saving the macro does not invalidate the preview cache in older browser builds.

learnings.title: Weekly QA sampling command
learnings.body: QA sampling pulls a random 3% of tickets closed in the previous week. Run `sampler pull --rate 0.03 --since 7d --queue all` from the qa-tools box, and the output lands in the shared QA sheet. Reviewers should score each sample within five business days so the weekly report stays on schedule.

learnings.title: Password reset canned response must not include the link in plain text
learnings.body: The approved password reset macro uses the secure reset button, which generates a one-time link. Do not paste the raw reset URL into the ticket body, because it is visible to anyone with access to the ticket history. If a customer can't use the button, send them to the self-service form instead.

learnings.title: Bulk merge tool merges tickets in reverse ID order
learnings.body: The bulk merge action in the Cairn admin console merges the selected tickets into the one with the highest ID, not the oldest, which surprises people. The surviving ticket also loses its original created date. Check the target ticket before running the merge, and note that undo is only available for 10 minutes.

learnings.title: IVR transfer to billing-v2 falls back to voicemail when no agents are online
learnings.body: When the billing-v2 phone queue has zero agents online, IVR transfers do not play a message; the call drops into the voicemail bridge after about 20 seconds. This is expected behavior, not an outage. Check the queue's presence board before reporting a phone issue to telephony.

learnings.title: Pigeonhole routing rules: first match wins
learnings.body: Pigeonhole routing rules are evaluated top to bottom, and the first matching rule stops evaluation. Rules further down that also match are never applied, which makes the rule list easy to break. When adding a rule, drag it above the catch-all and test it using the rule simulator.

learnings.title: Show timestamps in the customer's timezone
learnings.body: House rule: any timestamp shown to a customer in an email or the portal must be in the timezone saved on their profile, not the agent's local time. Agents in the Lisbon office kept quoting times in their own zone, which confused customers during outage follow-ups. The helper `fmt_customer_time(ticket)` in the support SDK does this for you.

learnings.title: Nightly CSAT warehouse export lags six hours
learnings.body: The nightly job that copies CSAT responses from Quill into the analytics warehouse runs with a six-hour lag, so the dashboard for the previous day is incomplete until around 09:00. Do not file a data quality ticket for missing responses before that time. If you need same-day numbers, use the live Quill report instead.

learnings.title: Impersonating a customer in Hearth requires an open ticket and a reason
learnings.body: To view the portal as a customer, use the impersonate button in Hearth, but only from an open ticket with the customer's ID attached. You must enter a reason code, and every session is logged to the audit feed that the security team reviews weekly. Impersonation is read-only and cannot change billing details.

learnings.title: Lantern duplicate detection threshold is 0.82
learnings.body: Lantern flags a new ticket as a possible duplicate when subject and body similarity is at least 0.82. Lowering the threshold below 0.8 creates many false positives on templated billing emails. If you see a duplicate that was missed, report the pair of ticket IDs in #lantern-tuning rather than adjusting the setting locally.

learnings.title: Queue skill tags are case sensitive
learnings.body: Routing skill tags in Pigeonhole are case sensitive, so a ticket tagged 'Billing' will not match agents with the skill 'billing'. The skill directory has both forms because of an old import. Use the lowercase form listed in the skills catalog, and ask the admin team if you need a new skill added.

learnings.title: Legacy plan customers don't see the Downgrade button
learnings.body: Customers on the legacy Starter plan do not see the Downgrade button in the self-service portal, so they open tickets asking how to downgrade. The verified answer is to route these tickets to the retention queue with the tag legacy_downgrade. The retention team will process the change manually within one business day.

learnings.title: Pseudolocale xx-PS catches hardcoded strings fast
learnings.body: Run `kodo pseudo --locale xx-PS` in the web build before opening a localization PR. Pseudo strings are wrapped in brackets and padded about 30% longer, so any English text still visible in that locale is hardcoded and needs a key. This takes about two minutes and catches most misses before translators see them.

learnings.title: Arabic plurals need all six ICU categories
learnings.body: Arabic requires zero, one, two, few, many, and other, and Tessera will flag any ICU plural block that omits one. Don't copy the English block and fill in only one and other. Use `=0` for an explicit zero message when the UI needs different wording for empty states.

learnings.title: Never concatenate translated fragments in the UI
learnings.body: House rule: every user-visible sentence goes through a single key with named placeholders, such as `{count} files selected`. Word order differs across languages, so `'You have ' + n + ' items'` will break Japanese and German. The `strfmt-lint` pre-commit hook rejects string concatenation inside `t()` calls.

learnings.title: Bundle publish needs a CDN purge or stale strings linger
learnings.body: After merging translation bundles, run `bundlectl publish --env staging` and then `cdnctl purge --prefix i18n/` before testing. The CDN caches locale JSON for 6 hours, so skipping the purge makes new strings look missing even though the publish succeeded. Production publishes follow the same two steps, with `--env prod`.

learnings.title: Glossa exports silently drop keys with embedded newlines
learnings.body: If a source string contains a literal line break, Glossa's CSV export omits the row and reports success. Use the newline escape sequence in the source string instead of a real line break. The `glossa-verify` step in CI compares key counts between source and export and fails when they differ.

learnings.title: Japanese locale only uses the other plural form
learnings.body: Japanese has no grammatical plural, so every plural key should contain only `other`. Adding `one` is harmless but translators are asked to leave it blank, and Tessera marks those cells as incomplete. Don't add extra forms there just to satisfy the linter.

learnings.title: iOS fallback goes to en-GB instead of en-US
learnings.body: The iOS bundle loader reads `fallbackChain.json`, which lists en-GB before en-US for any English variant. Users with an en-US device language who are missing a key will see British spelling. Change the chain in that file and rebuild, because the runtime does not read the setting from remote config.

learnings.title: Translation memory auto-accepts German matches at 0.85
learnings.body: The translation memory sync auto-accepts fuzzy matches at 0.85 or above, but only for German. Every other locale defaults to 0.95 because translators found the lower threshold produced awkward phrasing in French and Polish. Override per locale with `tm-sync --locale de --min-score 0.85`.

learnings.title: Customer names are stored raw and never transliterated
learnings.body: Support tooling must display customer names exactly as entered, including non-Latin scripts and diacritics. Do not run them through the transliteration helper, which was added for search only and produces unrecognizable output for Thai and Korean. If a search index needs ASCII, use the `name_search` field, which the ingest job fills.

learnings.title: Hebrew and Arabic need logical CSS properties
learnings.body: Physical properties like margin-left and text-align: left break layouts in RTL locales. Use margin-inline-start and text-align: start instead. The `no-physical-direction` ESLint rule flags violations in the design system, and the sidebar bug from March came from one missed margin-left in the nav component.

learnings.title: Snapshotter needs ctx tags for translator screenshots
learnings.body: Translators get screenshots from Snapshotter, but it only captures keys tagged with a `ctx:` value in the key metadata. Untagged keys show a blank frame in Tessera, which causes most of the ambiguous 'Save' translation questions. Tag every button and menu key with the screen it appears on, such as `ctx:settings-dialog`.

learnings.title: German button labels can grow to 1.4x English width
learnings.body: German labels in narrow buttons often exceed the English width by about 40%, which truncates the checkout 'Continue' button. Set `maxLength` in the key metadata for any label that lives in a fixed-width control. The layout check in Snapshotter fails the build when a German string overflows its container.

learnings.title: Glossary says Workspace translates but Board stays English
learnings.body: In the French glossary, 'Workspace' translates to 'Espace de travail' everywhere, but 'Board' stays as 'Board' because it is a product noun. Translators have repeatedly changed it to 'Tableau' and that breaks consistency with the marketing site. Glossary changes need approval from the product copy owner in the Glossa review queue.

learnings.title: Language resolver ignores all but the first Accept-Language tag
learnings.body: The lang-resolver service only reads the first tag in the Accept-Language header, so a request sending 'fr-CA,en;q=0.8' resolves to fr-CA even when that bundle is incomplete. The resolver does not fall back down the list. If a region bundle is partial, set the `lang_override` cookie for the affected users rather than relying on the header.

learnings.title: String freeze is 48 hours before each release branch cut
learnings.body: The i18n team freezes source strings 48 hours before the release branch is cut, enforced by `freeze --branch release/next`. After the freeze, new keys need an exception ticket with the translation deadline included. Translators can't finish late additions in time, so the freeze exists to protect launch quality in every locale.

learnings.title: French needs a non-breaking space before colons and guillemets
learnings.body: French typography requires a non-breaking space (U+00A0) before colons, semicolons, question marks, and inside guillemets. Regular spaces get wrapped onto their own line in narrow labels. The `fr-typo` lint rule converts the spaces automatically during import, so translators don't have to type the special character.

learnings.title: Machine translation is blocked for legal strings
learnings.body: Lingo-MT must never be used on legal text such as terms of service, privacy notices, or refund policy. Mark those keys with `legal: true` in the metadata, and the import job will refuse MT suggestions for them. Legal review is required for every locale before the copy ships.

learnings.title: Use pt-BR with a hyphen, not pt_br
learnings.body: Locale codes in URLs and bundle filenames must use a hyphen, such as pt-BR. An underscore version caused 404s in Safari because the router normalizes only hyphenated tags. The `locale-check` script in CI rejects any underscore in a code it finds in a route or manifest.

learnings.title: Android 'und' locale events come from pre-2.4 clients
learnings.body: In the events table, rows with locale 'und' come from Android clients older than 2.4, which did not send a locale value. Filter them out with `WHERE locale != 'und'` before reporting per-language adoption. The count is usually 3 to 4 percent of traffic, so it can distort small-market dashboards.

learnings.title: Missing-key alert fires above 50 per hour
learnings.body: The Grafana panel 'i18n missing keys' tracks lookups that fall back to the source language. The alert pages the on-call i18n rotation when the count exceeds 50 per hour for any single locale. Most spikes come from a new key that shipped before its translations, so check the release tag first.

learnings.title: zh-TW needs its own glossary entry for software
learnings.body: Taiwanese Chinese uses 軟體 for software, while the mainland term 軟件 reads as wrong to users in Taiwan. The zh-TW glossary carries that distinction, but translators working from zh-CN sometimes copy the wrong form. Always translate zh-TW from the zh-TW glossary, not from a shared Chinese glossary.

learnings.title: Rename keys with rename-key to keep translations
learnings.body: Renaming a key by editing it directly in the source file orphans every translation, and the translators then have to redo the work. Use `rename-key old.key new.key` instead, which moves the translations across all locales in one commit. Keys follow the pattern feature.area.element, so keep that shape when renaming.

learnings.title: Polish plural tests need 1, 5, and 22
learnings.body: Polish plurals split on a few cases: 1 is one, 2 to 4 are few, and 5 to 21 are many, with 22 to 24 back to few. When testing a count string, check 1, 5, and 22 at minimum, because 22 is the case that breaks naive implementations. The `plural-matrix` test helper runs all three automatically.

learnings.title: Export to XLIFF 1.2, not 2.0, for the vendor portal
learnings.body: The external vendor portal only accepts XLIFF 1.2 files, and 2.0 imports fail with a generic 'invalid document' error. Pass `--format xliff12` to the export command. The portal has been on this version since the vendor migration in 2022 and there is no open request to upgrade.

learnings.title: Don't override Swiss German number separators
learnings.body: Intl.NumberFormat with the de-CH locale uses an apostrophe as the thousands separator, which surprises people but matches Swiss convention. Earlier code overrode it with a period to match German, and the Zurich customers filed several complaints. Keep the platform formatter and don't special-case the separator.

learnings.title: Finnish compounds need break-word on narrow labels
learnings.body: Finnish produces very long compound words that overflow narrow table headers and sidebars. Apply `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to those containers, since normal word wrapping does nothing when the word has no spaces. The admin console had three overflow bugs in the Q3 audit, all fixed by that one rule.

learnings.title: Hotfix a production typo without a redeploy
learnings.body: For a typo in a production translation, run `i18nctl hotfix --key checkout.pay.label --locale es-ES --value 'Pagar ahora'`, which updates the bundle without a code deploy. Then bump the bundle version with `i18nctl version bump` so clients refetch. Record the hotfix in the i18n changelog, because the next full sync overwrites it unless the translation memory is also updated.

learnings.title: Lintel a11y rules block merges on missing alt text
learnings.body: The Lintel config in the monorepo root now includes the a11y preset, and it fails the build on img elements without an alt attribute. Decorative images should use alt="" instead of omitting the attribute, since omitting it still fails. Override per file with a lintel-disable comment only if a design-systems reviewer approves it in the PR.

learnings.title: Disabled button contrast token is exempt from the 4.5:1 check
learnings.body: The color-text-disabled token sits at about 2.8:1 on surface-2 and fails WCAG AA, but WCAG exempts inactive UI components. The contrast checker in Palette Lab flags it anyway, so add it to the allowlist file contrast-exemptions.json with a link to the design ticket. Do not use it for placeholder text, which does need to pass.

learnings.title: axe nightly job silently skips iframes
learnings.body: The axe-runner nightly job in CI does not descend into iframes unless frameSelector is passed in the run config. The embedded billing widget is an iframe, so its violations never appear on the dashboard. We added frameSelector: 'iframe[data-a11y-scan]' to the nightly config on 14 March, and the widget now shows up in reports.

learnings.title: VoiceOver rotor skips custom tab bar items
learnings.body: On iOS, the custom TabBarLite component does not expose its items to the VoiceOver rotor because the container lacks the tab trait. Set accessibilityTraits to include .tabBar on the container and .button on each item, then verify with the rotor set to Headings and Containers. Reported by Priya in mobile QA on build 4.12.0.

learnings.title: TalkBack reads Pressable buttons twice
learnings.body: When a Pressable wraps a Text child and also has accessibilityRole="button", TalkBack announces 'Log in, button, Log in, button'. The fix is to set accessible={true} on the Pressable and remove the redundant accessibilityLabel from the inner Text. Check with TalkBack on a Pixel emulator before merging, since the iOS behavior does not show this.

learnings.title: Modal focus trap must return focus to the trigger
learnings.body: The Modal component in the design system traps focus while open, but it does not restore focus on close unless returnFocusRef is passed. Several flows in the settings area dropped focus to the top of the document as a result. Pass a ref to the element that opened the modal, and treat a missing returnFocusRef as a lint warning in new code.

learnings.title: Captions for product demo videos via vtt-forge
learnings.body: Run vtt-forge transcribe --source demo.mp4 --lang en to produce a draft WebVTT file, then review it by hand because the tool mishandles product names like 'Quillbox' and 'Tallyhand'. Upload the reviewed .vtt next to the video in the CMS under the captions field. Videos without captions are blocked from the help center publish step.

learnings.title: Reduced motion is controlled by motionSafe in theme config
learnings.body: Animations should check the motionSafe flag exposed in theme.config.ts rather than calling matchMedia directly, because the flag also honors the in-app 'Reduce motion' toggle. The toggle writes to the user preference store under prefs.motion. If you add a new keyframe animation, wrap it in the motionSafe helper so it degrades to a 100ms fade.

learnings.title: Macro for screen reader users requesting alternate invoice format
learnings.body: Support agents get this question often: customers using JAWS ask for an invoice they can read in plain text rather than the PDF. The macro 'SR-Invoice-Alt' generates a text export through the billing portal's text export endpoint and attaches it to the ticket. It takes about 2 minutes, and the ticket should be tagged accessibility-request so we can count volume each quarter.

learnings.title: CSV exports lose header associations for screen readers
learnings.body: When analytics exports a report to accessible PDF through the pdf-bridge service, the table loses its th scope attributes unless the column header row is marked with the header flag in the source schema. Set header: true on the top row of the report definition YAML before exporting. We found this while preparing the Q1 board pack for a visually impaired board member.

learnings.title: Keyboard shortcuts in reports grid collide with NVDA
learnings.body: The reports grid binds J and K for row navigation, which clash with NVDA browse mode keys on Windows. Users in browse mode see the grid respond unexpectedly. We now only enable the shortcuts after the grid receives focus and an explicit Enter press, which the grid-shortcuts hook handles.

learnings.title: Heading audit counts hidden sections as present
learnings.body: The page-audit heading check reports a valid h1 to h2 sequence even when the h2 is inside a display:none panel, which screen readers do not announce. This produced false passes on the account settings page for two sprints. Use the --visible-only flag in page-audit, which is not the default, when running it on pages with collapsible content.

learnings.title: Accessible name for icon buttons comes from label, not title
learnings.body: Our IconButton component maps the title prop to a tooltip but does not reliably set the accessible name in every browser, so use the label prop instead. The label is rendered as visually hidden text and wired to aria-label. Code review should reject icon-only buttons that rely on title alone.

learnings.title: Status pills need an icon as well as color
learnings.body: Status pills in the orders table originally used only green, amber, and red to show state, which fails for users with color vision deficiency. The statusPill component now requires an icon from iconkit, such as check, alert, or x, alongside the color. Designers should not specify a color-only state in Figma, and the Palette Lab token check will fail if one is missing.

learnings.title: House rule: checkout PRs need an accessibility sign-off
learnings.body: Any pull request that changes files under apps/checkout/ requires a sign-off from someone on the a11y guild, applied as the a11y-approved label. The guild meets Tuesdays at 10:00 and reviews async through the #a11y-review channel. Merges without the label are blocked by the checkout-gate workflow.

learnings.title: Dashboard sticky header overlaps content at 400% zoom
learnings.body: At 400% browser zoom, the sticky header on the analytics dashboard covers about a third of the viewport, so focused elements can be hidden behind it. WCAG reflow requires content to remain usable at 320 CSS pixels wide. Add scroll-padding-top equal to the header height on the html element, which is set in global.css as --header-h.

learnings.title: Pa11y CI thresholds: fail at 3 serious issues
learnings.body: The pa11y-ci step in the release pipeline fails the build when a page has three or more issues with impact 'serious' and warns below that. Thresholds live in .pa11yci.json under the thresholds key. If a release is blocked by an accessibility regression, the on-call engineer can add a waiver through the release-waivers form, which expires after seven days.

learnings.title: Voice control testing: command names for Dragon and Voice Access
learnings.body: When testing voice control, the most reliable commands are 'click [label]' on Windows Dragon and 'tap [label]' on Android Voice Access. Give every interactive element a unique visible label, because duplicates produce a numbered overlay that confuses testers. Log results in the voice-control sheet under the Checkout tab.

learnings.title: Date picker announces changes after 250ms delay
learnings.body: The DatePicker updates an aria-live region when the selected date changes, but the announcement is debounced by 250ms to avoid double-speaking during fast keyboard navigation. If you need to change this, edit LIVE_DEBOUNCE_MS in datepicker/constants.ts. Lower values caused NVDA to drop announcements in our tests.

learnings.title: Form error summary must link to the first invalid field
learnings.body: The error summary at the top of forms should include a link for each error that jumps to the field's id, and the first link should receive focus on submit. Use the ErrorSummary component with the fields prop, which generates anchors to #field-id automatically. Hand-built summaries have repeatedly linked to nonexistent ids.

learnings.title: Skip link must not use display:none
learnings.body: The skip-to-content link in the app shell was hidden with display:none, which made it unreachable by keyboard. Use the visually-hidden utility class, then show it on :focus-visible so it appears when tabbed to. Verify it with a single Tab press on a fresh page load.

learnings.title: Chartnote generates alt text summaries for charts
learnings.body: Analysts can run chartnote describe --chart-id <id> in the BI workspace to draft alt text for a chart, which is written to the chart's description field. The output tends to list every data point, so trim it to the trend and the top two values. Charts shared externally need the reviewed description before the export is approved.

learnings.title: Android font scale testing at 200%
learnings.body: Users who increase system font size to 200% on Android hit clipping in the order summary card, which uses fixed-height containers. Test by setting fontScale to 2.0 in the emulator's display settings, not just the in-app slider. Switch fixed heights to minHeight, and confirm the card still fits inside the 360dp test device width.

learnings.title: Spanish bundle is missing aria-label translations
learnings.body: The es-MX locale file lacks translations for about 40 aria-label keys, so screen readers fall back to English labels such as 'Close' in an otherwise Spanish page. Missing keys are tracked under the a11y.* namespace in the translation tool, and the fallback warning appears in the dev console as i18n-missing. Assign translations to the localization team with the a11y-label tag.

learnings.title: VPAT refresh owner and cadence
learnings.body: The Voluntary Product Accessibility Template is refreshed every six months, and the owner is the compliance lead listed in the compliance wiki under Accessibility Program. Engineering provides the test evidence by exporting the latest axe and manual audit results to the evidence folder by the 1st of the month. Customers requesting a current VPAT should be sent the copy dated within the last twelve months.

learnings.title: Never write to concrete product indices; always go through the products_read alias
learnings.body: Application code must target the `products_read` and `products_write` aliases, never `products-000017` directly, because the alias swap is how `catalog-reindex` cuts over. Writing to a concrete index during a reindex means the documents get lost when the old index is deleted. The search-api lint job flags direct index names in PRs.

learnings.title: Set refresh_interval to -1 before bulk loads and restore it after
learnings.body: During the nightly `vendor-feed-loader` run, set `index.refresh_interval` to `-1` on the target index, then put it back to `1s` when the load finishes. We forgot the restore step once and search results lagged by about 40 minutes until someone noticed. The loader now sets it in a `finally` block so it resets even on failure.

learnings.title: Production templates use dynamic: strict, so unknown fields will be rejected
learnings.body: The `strict-default-v3` index template sets `dynamic: strict` on every index in prod. If a producer sends a new field, you get a 400 `strict_dynamic_mapping_exception` rather than a silently created mapping. To add a field, open a PR against `es-mappings` and bump the template version; do not PUT mapping changes by hand.

learnings.title: Target 20 to 40 GB per primary shard; logs-hot-30d ILM policy rolls over at 50 GB
learnings.body: Shard sizing guidance from the platform review: keep primaries between 20 and 40 GB, because smaller shards waste heap on overhead and larger ones make recovery slow. The `logs-hot-30d` ILM policy rolls over at 50 GB or 1 day, whichever comes first. If you need a custom shard count, set it in the template, not per index.

learnings.title: Deep pagination: from+size past 10000 fails, use search_after with a PIT
learnings.body: The `search-api-gateway` caps `from + size` at 10000 and returns an error beyond that. For exports and infinite scroll, open a point-in-time with `POST /<index>/_pit?keep_alive=2m` and page with `search_after` sorted on `_shard_doc` plus a unique tiebreaker. Scroll is deprecated here and the old `legacy-scroll` helper is scheduled for removal.

learnings.title: Sort and aggregate on the .raw keyword subfield, not the analyzed text field
learnings.body: Our product mappings declare `name` as text with a `keyword` subfield called `name.raw` (normalizer `lower_trim`). Sorting or aggregating on `name` throws an illegal_argument_exception about fielddata being disabled. Use `name.raw` in aggs and sorts, and remember it is capped at 256 characters.

learnings.title: Nightly snapshots to s3-snap-prod at 02:15 UTC; monthly restore drill is mandatory
learnings.body: The `snapshot-scheduler` job writes a snapshot to the `s3-snap-prod` repository at 02:15 UTC every night and retains 30 days. The first Monday of each month, someone runs the restore drill against the staging cluster and logs the result in the ops wiki. A snapshot that has never been restored is not a backup, as the 2023 audit made clear.

learnings.title: Rolling restarts: set delayed_timeout to 5m first or every node bounce triggers shard shuffling
learnings.body: Before restarting a data node, run `PUT _all/_settings {"index.unassigned.node_left.delayed_timeout":"5m"}` so the cluster waits for the node to come back instead of rebuilding replicas. Restart one node at a time and wait for green. Reset the setting to `1m` when the rolling restart is done, following the steps in `rolling-restart.md`.

learnings.title: parent circuit breaker trips at 70 percent: check _nodes/stats/breaker before raising limits
learnings.body: When you see `CircuitBreakingException` on the parent breaker, the first move is `GET _nodes/stats/breaker` to see which child breaker is driving usage. Raising `indices.breaker.total.limit` only masks the problem, and we have hit it twice from unbounded fielddata on a `tags` text field. Fix the query or mapping, then reconsider the limit.

learnings.title: Painless scoring scripts live in scoring-scripts repo and ship with es-scripts push
learnings.body: Stored Painless scripts are versioned in the `scoring-scripts` repo and deployed with `es-scripts push --env staging` followed by the same command with `--env prod`. Name stored scripts with the prefix `ranker_v2_` so the dashboard can list them. Do not edit a stored script in place; push a new version and update the query reference.

learnings.title: Synonym changes need _reload_search_analyzers on every node, or results are inconsistent
learnings.body: Synonym files are attached only to `search_analyzer`, so editing `synonyms/product_terms.txt` does nothing until the analyzers are reloaded. Run `synsync push` which calls `POST /products_read/_reload_search_analyzers` on each node. Reloading on only one coordinating node caused a week of mismatched results in the spring.

learnings.title: SKU search ngram analyzer: min_gram 3 and max_gram 6 only, anything wider blows up the index
learnings.body: The `sku_ngram` analyzer uses an edge_ngram tokenizer with min_gram 3 and max_gram 6 on the `sku` field. Widening max_gram to 10 roughly tripled the index size for the catalog and slowed indexing by a factor of two in our benchmark. If partial-match needs go beyond 6 characters, use a separate prefix query instead.

learnings.title: Rollover alias for events uses date-math names: events-{now/d} with max_size 50gb
learnings.body: Event indices are created as `events-{now/d}` through the `events-writer` alias so that a daily rollover is automatic. The rollover condition is max_size of 50gb, and the `events-retention` job deletes anything older than 90 days. To inspect current rollover status, use `GET _cat/aliases/events-writer?v`.

learnings.title: Batch bulk requests at 5 to 15 MB; ingest-shipper uses 500 docs per batch
learnings.body: The `ingest-shipper` service sends bulk requests of 500 documents, which keeps payloads within the 5 to 15 MB sweet spot for our document sizes. If you see `es_rejected_execution_exception` it means the write thread pool queue (default 200) is full, so back off and retry with jitter. Do not raise the queue size on prod nodes without talking to SRE.

learnings.title: pii-scrub-v2 ingest pipeline removes email and phone fields; test with _simulate first
learnings.body: Every log index runs the `pii-scrub-v2` ingest pipeline, which removes `user.email` and `user.phone` before storage. Before changing it, test with `POST _ingest/pipeline/pii-scrub-v2/_simulate` using a sample from the `pii-fixtures` folder. A regression in this pipeline shipped to prod once and required a manual reindex to clean up.

learnings.title: Use composite aggregation for more than 10000 buckets; terms agg silently truncates
learnings.body: The `terms` aggregation on `order_id` returns only the top buckets with no error, which gave the ops dashboard wrong totals for a month. Switch to a `composite` aggregation with `after_key` paging whenever the expected cardinality exceeds 10000. The `kibana-lens-kit` templates already use composite by default for customer-level views.

learnings.title: ILM stuck in ERROR after a mapping conflict: fix the mapping, then POST _ilm/retry
learnings.body: When an index shows `step: ERROR` in `_ilm/explain`, the usual cause is a mapping conflict during rollover. Correct the field type in the template, then run `POST <index>/_ilm/retry`. Do not delete the index to clear the error, because the rollover alias will point at nothing and writers will fail.

learnings.title: Mapping explosion incident: total_fields limit is 2000, use flattened for attribute bags
learnings.body: A vendor started sending product attributes as arbitrary keys, and the mapping grew past 2000 fields, after which every write failed with `illegal_argument_exception`. The `attributes` object is now mapped as `flattened`, and the `index.mapping.total_fields.limit` stays at 2000. If you need per-key filtering, use the `attr_kv` pattern documented in the search wiki.

learnings.title: Reindex with requests_per_second=800 and slices=auto; watch progress with reindex-watch
learnings.body: For large reindexes, start `_reindex` with `requests_per_second=800` and `slices=auto` so it does not starve live search traffic. The task id is printed by `catalog-reindex`, and `reindex-watch <task_id>` shows throughput and estimated time remaining. Above 1000 requests per second we saw p99 search latency jump past our 300 ms SLO.

learnings.title: Cross-cluster search: query search-east alias and set ccs_minimize_roundtrips to false for small result sets
learnings.body: Queries from the analytics notebooks go through the `search-east` remote alias, which spans the us-east and eu-west clusters. For queries returning under 1000 hits, set `ccs_minimize_roundtrips` to false to cut tail latency. Remote cluster credentials rotate every 90 days through `vault-sync`, so a sudden authorization failure usually means a rotation was missed.

learnings.title: Integration tests must use refresh=wait_for or they flake; use esfixtures.seed() helper
learnings.body: Newly indexed documents are not searchable until a refresh, so tests that index then immediately search fail intermittently. Use `esfixtures.seed()`, which indexes with `refresh=wait_for` automatically, rather than raw client calls. Adding `refresh=true` to every call works too but slows the CI suite noticeably.

learnings.title: Put exact-match and range clauses in filter context, not must, to keep them cacheable
learnings.body: Our product-search code reviewers reject queries that put status or category checks inside `must`, because filter context skips scoring and is eligible for the node query cache. Move these clauses into `bool.filter`. Scoring-only clauses such as the title match stay in `must`.

learnings.title: Heap rule: -Xms and -Xmx both 30g via es-node-profile, never above 31g
learnings.body: JVM heap on data nodes is set to 30g for both min and max, generated by the `es-node-profile` tool on the 64 GB instance class. Going above 31 GB disables compressed object pointers and actually reduces usable memory, which we confirmed with a heap dump comparison. The remaining RAM is left for the filesystem cache, which Lucene relies on heavily.

learnings.title: Find the biggest indices quickly with _cat/indices sorted by store.size
learnings.body: To see which indices are eating disk, run `GET _cat/indices?v&s=store.size:desc&h=index,pri,rep,docs.count,store.size`. For unassigned shards, follow up with `GET _cluster/allocation/explain` which names the specific decider blocking allocation.
