Paste the output into the #search-oncall thread so the next person does not have to rerun it.

learnings.title: Dense vectors are fixed at 384 dims from mini-embed-v2; dims cannot change after index creation
learnings.body: The `product_embedding` field is a `dense_vector` with 384 dimensions, matching the output of the `mini-embed-v2` model served by `embed-gateway`. Elasticsearch does not let you change dimensions on an existing field, so a model upgrade requires a new index and a reindex. Use `num_candidates` of at least 100 for kNN queries, or recall drops noticeably.

learnings.title: Never run delete_by_query with conflicts=proceed on the orders index
learnings.body: Ops once ran `_delete_by_query` with `conflicts=proceed` against `orders-*` to purge test accounts, and it removed documents that were being updated concurrently, causing a support escalation. The current rule is to use `_delete_by_query` only with a PIT-based dry run first, and the `purge-tool` wrapper enforces that. Any one-off deletion must be approved in the data-change channel.

learnings.title: Purge by surrogate key, not by URL, for catalog pages
learnings.body: The catalog service tags responses with Surrogate-Key headers like sku:<id> and cat:<slug>. After a price change, run `edgectl purge --key sku:48213` because URL purges miss the category listing pages that embed the SKU.

learnings.title: Accept-Language was exploding the homepage cache into 400+ variants
learnings.body: The edge was varying on the raw Accept-Language header, which produced over 400 cache variants for the homepage. We now normalize it to the primary two-letter tag inside the edge function before the cache key is computed. Hit ratio went from 61% to 93% over the last sprint.

learnings.title: Staging CDN purges do not touch prod
learnings.body: The stg-west zone has no shared control plane with prod. Running `edgectl purge --zone stg-west` has no effect on production. QA was bitten twice by assuming a fix was live when it was only purged in staging.

learnings.title: House rule: marketing HTML caching limits
learnings.body: Marketing site HTML gets max-age=60 with stale-while-revalidate=600 by default. Anything longer needs sign-off in #edge-policy. A pricing banner stuck for an hour in March after someone set max-age=3600 without asking.

learnings.title: Set-Cookie leaking through the locale route
learnings.body: The edge marks any response with Set-Cookie as private, but the legacy /api/locale route adds the cookie in a middleware that runs after our header policy. That meant anonymous users got cached responses with someone else's locale cookie. The fix was the origin-shield rule strip-cookie-locale, which removes Set-Cookie before the cache write.

learnings.title: Canary the image resizer before promoting
learnings.body: Before promoting image resizer changes, run `imgsvc canary --percent 5 --soak 20m`. The cache key includes the w= and q= parameters, so a bad default for either creates a wave of misses across every PoP. Watch the miss ratio during the soak, not just error rate.

learnings.title: cachelens undercounts HEAD hits
learnings.body: cachelens reports HEAD requests as misses even when they are served from cache, because the collector only counts GET in the hit numerator. Uptime monitors send mostly HEAD, so the dashboard looks worse than it is. Check the cache_status field in raw edge logs when you need the real number.

learnings.title: Origin shield collapse window numbers from the 14 Nov sale
learnings.body: Request collapsing at the origin shield uses a 1500 ms window. During the 14 Nov flash sale we saw about 2,300 concurrent misses on /api/inventory collapse into 41 origin hits. Endpoints with a TTL under 2 seconds don't benefit much from collapsing, so don't bother enabling it for them.

learnings.title: Do not add Vary: Cookie to the dashboard
learnings.body: Someone asked whether the dashboard needs Vary: Cookie to stay correct for logged-in users. The answer is no: the edge ignores Vary on cookies and uses the cache-key template instead. Adding Vary: Cookie just turns off caching for logged-in users with no correctness gain.

learnings.title: Purge returns 403 scope mismatch
learnings.body: If `edgectl purge` returns 403 with 'scope mismatch', the CI token was probably minted with cdn:read only. Request cdn:purge through vaultctl in #infra-access. The purge scope is separate from the deploy scope, so an existing deploy token won't cover it.

learnings.title: Strip tracking params from cache keys
learnings.body: utm_* and fbclid params should be ignored in the cache key. The config is in keys/default.yaml under ignore_query. Adding gclid to that list last quarter cut origin requests to /products by roughly 18%.

learnings.title: Weak ETags from gzip are breaking 304s
learnings.body: After the gzip middleware was added, origin started emitting weak ETags with a W/ prefix. The edge then failed to match clients' If-None-Match values, which turned revalidations into full 200 responses. The fix computes the strong ETag before compression, and test_etag_stable guards against regressions.

learnings.title: Fingerprinted assets must never change content
learnings.body: Hashed bundle filenames under /static/ are served with immutable and max-age=31536000. Never reuse a filename for different content. The build step `build-manifest --check` fails the pipeline if it detects a content change under an existing hash.

learnings.title: edgectl purge rate limit and the silent CLI retry
learnings.body: edgectl purge is limited to 20 requests per minute per zone. For bulk work, use `--batch-file` with up to 500 keys in a single call. Past the limit the API returns a rate-limit error and the CLI retries silently for about 3 minutes, which looks like a hang.

learnings.title: Sydney cold starts hit origin directly
learnings.body: Regional tiering: iad and fra are parents for the US and EU edges. syd has no parent tier, so after a full purge its cold starts go straight to origin. Expect 3 to 4 times normal origin load in Sydney and schedule full purges with that in mind.

learnings.title: Negative caching of 5xx responses
learnings.body: The edge caches origin 5xx responses for 10 seconds through error_ttl. This is intentional but means a 502 blip lasts 10 seconds on every PoP. During deploy windows, run `edgectl policy set --error-ttl 0` and reset it afterward.

learnings.title: Support triage for stale prices
learnings.body: When a customer reports a stale price, open the support console's Inspect tab and read the X-Cache-Age header. If the age is over 300, ask engineering to purge key price:<sku>. Do not request a full zone purge for a single SKU, as it causes origin load spikes.

learnings.title: Experiment bucket cookie must stay out of the landing page cache key
learnings.body: The ab_bucket cookie must not be part of the landing page cache key. Variants are routed with an edge rewrite from /lp/* to /lp-v2/* instead. In October a variant leaked into the cache for 14 minutes and showed the wrong copy to everyone.

learnings.title: Edge log schema gap before runtime v3.4
learnings.body: Edge logs land in the edge-logs-raw bucket, partitioned by hour. The cache_status field is only populated for HTTP/2 requests before edge runtime v3.4, so older dashboards undercount misses. Filter on protocol before comparing time ranges that span the upgrade.

learnings.title: Purge propagation timing and --wait
learnings.body: A global purge takes about 8 seconds at p50 and 35 seconds at p99 across the 42 PoPs. `edgectl purge --wait` blocks until every PoP acknowledges. Do not use --wait in the deploy pipeline, since it can add up to 90 seconds to a release.

learnings.title: Query string ordering and array params
learnings.body: The default cache key sorts query parameters alphabetically, so ?a=1&b=2 and ?b=2&a=1 share one entry. Repeated keys like ?id=1&id=2 are not normalized, so use the id[] convention in the API client. Otherwise you get duplicate cache entries for the same data.

learnings.title: Authorization header bypasses cache unless allowlisted
learnings.body: Requests carrying an Authorization header skip the cache unless the path appears in public-cacheable.txt. Adding a new public endpoint requires that allowlist entry plus a Cache-Control: public header from origin. Forgetting either one silently disables caching for that route.

learnings.title: Rolling back an edge function leaves bad cache entries
learnings.body: To revert a bad edge function, run `edgefn rollback --to prev --zone all`. That alone does not evict what the bad version wrote. Also purge the function's namespace with `edgectl purge --key fn:resize`, or you'll keep serving broken transforms.

learnings.title: Manual cert push to the edge takes about 4 minutes
learnings.body: certs from certbot-internal are pushed by cert-sync every 6 hours. For an urgent rotation, run `certsync push --host img.cdn.internal`. It takes about 4 minutes to reach all PoPs, so schedule the change before the old cert expires, not at expiry.

learnings.title: Zone mirror lags console edits by up to 5 minutes
learnings.body: The dnsctl tool pushes changes from our source of truth to the Route53 mirror on a 5-minute cron, so a record edited directly in the AWS console can disagree with `dnsctl status` for a while. To force a sync immediately, run `dnsctl sync --zone corp.example.net --force`. Do not hand-edit the mirror, because the next cron run will silently overwrite it.

learnings.title: Lower TTLs 24h before any API cutover
learnings.body: House rule: drop the TTL on api.example.net to 60s at least 24 hours before a migration, since resolvers in the wild were caching the old 3600s value for the full hour during the March move. Restore to 300s once the cutover has been stable for two business days. Record the change in the #netops-changes channel so on-call knows the window.

learnings.title: Split-horizon: why laptops off VPN get 10.x for internal names
learnings.body: The internal.example.net zone is split-horizon, so inside the VPN it resolves to 10.40.x addresses and outside it resolves to the CDN. If a laptop off VPN returns a 10.x address, the usual cause is a stale resolver entry from the old VPN profile. Run `scutil --dns` on macOS to see which resolver is answering, and re-login to the VPN client to reset it.

learnings.title: VPN tunnel MTU is 1380, TLS hangs on large chains
learnings.body: Symptom: TLS handshakes to internal services hang after the ClientHello when the certificate chain is large, while small requests work fine. The VPN tunnel MTU is 1380 and path MTU discovery is blocked by the gateway, so large packets are dropped. Verify with `ping -M do -s 1352 10.40.0.10`, and set the interface MTU to 1380 in the VPN profile if the ping fails.

learnings.title: NAT gateway idle timeout is 350s; keep pools below it
learnings.body: The shared NAT gateway silently drops TCP connections that sit idle for more than 350 seconds, which shows up as random 'connection reset by peer' errors in our Python and Go workers. Set the HTTP client keepalive to 300s and enable a keepalive probe on the pool. Do not raise the gateway timeout, because the network team will not change it for a single service.

learnings.title: Use dnsq, not dig +trace, for internal resolvers
learnings.body: Quick reference: `dig +trace` only walks public root and authoritative servers, so it will never show what the internal resolvers return for corp names. Use `dnsq @10.0.0.53 svc-billing.corp.example.net A` to query a specific internal resolver directly. Add `+tcp` if you suspect a truncated response from a large TXT record.

learnings.title: No wildcard CNAMEs under svc.example.net
learnings.body: We stopped using wildcard CNAMEs under svc.example.net after a wildcard silently captured the health-check hostname for two services and sent traffic to the wrong load balancer. Every service now gets an explicit record created through `svcdns add`. If you need a new name, file it through the template, not by adding a wildcard.

learnings.title: acmeflow DNS-01 challenges need the TXT record in Northwind
learnings.body: Our certificate renewal tool acmeflow uses the DNS-01 challenge, which writes a TXT record at _acme-challenge under the target domain. The Northwind DNS provider takes roughly 90 seconds to publish, and acmeflow checks only once after 30 seconds, so renewals fail intermittently. Set `propagation_wait: 120` in the acmeflow config for any zone hosted at Northwind.

learnings.title: netprobe reports RTT in microseconds, not milliseconds
learnings.body: The netprobe CLI prints round-trip times in microseconds in its default table output, which has caused at least two incorrect latency reports to leadership. A value of 48213 means about 48 ms. Pass `--units ms` to get milliseconds, or read the JSON output which always uses ms. Please fix any dashboards that ingest the raw table.

learnings.title: ndots:5 causes four extra lookups per external call in pods
learnings.body: Kubernetes sets ndots:5 by default, so every lookup for an external name like api.stripe-proxy.net first tries four internal search suffixes before the real query. For our batch jobs this roughly quintupled CoreDNS traffic during the Q2 backfill. Set `dnsConfig.options: [{name: ndots, value: "2"}]` in the pod spec for any job that calls outside the cluster heavily.

learnings.title: NAT port exhaustion shows up as ErrorPortAllocation
learnings.body: When a service opens too many connections to a single destination IP through the egress NAT, new connections fail without a clear app error. Check the CloudWatch metric ErrorPortAllocation on the nat-egress-prod gateway; anything above zero means a single IP is saturating its 55,000 source-port budget. The usual fix is connection pooling in the client, not more NAT gateways.

learnings.title: Load balancer health checks come from three CIDRs
learnings.body: Health checks for our internal ALBs originate from 10.60.0.0/24, 10.61.0.0/24, and 10.62.0.0/24, and security groups must allow all three or targets will flap. A common mistake is allowlisting only the VPC CIDR, which excludes the health-check subnets in the second region. If a new service shows 'unhealthy' with a 200 response in curl, check this first.

learnings.title: DNSSEC DS mismatch returns SERVFAIL; use delv to confirm
learnings.body: The example.net zone is DNSSEC signed, and a mismatch between the DS record at the registrar and the active KSK produces SERVFAIL for everyone, not just us. Run `delv @8.8.8.8 www.example.net A` to see the validation failure reason directly. Key rollovers are scheduled in the dnssec-rollover calendar, and nobody should touch the registrar DS without the netops on-call present.

learnings.title: Grafana net-edge-overview hides burst packet loss
learnings.body: The packet loss panel on the net-edge-overview dashboard averages over 5-minute windows, which smooths out short bursts that cause real customer timeouts. Switch the panel query to the raw 15s series before drawing conclusions about loss. The dashboard default was left at 5m because the old exporter could not produce anything finer.

learnings.title: JVM services pin DNS cache TTL to 10 seconds
learnings.body: Our base JVM images set networkaddress.cache.ttl=10 in java.security, because services behind the blue-green failover kept resolving the retired IP for minutes. If you bake your own image, do not drop that line, and do not set the value to 0 since that disables the cache and multiplies resolver load. Verify inside a running container with `jcmd <pid> VM.system_properties | grep cache`.

learnings.title: Peering does not transit; route through tgw-prod-east
learnings.body: VPC peering in our setup is not transitive, so a service in vpc-analytics cannot reach vpc-warehouse through vpc-core even if both peerings exist. All cross-VPC traffic should go through the transit gateway tgw-prod-east, which has the route tables already populated. If a new VPC needs access, request an attachment via the netops queue rather than adding another peering.

learnings.title: fwgate evaluates explicit deny rules before any-source allows
learnings.body: The fwgate firewall evaluates rules in priority order, but any rule with source 0.0.0.0/0 is implicitly placed after all rules with explicit sources, regardless of its priority number. This surprised the reporting team, whose new allow-all rule for the BI tool was never hit. Make the source explicit, even if it is a /16, to get predictable ordering.

learnings.title: Office guest Wi-Fi rewrites NXDOMAIN; force DoH on laptops
learnings.body: The office guest-net Wi-Fi hijacks NXDOMAIN responses and returns a captive portal IP, which breaks CLI tools that expect a clean failure. Engineers working on that network should enable DNS over HTTPS in the company Mac profile, which bypasses the hijack. If a tool hangs instead of failing, check whether it is hitting the captive portal address 192.0.2.1.

learnings.title: Flush macOS DNS cache with two commands
learnings.body: On macOS Sonoma and later, run `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache` followed by `sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder` to clear the resolver cache. Running only the first command leaves stale entries for up to 30 minutes in the mDNSResponder process. The Linux equivalent on our fleet is `resolvectl flush-caches`.

learnings.title: Warehouse allowlist uses the egress IP, which changes on NAT replacement
learnings.body: Analysts connecting to the warehouse from our office are allowlisted by egress IP 203.0.113.42, but that address changes whenever the NAT gateway is replaced. Before a scheduled maintenance window, the netops team posts the new IP in #netops-changes and updates the allowlist 24 hours ahead. If your BI connection suddenly fails with a timeout, check the current egress IP with `curl -s https://ifconfig.corp.example.net`.

learnings.title: dns-canary alerts when p95 exceeds 150ms
learnings.body: The dns-canary job queries six internal and external names every 30 seconds from six regions and alerts when the p95 latency exceeds 150ms for 10 consecutive minutes. A single region alerting usually means a regional resolver problem, while all six alerting points to the upstream forwarder. Acknowledge in PagerDuty with the region tag so the right resolver owner gets paged.

learnings.title: TIME_WAIT buildup in batch workers; widen the local port range
learnings.body: The nightly batch workers were exhausting ephemeral ports, and `ss -s` showed over 40,000 sockets in TIME_WAIT on each host. The fix was to set net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range to '20000 65000' through our sysctl role and enable connection reuse in the HTTP client. Check the value with `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` before debugging anything else on those hosts.

learnings.title: checkcname results are cached for 15 minutes
learnings.body: Customers who set up a CNAME for our custom domain feature often see 'not verified' right after making the change, because the admin console's checkcname tool caches DNS results for 15 minutes. Tell the customer to wait before retrying, and do not tell them propagation takes 48 hours, which is out of date. If the record is still wrong after 15 minutes, compare the answer from `dnsq @1.1.1.1` against what they entered.

learnings.title: trusted hops for X-Forwarded-For is 2 at ingress-gw
learnings.body: The ingress-gw service is configured with trusted_hops: 2, meaning the client IP is the second-to-last entry in X-Forwarded-For, not the first. Services that read the first entry will log the CDN edge address instead of the customer's address, which breaks rate limiting and geo rules. Use the shared helper client_ip() in the platform SDK rather than parsing the header yourself.

learnings.title: Reverse DNS for mail relays must match HELO name
learnings.body: Our outbound mail relays need PTR records that match the HELO hostname exactly, or receiving servers will greylist or reject us. Create the PTR through `ptrctl set 203.0.113.17 mx-relay-03.mail.example.net` and then confirm with `dig -x 203.0.113.17 +short`. The PTR change is not instant, so allow about 20 minutes before testing with an external checker.

learnings.title: Synthetic checks from office network are not representative
learnings.body: Synthetic uptime checks that run from the office network show lower latency than the same checks from production regions, because the office has a direct peering path to our data centers. Do not use office results to set SLO baselines or alert thresholds. Use the 'cloud-probe' location group in the synthetics tool for any customer-facing latency number.

learnings.title: Internal CA chain must be bundled for the Java truststore
learnings.body: Services that call internal HTTPS endpoints fail with PKIX path building errors unless the internal root and intermediate are both in the truststore. The corp-ca-bundle.pem file in the platform-certs repo contains both, but some teams copied only the root in 2023. Re-import with `keytool -importcert -file corp-ca-bundle.pem -alias corp-ca -keystore cacerts` as a deploy step for any service built before June.

learnings.title: Wireguard handshake every 120s; ignore it when debugging
learnings.body: The site-to-site WireGuard tunnels to the Denver office send a keepalive handshake every 120 seconds, which fills the logs with 'handshake completed' lines that look like errors to new people. The real signal is the 'latest handshake' age in `wg show`, which should stay under 180 seconds. If it goes above 180, restart the wg-quick@office-den unit on the gateway.

learnings.title: Squash-merge is the only merge method allowed on main
learnings.body: Repo settings on the monorepo allow only squash merges into main, so the PR title becomes the commit subject. The merge-bot rejects titles that don't follow Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, chore:), so fix the title before clicking merge rather than amending after. Individual commit messages inside the PR don't matter for history.

learnings.title: Force-push guardrail blocks release branches
learnings.body: The pre-push hook installed by make setup runs guardrail-check and refuses force pushes to release/* and main. On feature branches, use git push --force-with-lease, never plain --force. If you truly need to rewrite a release branch, ask in #release-eng and they will run git push with the break-glass token from Keystone.

learnings.title: Pointer files after clone mean git-lfs is missing
learnings.body: The assets/ folder is tracked with Git LFS, so a clone without git-lfs installed gives you 130-byte pointer files where fonts and images should be. Install git-lfs and run git lfs pull --include='assets/fonts/**' to fetch only what you need. The design-system build fails with a confusing SVG parse error when this happens.

learnings.title: Set up the commit template with make setup
learnings.body: Running make setup in the repo root sets commit.template to .gitmessage and turns on commit.gpgsign. The template includes a Ticket: footer line that the commit-lint job requires for any branch matching OPS-* or PAY-*. If you cloned before this was added, rerun make setup; nothing else needs changing.

learnings.title: Reverting a merge commit needs -m 1
learnings.body: To undo a merge to main, run git revert -m 1 <merge-sha>, because the -m flag selects the mainline parent. Anyone who later wants that feature back has to revert the revert first, or the re-merge will silently produce no changes. We hit this in March with the ledger export branch and it took a day to untangle.

learnings.title: Use git worktree for hotfixes instead of stashing
learnings.body: On-call has been using git worktree add ../hotfix-4.2 origin/release/4.2 so the main checkout stays on whatever feature branch you were working on. Remove it afterwards with git worktree remove ../hotfix-4.2 and then git worktree prune if the folder was deleted by hand. Stashing has caused two incidents where the wrong branch got a hotfix commit.

learnings.title: Signed commits via SSH keys are required on release branches
learnings.body: The verify-commits check blocks any commit on release/* that lacks a valid signature. Configure git with gpg.format ssh and user.signingkey pointing at your public key, then register that key in Keystone under Settings > Signing Keys. Keys registered after your commit was pushed do not retroactively validate it, so re-sign and push again.

learnings.title: Submodule vendor/charts is empty after pulling
learnings.body: The vendor/charts directory is a git submodule, and a plain git pull leaves it as an empty folder. The helm lint step then fails with 'no Chart.yaml found' which looks unrelated. Run git submodule update --init --recursive after every pull that touches .gitmodules, or just use the make sync target which does this for you.

learnings.title: Rerere saved us during release cherry-picks
learnings.body: We enabled rerere org-wide with git config --global rerere.enabled true after the 2024.05 train. During the cherry-pick sequence for the 2024.06 release, rerere auto-resolved roughly 40 percent of the conflicts in the billing templates from recorded resolutions. Resolutions are cached in .git/rr-cache and do not sync between machines, so the release captain's laptop has the useful ones.

learnings.title: Branch names must start with a ticket prefix
learnings.body: The branchlint check in CI requires branch names in the form <PREFIX>-<number>/<short-slug>, with prefixes limited to OPS, PAY, DATA, and WEB. Names longer than 60 characters are rejected, which bites people who paste a full ticket title. Rename with git branch -m before opening the PR, because the check runs on the branch name at PR creation and won't re-run on rename.

learnings.title: Release branch cut schedule and backport labels
learnings.body: Release branches are cut as release/YYYY.MM on the second Tuesday of each month, and the freeze happens at 14:00 UTC the day before. To backport a fix, merge it to main first and then add the label backport-to-YYYY.MM to the PR, which triggers the cherry-pick bot. Always cherry-pick with git cherry-pick -x so the original SHA is recorded in the message.

learnings.title: Gitleaks false positives in fixtures
learnings.body: The sentinel-scan pre-commit hook flags strings in testdata/fixtures/ that look like API keys, which blocks commits to the payments test suite. Add the path to the allowlist in .sentinel.toml under [allowlist] paths rather than using --no-verify. Using --no-verify gets the commit flagged again in the nightly audit job.

learnings.title: Stash skips untracked files by default
learnings.body: git stash on its own leaves untracked files in place, so a stash followed by checkout can leave new migration files behind and make the tree look dirty. Use git stash push -u to include untracked files. The devbox sync command also deletes untracked files in the workspace, so move anything you care about into a commit first.

learnings.title: Org dotfiles set pull.rebase to true
learnings.body: The dotfiles-sync tool sets pull.rebase true and rebase.autoStash true for everyone on the company laptop image. If you see a merge commit appear from a plain git pull, your local ~/.gitconfig is overriding the org default, usually from an old setup script. Remove the pull.rebase line and rerun dotfiles-sync apply.

learnings.title: Sparse checkout for the billing monolith
learnings.body: The full monorepo clone is about 38 GB, so the repo-clone script defaults to sparse checkout with cone mode. Run repo-clone --profile billing to get services/billing and libs/common only, which takes about 4 minutes on the office network. Add more paths later with git sparse-checkout add <path>, and don't use set unless you want to drop the existing paths.

learnings.title: Bisect with a flaky test needs exit code 125
learnings.body: When running git bisect run on the ledger suite, flaky failures poison the result. Wrap the test in a script that exits 125 when the environment is broken, since bisect treats 125 as skip. Exit 1 marks the commit as bad, so a flaky failure will point you at the wrong commit with no warning.

learnings.title: stale-branch-reaper deletes remote branches after 90 days
learnings.body: The stale-branch-reaper job runs every Sunday night and deletes remote branches with no commits in 90 days. Branches with a keep/ prefix are exempt, so rename important long-lived experiments to keep/<name>. The reaper posts a list to #eng-hygiene 48 hours before deletion, and deleted branches can be restored from the reflog snapshot for 14 days.

learnings.title: Commits must use a corporate author email
learnings.body: The pre-receive hook mailcheck rejects pushes where the commit author email is not on the corp domain, which often happens after a fresh laptop setup with a personal Gmail in git config. To fix a rejected push, run git config user.email with your work address and then git rebase -r --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author' origin/main. Do this before pushing again.

learnings.title: Merge queue batches are capped at eight PRs
learnings.body: The merge queue runs up to eight PRs in one batch against a temporary branch named mq/batch-<id>. If a PR in the middle of the batch fails, the queue ejects it and reruns the rest, adding about 20 minutes. Use mq retry <pr-number> to re-enqueue an ejected PR once the failure is understood, rather than pushing a new commit.

learnings.title: Line ending normalization broke Windows shell scripts
learnings.body: The repo .gitattributes sets * text=auto eol=lf, but scripts/*.sh were committed with CRLF in 2023 and failed on Windows checkouts with a bad interpreter error. The fix was git add --renormalize . followed by a single commit labeled chore: normalize line endings. If you see the error on a fresh checkout, check the file with file scripts/deploy.sh before changing anything else.

learnings.title: Recovering from a reset --hard on a shared branch
learnings.body: Someone ran git reset --hard on feature/ledger-v2 and force-pushed, dropping three commits from the remote. The recovery was to fetch the backup refs that gitgate snapshots every 15 minutes at refs/gitgate/<branch>/<timestamp>, then push that ref back to the branch. Those snapshots are retained for 14 days, so tell the team lead within the hour so the window isn't missed.

learnings.title: Release tags must be annotated and match the changelog
learnings.body: Release tags use the form v2024.06.1 and must be annotated, because the release pipeline reads the tag message for the notes. Run make tag VERSION=2024.06.1, which refuses to proceed if CHANGELOG.md has no matching heading. Lightweight tags created with git tag directly get ignored by the publisher without any error.

learnings.title: Affected-test selection depends on your merge-base
learnings.body: CI computes affected tests using the merge-base between your branch and origin/main, so a branch cut from an old main can run the full suite of about 52 minutes instead of the usual 9. Run git fetch origin main and git rebase origin/main before pushing to keep selection tight. The job log prints the merge-base SHA at the top, which is the quickest way to check.

learnings.title: PRs over 800 changed lines need two approvers
learnings.body: The size-labeler bot tags any PR with more than 800 changed lines as size/xl and requires two approvals before merge. Generated files such as openapi clients and lockfiles are excluded from the count if they live under gen/ or are named *.lock. If your change is large because of a rename, split the rename into its own PR, which usually drops it below the threshold.

learnings.title: Add formatter commit to blame ignore file
learnings.body: After the repo-wide Prettier migration, git blame pointed at the formatting commit for almost every line. The team added its SHA to .git-blame-ignore-revs, and each developer needs git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs set locally. GitHub honors the file automatically, but the local git command does not until the config is set.

learnings.title: Never hand-merge pnpm-lock.yaml during a rebase
learnings.body: When a rebase conflicts on pnpm-lock.yaml, do not try to resolve the markers by hand, since the file is machine-generated and conflicts that look trivial often drop dependency entries. Accept either side with git checkout --theirs pnpm-lock.yaml, then run pnpm install --lockfile-only to regenerate it. The lockfile-drift check in CI will fail the PR if you skip the regeneration step.

learnings.title: Hotfixes must target both release and main
learnings.body: A hotfix branch should be cut from the current release/* branch, not from main, or the fix will not appear in the shipped build. Open the PR against the release branch and then use the dual-target bot by commenting /also-main on the PR, which opens a matching PR into main. Both PRs need the hotfix label so the on-call review rotation picks them up.

learnings.title: CODEOWNERS for ledger/ now requires two approvals from finops-eng
learnings.body: After the March reconciliation incident, the CODEOWNERS entry for ledger/ in the monorepo was changed to require two approvals from @finops-eng. The revbot auto-approver ignores anything under that path, even with the dependabot label. For an emergency bypass, page the finops on-call lead through PagerDuty service FIN-PRIMARY and they will add the override label.

learnings.title: Reviewer assignment: rotor picks by timezone overlap, not by file owner
learnings.body: Rotor assigns reviewers round-robin, but it weights toward people whose working hours overlap the PR author's by at least four hours. If you want a specific reviewer, add them manually, because rotor will still add one more name. Lisbon and Austin authors often end up with the same two Lisbon reviewers, so check the rotor dashboard if your PR has sat for a day.

learnings.title: Soft cap of 400 changed lines; pr-size-bot warns at 600
learnings.body: The pr-size-bot comment appears at 400 changed lines and turns red at 600. Generated files under gen/ and any lockfile are excluded from the count. Reviewers are allowed to ask for a split in the first review round, and authors should not argue it into a 900-line review.

learnings.title: Prefix nit comments with 'nit:' and never block on them
learnings.body: Our convention is that any review comment starting with 'nit:' is non-blocking and the author can merge without addressing it. Use 'blocking:' explicitly for things that must change before merge. The team agreed on this in the Q3 retro after three separate threads turned into two-day debates about variable names.

learnings.title: staleness-sweeper closes PRs idle for 9 days, and the reopen command
learnings.body: The staleness-sweeper job marks PRs with no activity for 9 days as stale and closes them after another 3. To reopen one, comment '/unstale' on the PR, which resets the clock. Closing does not delete the branch, so the work can still be recovered from the remote if the reopen fails.

learnings.title: Migration PRs need a @dba-rota reviewer and the checklist template
learnings.body: Any PR touching files under db/migrations/ must include the migration checklist from the PR template, and must tag @dba-rota as a reviewer. The DBA rota reviewer checks lock duration estimates against the staging replica numbers in the migration dashboard. Migrations that lock a table for more than 2 seconds are sent back regardless of other approvals.

learnings.title: Use 'stackctl sync' after rebasing a stacked PR chain
learnings.body: When you have a stack of PRs, rebasing the bottom one does not update the ones above it on GitHub. Run 'stackctl sync --from <bottom-branch>' to rebase the whole chain and push the updated refs in order. If you skip this, reviewers see diffs that include commits already merged into the base.

learnings.title: Self-approval blocked on release/* branches
learnings.body: The Git host is configured so an author cannot approve their own PR when the target branch matches release/*. Even if you are the only engineer on a hotfix, you must get one reviewer from the release captains group. Ask in #release-captains and someone from the rota will pick it up within the hour during business hours.

learnings.title: Visual diff bot needs a Lumen snapshot approval for UI changes
learnings.body: UI changes under web/components/ trigger the Lumen visual diff job, which posts screenshots of changed pages to the PR. A reviewer must click 'approve snapshots' in the Lumen panel, separate from the code approval. Snapshots are compared at 1280px and 390px widths only, so a layout bug on a 1024px tablet will slip through.

learnings.title: Mechanical rename PRs use the 'mechanical' label and still need one human pass
learnings.body: Bulk renames and codemods can carry the 'mechanical' label, which lets them skip the usual two-reviewer requirement. They still need one human to look at the codemod script output, not the full diff. Reviewers should spot-check at least five random files and confirm the script was run from a clean checkout.

learnings.title: Only the reviewer resolves threads on the infra repo
learnings.body: In the infra repo, authors do not mark review threads as resolved. The reviewer who opened the thread clicks resolve once they are satisfied with the reply. This rule came from a Terraform change last spring where a thread was resolved by the author without the reviewer seeing the follow-up commit.

learnings.title: Conventional comment prefixes used across the analytics team
learnings.body: The analytics team uses conventional comment prefixes: 'question:', 'suggestion:', 'issue:', and 'praise:' in addition to 'nit:'. The prefix sits at the start of the comment and is mandatory for dbt model reviews. Reviewers who write 'hmm' or 'thoughts?' with no prefix are asked to rewrite the comment before the author responds.

learnings.title: dbt PRs must attach the diffscope row count report
learnings.body: Every PR that modifies a dbt model must run 'dbt build --select state:modified+' in CI and attach the diffscope report that CI posts. Reviewers check the row count delta column, and any change above 1.5 percent on a mart table needs a note explaining it. Diffscope compares against the prod snapshot taken at 02:00 UTC.

learnings.title: Terraform PRs must paste the plan summary from tfplan-summary
learnings.body: Infra PRs must include the output of tfplan-summary, which the CI job posts as a collapsed comment. The summary lists creates, updates, and destroys per workspace, and any destroy line needs an explicit callout in the PR description. Reviewers have rejected several plans where a destroy on a load balancer was buried in the middle of a long diff.

learnings.title: Merge queue ejects PRs if approval changes mid-run
learnings.body: The merge queue (queuectl) snapshots the approval state when a PR enters the queue. If a reviewer dismisses their approval or pushes a new commit while the queue is running, the PR is ejected with the message 'approval state changed'. Re-enter it with 'queuectl requeue <pr-number>' once the review is settled.

learnings.title: Applying GitHub suggestion blocks creates commits authored by the bot
learnings.body: When a reviewer uses the suggestion block and the author clicks 'Commit suggestion', the resulting commit is authored by the Git host's bot account, not the reviewer. This breaks our contribution tracking, so for anything the reviewer wants credit for, push the change manually with a Co-authored-by trailer. The bot commits are excluded from the quarterly review metrics.

learnings.title: gitleaks-lite false positives on test fixtures: use the allow comment with a ticket
learnings.body: The pre-commit hook gitleaks-lite flags high-entropy strings in test fixtures, which blocks many PRs in the payments test suite. The accepted fix is to add the comment '# gitleaks:allow SEC-' followed by a ticket number on the same line. Reviewers should verify the ticket exists and that the string is not a real credential.

learnings.title: Reviews go in first-response SLA of one business day, tracked in ReviewPulse
learnings.body: The team target is a first response on every review request within one business day, and ReviewPulse shows the clock for each open PR. The dashboard counts a reply or a reaction as a response, so a thumbs-up does not count as a review. Teams that breach the SLA twice in a sprint get a line in the Monday planning doc.

learnings.title: Jupyter notebooks are not reviewed directly; run nbsync first
learnings.body: Notebooks in the research repo do not diff well, so reviews happen on the .py files produced by 'nbsync pull <notebook>'. Authors commit both the notebook and the synced script, and reviewers comment only on the script. If a reviewer finds a logic error, the fix goes into the script and then 'nbsync push' regenerates the notebook.

learnings.title: Draft PRs skip CI on the cheap runner pool unless 'ready-for-review' is set
learnings.body: Draft PRs run only the lint stage on the cheap runner pool and skip the full integration suite. To trigger the full suite, run 'pr ready' from the CLI or click Ready for review, and CI will queue on the standard pool. Reviewers should not be assigned to drafts, since rotor ignores them until they are marked ready.

learnings.title: Feature flag defaults must be checked in config/flags.yaml during review
learnings.body: Any PR that adds a feature flag must set its default in config/flags.yaml, and reviewers check that the default is off in production. The flag linter fails if a new flag has no owner field, but it does not check the default value. Two incidents last year came from flags that shipped enabled because the reviewer assumed the linter had caught it.

learnings.title: covwatch blocks PRs that drop coverage by more than 0.5 points
learnings.body: The covwatch job compares coverage on the PR branch against main and posts a delta comment. A drop greater than 0.5 percentage points blocks merge until a reviewer adds the 'coverage-waiver' label with a reason. Generated code and the vendored sdk/ directory are excluded from the calculation.

learnings.title: Auth middleware changes require the needs-sec label and a secteam review
learnings.body: Changes to auth middleware under server/auth/ must carry the 'needs-sec' label, which auto-assigns the security team. Their review SLA is two business days, longer than the standard one, so plan accordingly for releases. A secteam reviewer must approve even if the change looks trivial, because a rename once broke session expiry for a week.

learnings.title: Approve with a reason in the body when overriding a failing check
learnings.body: When you approve a PR that has a red check, the approval body must state which check failed and why it is acceptable. Our audit export pulls approval bodies into the quarterly compliance report, and blank approvals on red builds get flagged. Use the template 'Overriding <check-name>: <reason>, tracked in <ticket>'.

learnings.title: Commit trailers Reviewed-by are enforced by the tessera-lint hook
learnings.body: The commit-msg hook tessera-lint rejects commits that include a Reviewed-by trailer for someone who has not approved the PR. This catches people who paste a trailer for a colleague who only commented. Install the hook with 'tessera-lint install' after cloning, since it is not applied automatically by the repo bootstrap script.

learnings.title: Frontend PRs over 300 lines get a Storybook review link requirement
learnings.body: For component changes over 300 lines, the PR description must include a Chromatic link to the Storybook build for the affected components. Reviewers open the link instead of checking out the branch, which cut average review time on the design system repo from two days to about one. Stories without a play function are flagged in the PR checklist.

learnings.title: Squash merge is the default, but keep the commit body for migrations
learnings.body: The default merge method in our repos is squash, and the squash commit message is pulled from the PR title and description. For migration PRs, keep the full commit log by choosing 'merge commit' instead, because the migration runner reads the individual commit SHAs to order the scripts. Reviewers should check the merge method selector before approving a migration.

learnings.title: Review requests on Fridays after 15:00 UTC are held until Monday
learnings.body: Review requests opened after 15:00 UTC on Friday are marked 'weekend hold' by the rota bot and do not appear in reviewers' queues until Monday. This prevents on-call engineers from being pulled into reviews during their rest window. If something is urgent, tag @oncall-platform in the PR instead of requesting a standard review.

learnings.title: Reviewers check the dependency diff in lockfiles, not the lockfile itself
learnings.body: Lockfile diffs are too large to review line by line, so reviewers use 'depdiff lockfile-old lockfile-new' to get a summary of added, removed, and upgraded packages. Flag any new transitive dependency with a non-OSS license, since the license scanner only runs nightly. Do not approve a PR that adds more than five new top-level packages without a note from the author.

learnings.title: Quarantine flaky tests with the flakebot label, not skip markers
learnings.body: Never add @pytest.mark.skip to a flaky test, because skipped tests disappear from the flake dashboard. Apply the flakebot:quarantine label on the PR instead, which keeps the test running in the nightly job and posts results to #qa-flakes. Quarantined tests auto-expire after 14 days, and flakebot will reopen the ticket if they are still failing.

learnings.title: pytest-xdist workers need their own Postgres schema
learnings.body: Running pytest -n 4 against the shared ci_pg instance caused random unique-constraint failures in the accounts suite. Our conftest now creates a schema named test_<worker_id> per worker through the worker_db fixture. If you add a new fixture that touches the database, take worker_db as an argument rather than connecting directly.

learnings.title: Regenerate snapshots with make snap-update, then review the diff
learnings.body: Run make snap-update from the repo root instead of pytest --snapshot-update, since the Makefile target also re-formats the JSON fixtures. The reviewer must check the snapshot diff tab in Gitlab, and PRs with more than 400 changed snapshot lines need a second approver from the owning team. Snapshot updates in the same commit as logic changes get bounced by the pre-merge bot.

learnings.title: covgate blocks merges below 82% coverage on changed lines
learnings.body: Our covgate step compares coverage only on lines touched by the diff, not the whole package, so a small PR adding untested code will fail even if total coverage looks healthy. The threshold is 82% and is set in .covgate.yml under changed_lines_min. To run locally, use covgate check --base origin/main before pushing, which takes about 20 seconds.

learnings.title: Playwright smoke suite runs against preview envs, not staging
learnings.body: The @smoke tagged Playwright tests are wired to the preview environment that Argo spins up for each PR, and they will fail if the preview deploy is still warming up. If you see ECONNREFUSED on the first navigation, wait for the preview-ready check in the PR and rerun the job rather than changing the test. Staging is only used by the nightly e2e pipeline.

learnings.title: Load test threshold for checkout is p95 under 300ms at 500 VUs
learnings.body: Ran pulsar-lite against the checkout API last sprint and the agreed release gate is p95 latency below 300ms at 500 concurrent virtual users, with error rate under 0.5 percent. The scenario file lives in loadtests/checkout/steady.js and must be run from the perf-runner VM, because laptops on VPN skew the results by roughly 40ms. Results are auto-posted to the #perf-gate channel.

learnings.title: Mutation testing runs nightly on billing module only
learnings.body: We tried running mutmut across the whole monorepo and it timed out after six hours, so the nightly job now targets only services/billing and services/ledger. The surviving-mutant report is in the mutants/ artifact of the nightly pipeline, and anything above 15 percent survival needs a ticket. Do not run it locally on the full tree; use mutmut run --paths-to-mutate services/billing for quick checks.

learnings.title: Test Postgres template db tpl_ci_v4 must be rebuilt after migrations
learnings.body: The CI database is cloned from a template named tpl_ci_v4, and cloning is instant only if the template matches the latest migration head. If the migration step in CI goes from 20 seconds to 9 minutes, someone forgot to bump the template, so run ./scripts/rebuild_template.sh v4 on the ci-db host. The script also deletes the stale v3 template to free disk space.

learnings.title: Freeze time with the clockwork fixture, not freezegun
learnings.body: freezegun conflicts with our async event loop helpers and causes intermittent hangs in the notifications tests, so we standardized on the clockwork pytest fixture from libs/testkit. Use the frozen_clock fixture and call frozen_clock.advance(minutes=5) instead of patching datetime directly. Tests that still import freezegun will be flagged by the lint rule TK102.

learnings.title: Golden file refresh needs a reviewer from the data team
learnings.body: The golden outputs in tests/golden/reports are compared byte-for-byte, and running make golden-refresh rewrites all of them, including any that changed unintentionally. Because these files feed the weekly reporting dashboard, the PR must have a review from someone on data-platform, and the description should list which report keys changed. Refreshing a single file is possible with GOLDEN_ONLY=monthly_churn make golden-refresh.

learnings.title: dbt severity: use warn for freshness, error only for finance tests
learnings.body: After the Q2 incident we changed all dbt tests on finance models to severity: error and everything else defaults to warn, so a nightly warn does not page anyone. Use dbt test --select tag:finance_critical in the pre-deploy hook to block releases. If you add a test with no severity set, it inherits warn, which is intentional.

learnings.title: Limit CI retries to 2 and only for e2e jobs
learnings.body: We removed the global retry setting after it started hiding real regressions in the order service, and retries are now enabled only for jobs tagged e2e using retry: 2 in the job definition. Unit and integration jobs should fail on first error. If you need to retry a unit test to diagnose it, do it locally with pytest --count=5 instead of pushing empty commits.

learnings.title: Feature flags in tests come from flags.test.yaml
learnings.body: The flag service's test environment reads from config/flags.test.yaml, and any flag not listed defaults to off in CI, which is why new features sometimes look broken only in the pipeline. Add the flag key and its test value to that file in the same PR as the feature. The flag SDK fixture in libs/testkit/flags.py also lets you override a single flag per test with the flag_override fixture.

learnings.title: pytest-timeout is 30 seconds by default, bump per test with marker
learnings.body: The default per-test timeout in pytest.ini is 30 seconds, which catches hung tests but also trips slow integration tests against the sandbox gateway. Use @pytest.mark.timeout(120) on the specific test rather than raising the global default, because the global change slowed the whole pipeline by about 9 minutes last time. Timeouts are logged to the test report under the timeout key.

learnings.title: Never put live gateway keys in test fixtures, use mockpay
learnings.body: During a review last month we found a sandbox key committed to a fixture file in the subscriptions repo, which triggered a rotation. All tests should point at the mockpay service, which runs in the test docker-compose profile on port 4410 and mimics the gateway's responses. If you need a new response shape, add it to mockpay/scenarios rather than hardcoding it into the test.

learnings.title: CI shards are balanced by the .durations/ci.json file
learnings.body: The test runner splits the suite into eight shards using the historical timings in .durations/ci.json, so a test that suddenly takes three times longer can unbalance the whole run. The file is regenerated every Sunday by the durations-refresh job, but you can update it manually with make durations after a big change. If one shard consistently runs more than 12 minutes longer than the rest, open a ticket for the platform team.

learnings.title: Bug fix PRs must include a regression test named after the ticket
learnings.body: The merge checklist requires that any PR labeled bugfix contains at least one test whose name includes the Jira key, such as test_refund_idempotent_OPS_1842. The pre-merge check greps test names for the ticket key and blocks the merge if none is found. If the bug cannot be reproduced in a unit test, note that in the PR description and an integration test will be accepted instead.

learnings.title: Hypothesis runs 50 examples locally and 200 in CI
learnings.body: Our Hypothesis settings profile sets max_examples to 50 for local runs and 200 in CI, selected by the HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE variable set in the CI template. The deadline is disabled because the database fixtures make first examples slow. If a property test fails only in CI, reproduce it with HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci pytest and check the printed seed in the failure output.

learnings.title: Storybook a11y gate fails on any serious axe violation
learnings.body: The storybook-a11y job runs axe-core against every story, and it fails the build on violations rated serious or critical, while moderate ones are only reported. The rule set is in .storybook/axe.config.json, and stories can opt out of a specific rule with parameters.a11y.disable in the story file, but this needs a comment linking to a ticket. The job takes about 6 minutes, so run npm run a11y:quick while iterating.

learnings.title: Manual QA sign-off uses the qa-signoff label and the release sheet
learnings.body: For releases that touch checkout or onboarding, QA must add the qa-signoff label to the release PR only after completing the checklist in the Release Readiness sheet for that version. Each row needs a tester initial and a link to the test run, and rows marked N/A must include a reason. The release bot will refuse to deploy to production without the label, and the label expires after 48 hours.

learnings.title: Analytics event tests validate against eventrail schemas
learnings.body: Any test that emits an analytics event should validate the payload using eventrail.validate(event_name, payload) from libs/analytics, which pulls the schema from the registry at the version pinned in pyproject. Schema versions are pinned so a registry change does not break CI overnight. If the validator reports a missing required field, check whether the schema has been bumped to v3 before changing the producer.

learnings.title: docker compose test profile starts only the integration deps
learnings.body: Running docker compose --profile integ up -d starts Postgres, Redis, mockpay and the queue emulator, but not the full API stack, which saves about 2 GB of memory on laptops. Integration tests tagged @needs_api will fail unless you also start the api service with --profile integ-api. Tear down with docker compose --profile integ down -v, since the -v flag is needed to clear the queue emulator state.

learnings.title: Randomized test order seed is printed on failure, rerun with -p randomly
learnings.body: pytest-randomly is enabled on the backend repo, so test order changes every run and a failure can disappear on rerun. The seed is printed at the top of the CI log as Using --randomly-seed=NNNN, and you can reproduce the same order locally with pytest --randomly-seed=NNNN. If a test only fails under a specific seed, it almost always leaks state through a module-level cache in libs/pricing.

learnings.title: Nightly sandbox data refresh at 02:00 UTC wipes test accounts
learnings.body: The nightly refresh job at 02:00 UTC resets the sandbox tenant to the baseline snapshot, which deletes any test accounts created manually the previous day. If your end-to-end test relies on an account persisting across days, create it through the fixture in e2e/support/accounts.ts so it is recreated on each run. Manual data created in the sandbox after 01:30 UTC may be lost during the refresh window.

learnings.title: Contract tests verify provider states through the Pact broker at pact.internal
learnings.body: Consumer-driven contract tests publish to the Pact broker at pact.internal, and the provider verification job runs on the pricing service whenever a pact changes for the branch. A verification failure usually means the provider state name is misspelled, so check the provider states list in the broker UI first. Pacts for main are only verified against environments marked deployable, so a newly merged provider change may take up to 10 minutes to show up.

learnings.title: Test factories generate IDs from a per-run seed, so avoid hardcoded IDs
learnings.body: The shared factory library in libs/testkit/factories assigns IDs from a counter seeded per test run, so hardcoding an ID like 1001 in a test will collide with a generated record in parallel runs. Use factories.account() and read the id from the returned object instead. The counter resets between sessions, so never persist generated IDs into fixture files checked into git.

learnings.title: Accessibility of PDF exports tested with the pdfcheck CLI
learnings.body: The statements team found that tagged-PDF requirements were regressing silently, so the export tests now run pdfcheck --profile tagged on each generated file. The CLI reports missing structure tags and language metadata, and a failure exits with code 3, which the CI step maps to a hard failure. Run pdfcheck --profile tagged out/*.pdf locally after changing the template, because the output directory is not cleaned between tests.

learnings.title: Shadow traffic tests replay 1 percent of prod reads into staging
learnings.body: Before major read-path changes, the platform team replays one percent of production read requests into staging using the shadowrun tool, and compares the response bodies ignoring fields listed in shadow.ignore.yaml. Mismatches above 0.2 percent block the rollout automatically. Replay is only enabled for GET endpoints, so write-path changes still need the integration suite and a canary.

learnings.title: Stale stats flip orders_lookup to seq scan after bulk loads
learnings.body: After any bulk load touching more than about 5% of rows, the planner for orders_lookup starts choosing a sequential scan and p95 jumps from 12ms to 900ms. Run ANALYZE orders manually as the last step of the backfill job. Autovacuum analyze is too slow to catch this during the nightly import window.

learnings.title: pgb-ledger pool sizing rule for app pods
learnings.body: House rule: each app pod gets at most 40 connections to pgb-ledger in transaction mode. We learned this the hard way when 120 pods x 20 connections exhausted the db host's max_connections during a deploy. If you need more throughput, raise the pod's worker count before touching the pool.

learnings.title: flamescope-lite sampling duration
learnings.body: Use flamescope-lite with --duration 30s and --hz 99 when capturing production CPU profiles. Longer captures just bloat the viewer and make the flame graph unreadable. The pprof endpoint is only reachable on port 6060 through the bastion VPN.

learnings.title: Jitter catalog cache TTLs to avoid midnight stampede
learnings.body: Catalog keys written with a fixed 3600s TTL all expired together at 00:00 UTC and caused a thundering herd on the catalog DB. Now the cache helper adds random jitter of 0 to 15 percent to every TTL. Miss spikes at midnight dropped from roughly 60k/min to under 4k/min.

learnings.title: Run k6-kiln from loadgen pool, not laptops
learnings.body: Don't run k6-kiln from a laptop for anything you plan to quote in a review. Laptop NICs and Wi-Fi top out around 400 rps and the numbers look like a regression that isn't there. Use the loadgen-west pool, which you can request through the infra channel with the ticket template LG-REQ.

learnings.title: Main chunk budget enforced by budgetkeeper
learnings.body: CI runs budgetkeeper on every PR against the main bundle. The gate is 180 KB gzipped and a PR that exceeds it fails with a message showing the top three contributors. Lazy-load anything only used on the settings page, since that has been the most common cause of failures.

learnings.title: G1 region size for svc-inventory
learnings.body: svc-inventory runs with a 24g heap and the default G1 region size was producing 310ms p99 GC pauses. Setting -XX:G1HeapRegionSize=16m brought p99 pause down to about 90ms. Don't copy this to services with heaps under 8g, where it made pauses slightly worse in our tests.

learnings.title: Event loop lag alert on edge-gw
learnings.body: The edge-gw alert fires when event loop lag exceeds 70ms for two consecutive minutes. Most of the time it is a synchronous JSON schema compile on a hot path, not actual load. Run loopwatch against a pod before scaling up, because adding replicas hides the problem without fixing it.

learnings.title: Elasticsearch reindex settings checklist
learnings.body: Before a bulk reindex on search-catalog, set refresh_interval to 30s and replicas to 0. Use bulk requests of about 5MB, which benchmarked better than 1MB or 20MB. Restore refresh_interval to 1s and replicas to 1 afterwards, and check the cluster is green before closing the ticket.

learnings.title: enrich-worker poll size and rebalance storms
learnings.body: Setting max.poll.records above 200 on enrich-worker caused constant consumer group rebalances once batch processing went past 300ms. The session timeout kicked in before the batch finished. Keep max.poll.records at 200 and scale partitions instead if lag builds up.

learnings.title: Tax rate in-process LRU settings
learnings.body: The tax-rate lookup in billing-core uses an in-process LRU with 4096 entries and a 10 minute TTL. That gives a hit rate around 97 percent and removes most calls to the rates service. Don't raise the TTL past 15 minutes, because rate changes at quarter boundaries must show up within the window.

learnings.title: querytrap fails tests on N+1 queries
learnings.body: In staging, the querytrap middleware fails any request that issues more than 25 SQL queries and logs the call site. If a legitimate endpoint needs more, annotate the handler with @allow_queries(n) and link the ticket in the comment. This has caught more N+1 regressions than code review has.

learnings.title: Replace iterrows in nightly rollup
learnings.body: The nightly-rollup job was spending most of its time in pandas iterrows over 2M rows. Rewriting the aggregation as a groupby with vectorized operations cut runtime from 47 minutes to about 70 seconds. Anyone adding a new metric to rollups should follow the same pattern and avoid per-row Python loops.

learnings.title: Gzip threshold on api-edge
learnings.body: api-edge only compresses responses above 1024 bytes. Below that size, the CPU cost of compression exceeded the bytes saved, and p50 latency went up measurably in the 2023 test. If you change this, benchmark on bench-runner-03 with a realistic payload mix, not synthetic JSON.

learnings.title: Keepalive mismatch causes intermittent 502s
learnings.body: The load balancer closes idle upstream connections after 60 seconds, so app keepalive has to be longer than that. We set the app keepalive to 75s on all services behind lb-prod. Before this change, around 0.02 percent of requests returned 502 during low-traffic hours.

learnings.title: COPY beats multi-row INSERT for ingest tables
learnings.body: For ingest-stage tables, COPY from a staging file was about 5x faster than multi-row INSERT in our benchmarks. The loader writes to a temp table and then does an INSERT ... SELECT with ON CONFLICT. Use the shared helper pg_ingest.copy_batch instead of rolling your own.

learnings.title: Autovacuum settings for events_raw
learnings.body: events_raw gets heavy churn, so the default autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor of 0.2 lets bloat run for hours. We set it to 0.02 with autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit at 2000 for that table only. Check pg_stat_user_tables.n_dead_tup weekly to confirm it is keeping up.

learnings.title: Benchmark hygiene on bench-runner-03
learnings.body: Before any microbenchmark on bench-runner-03, pin the CPU governor to performance and disable turbo through the bench-prep script. Run five iterations and discard the first, since the first run always includes page cache warmup. Results without these steps have varied by 15 percent between identical runs.

learnings.title: Five-minute p99 spike traced to sidecar cron
learnings.body: The recurring p99 spike every five minutes on checkout-api turned out to be the metrics-flush cron in the logging sidecar. It was synchronized with the app's own flush interval. Moving the sidecar cron to a two-minute offset removed the spike entirely.

learnings.title: Android cold start budget and device lab
learnings.body: The mobile cold start budget is 1.2 seconds on the pixel-ref-4a in devfarm, which is our reference mid-tier device. Flagship numbers don't count toward the gate because they hide regressions that matter for most users. Run the startup trace through devfarm-cli before merging changes to the app initializer.

learnings.title: Bump CACHE_EPOCH instead of flushing Redis
learnings.body: To invalidate a cache namespace across the cluster, bump the CACHE_EPOCH value in the service config rather than running FLUSHALL. A full flush on redis-shared-02 caused a 40 second brownout for unrelated tenants last spring. Epoch bumps only orphan the old keys, which expire on their own.

learnings.title: Keyset pagination on ledger_entries
learnings.body: OFFSET pagination on ledger_entries got slower as the table passed 1M rows, reaching over 3 seconds at deep pages. Switch to keyset pagination on (created_at, id) and pass the last seen tuple as the cursor. The ledger API v2 already does this, so only the legacy export endpoints still need migrating.

learnings.title: sync.Pool for report buffers
learnings.body: Report rendering in reportgen was allocating a fresh 64KB buffer per section. Wrapping the buffers in sync.Pool dropped alloc_space by about 2.1 GB per minute according to the pprof heap profile. Always Reset() the buffer before putting it back, or stale data leaks into the next report.

learnings.title: CDN immutable caching and purge latency
learnings.body: Static assets under /static/ are served with cache-control max-age 31536000 and immutable, so they should be versioned by filename hash. Purges through purgeline take around 40 seconds to reach all three POPs, which is slower than most people expect. Don't rely on purge for correctness during a deploy.

learnings.title: Sample-on-demand flag in production
learnings.body: The sample-on-demand flag enables 1 percent CPU profiling on a service in production. Leaving it at 100 percent or leaving it on for a full day adds about 8 percent CPU overhead. Turn it on, capture what you need, and turn it off in the same session using the flag's auto-expire of 20 minutes.

learnings.title: gRPC max message size and batch RPCs
learnings.body: The gRPC server limit on inventory-sync is 4MB per message. Batches above that size return RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, which the client often misreads as an upstream outage. Cap batch sizes at 2000 items in the client library, which keeps most payloads under 3MB.

learnings.title: Cursor pagination: never expose offset params on v2 collections
learnings.body: The v2 list endpoints use opaque cursors encoded by the `pagekit` library, and the `offset` query param is rejected with 400 `unsupported_param`. If you need to jump to a page, use the `after` cursor from the previous response instead. Default page size is 50 and the hard max is 200, so requests above that are silently clamped to 200.

learnings.title: Error envelope shape is fixed; add codes, never new top-level keys
learnings.body: All errors return `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}` as defined in the `errkit` schema. Clients on the mobile app parse only those three fields plus `request_ref`. Adding a top-level key broke the iOS build in March, so the `apilint` CI check now fails on any new top-level property in an error response.

learnings.title: PATCH semantics: absent means unchanged, explicit null means clear
learnings.body: Our PATCH handlers distinguish between a missing field and `null`, and the generated Go structs use `optional.Value[T]` to preserve that. If you send `"nickname": null` the field is cleared, but omitting it leaves the stored value alone. Several 2023 bugs came from people using plain pointers, which collapse both cases.

learnings.title: Idempotency-Key header keeps responses for 24 hours
learnings.body: POST endpoints on the orders service accept an `Idempotency-Key` header, and the gateway caches the first response for 24 hours in the `idem-cache` Redis cluster. Replays return the cached status and body with an extra `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header. Keys longer than 255 characters get a 400, and reusing a key with a different request body returns 422.

learnings.title: Dates in responses are RFC 3339 with explicit offset, always
learnings.body: Team decision from the API guild in January: every timestamp field is an RFC 3339 string with a numeric offset, such as `2024-03-11T09:30:00+00:00`, and we never send bare epoch integers in public APIs. Internal gRPC services can still use `google.protobuf.Timestamp`. The linter rule `time-format-rfc3339` flags any field whose name ends in `_at` but whose schema type is `integer`.

learnings.title: Field names are snake_case on the wire, camelCase only in the SDKs
learnings.body: The wire format uses snake_case for every property, including nested objects, and the SDK generator `rivet-gen` converts to camelCase when producing TypeScript and Kotlin clients. Do not hand-write camelCase keys in the JSON handlers because the Python SDK maps by exact name. The `naming` rule in `apilint` will catch any mixed-case property in the OpenAPI spec.

learnings.title: Deprecation: add Sunset header and Deprecation link at least 180 days out
learnings.body: When you deprecate an endpoint, add a `Deprecation: true` header and a `Sunset:` date that is at least 180 days in the future, and link the migration guide in a `Link` header with `rel="deprecation"`. The gateway dashboard in Grafana panel `API / Deprecated Traffic` shows which API keys still call the old path. Do not remove anything until that panel has been flat for two weeks.

learnings.title: Breaking-change check runs against the last released spec in schemaforge
learnings.body: The CI job `breaking-check` diffs your OpenAPI file against the last tagged release stored in `schemaforge`, and fails the PR on removed fields, narrowed enums, or new required request properties. To intentionally break something, add the label `api-major-approved` and get sign-off from someone in the API guild. The job takes about four minutes on a cold cache because it downloads every historical spec.

learnings.title: Collections return [] instead of 404 when the parent exists
learnings.body: If you request `/accounts/{id}/invoices` for a valid account with no invoices, the response is `200` with an empty `items` array, not a `404`. A 404 is reserved for the parent resource not existing. The support console depends on this distinction to show the 'no invoices yet' state, so changing it would show users a generic error page.

learnings.title: Bulk endpoints cap at 500 items and reject the whole batch on validation
learnings.body: Bulk create and bulk update endpoints accept at most 500 items per request and return `413 batch_too_large` above that. Validation is all-or-nothing: one bad item fails the entire batch with a 422 that lists every offending index under `details`. We chose this over 207 Multi-Status because the mobile client could not handle partial success responses cleanly.

learnings.title: Long-running operations return 202 with an operation resource
learnings.body: Any action that takes longer than two seconds, such as exports or report generation, should return `202 Accepted` with a `Location` header pointing to `/v1/operations/{id}`. The operations resource moves through `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, and `failed`, and the `result_url` field appears only on success. Polling should back off in the client; the server does not push updates.

learnings.title: Resource IDs carry a type prefix and are 26 characters
learnings.body: Every public ID is a prefixed ULID, for example `acc_01HZX3K9M2QWERTYUIOPASDFGH`, where the prefix identifies the resource type. The `idkit` package validates both the prefix and length on input, and it rejects IDs whose prefix does not match the endpoint, returning 404 rather than 400 to avoid leaking the existence of other resource types. Do not store the raw ULID without its prefix in the new billing tables.

learnings.title: Sorting uses a single sort param with a leading minus for descending
learnings.body: List endpoints accept `sort=created_at` for ascending and `sort=-created_at` for descending, and multiple fields are comma-separated, as in `sort=-priority,created_at`. Only fields listed in the resource's `sortable` annotation are allowed, and other values return 400 `invalid_sort`. The old `order_by` and `direction` params are gone from v2.

learnings.title: Sparse fieldsets via fields param, parsed by the shared gateway middleware
learnings.body: Clients can request a subset of properties with `fields=id,name,status`, and the gateway middleware strips the rest before serialization. Nested fields use dot notation such as `fields=owner.email`, which works on one level of nesting only. The middleware does not reduce the database query, so do not rely on it to speed up slow endpoints.

learnings.title: Enum values are lowercase snake_case and never change casing
learnings.body: Enum string values across public APIs are lowercase snake_case, for example `pending_review` and `auto_renewed`, and the server rejects uppercase variants on input. Last year the shipping service briefly returned `IN_TRANSIT` and three partner integrations broke within a day. If you need a new value, add it to the enum in the spec and the `enum-stability` check will flag any renames.

learnings.title: Trace IDs go in X-Request-Ref, not in custom X- headers per service
learnings.body: Every response carries an `X-Request-Ref` header whose value matches the `request_ref` field in error bodies, and support uses this value to search the `tracehound` dashboard. Services must not invent their own correlation headers such as `X-Corr-Id` because the gateway strips anything it does not recognize. If the incoming request has a valid `X-Request-Ref`, the gateway propagates it instead of generating a new one.

learnings.title: Nullable arrays are a lint error; return [] for empty
learnings.body: The API spec forbids `nullable: true` on array-typed properties, and the `apilint` rule `no-nullable-arrays` enforces this in CI. Clients written in Swift crash when they receive `null` where they expect a list, which is why the rule exists. If the data is genuinely absent, omit the field from the response and document that in the description.

learnings.title: Money fields are objects with amount string and currency code
learnings.body: Monetary values in public responses take the shape `{"amount": "19.99", "currency": "EUR"}` with the amount as a string, and the currency as an ISO 4217 code. Do not return raw numbers for money, because the TypeScript SDK parses numbers as floats. The `money` schema component in `commonspec` is the only approved definition; copy-pasting a local variant will be rejected in review.

learnings.title: Version lives in the path for public APIs, header for internal services
learnings.body: Public REST endpoints use `/v1/` and `/v2/` path prefixes, while internal services use the `Api-Version: 2024-06` header, which is validated by the `versionmw` middleware. Do not mix the two conventions within a single service because the docs generator assumes one or the other. Date-based header versions are pinned per API key in the admin console under `Compatibility`.

learnings.title: Search endpoints accept filter[field] syntax, not JSON bodies on GET
learnings.body: Filtering on collection endpoints uses bracket syntax, for example `filter[status]=open&filter[assignee_id]=usr_123`, and multiple values are comma-separated within the same bracket. The team tried JSON request bodies on GET in 2022 and several proxies dropped them, so that approach is banned. Complex queries that cannot be expressed this way should go through the `POST /v2/searches` resource instead.

learnings.title: Response size limit is 1 MB; use links for anything larger
learnings.body: The gateway truncates any response body over 1 MB and returns a 502 with `error.code = upstream_payload_too_large`, which is confusing to clients. For large documents, return a signed download link in the `download_url` field instead of embedding the content. The threshold was set after the invoice PDF incident in the storage team's postmortem last quarter.

learnings.title: Generated SDK version bumps happen on merge to main, not on release branch
learnings.body: When an OpenAPI change merges to `main`, the `sdkgen-publish` pipeline regenerates the Python, Go, and TypeScript clients and bumps their minor versions automatically. Release branches do not trigger regeneration, so a hotfix to the spec needs to be cherry-picked to main first. Check the `#sdk-releases` channel for the generated changelog before announcing anything to partners.

learnings.title: Boolean query params accept only true and false, lowercase
learnings.body: Query parameters like `include_archived=true` must be exactly `true` or `false` in lowercase, and any other value such as `1`, `yes`, or `TRUE` returns 400 `invalid_boolean`. This is enforced by the shared `querybind` package, which every service imports. If you need a tri-state filter, use a string enum instead of a boolean.

learnings.title: Reserved path segments: never use 'me' as a resource ID
learnings.body: The router treats `/users/me` as an alias for the authenticated user, so an actual user with ID `me` cannot be addressed and is not allowed to exist. Similarly, `search`, `bulk`, and `export` are reserved as sub-paths on every collection. The route registration helper `mountcollection()` throws at startup if a handler tries to claim one of these names.

learnings.title: Rate limit headers use the draft RateLimit fields, values in tenths of a second
learnings.body: Responses include `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, and `RateLimit-Reset` following the IETF draft field names, with the reset value expressed in seconds. The internal dashboard shows these values per API key, and the partner docs state that a limit of 600 means 600 requests per minute. Do not add the older `X-RateLimit-*` headers back, since two partners parse them and double-count the window.
