learnings.title: Partial updates to nested objects are not allowed; send the whole sub-object
learnings.body: PATCH on a nested object like `shipping_address` replaces the entire sub-object, not individual fields inside it. Sending `{"shipping_address": {"city": "Lyon"}}` will fail validation with `missing_required_field` for street and postal_code. This was intentional to avoid half-updated addresses, and the rule is documented in the `patch-semantics` section of the API handbook.

learnings.title: Webhook-free polling endpoints must return ETag and honor If-None-Match
learnings.body: Read endpoints that are polled by integrations must return an `ETag` header computed from the resource version, and respond with `304 Not Modified` when the client sends a matching `If-None-Match`. The CDN drops the 304 body automatically, so you only need to set the header correctly in the handler. Partners polling `/v1/inventory` cut their bandwidth by about 70 percent after this shipped in the August release.

learnings.title: Empty-string values in requests are normalized to null before validation
learnings.body: The request decoder in `reqnorm` converts any empty string `""` to `null` for optional fields before the schema runs, which means `"middle_name": ""` is treated the same as omitting it. This does not apply to required fields, which still reject empty strings with `422 blank_value`. Engineers new to the team often assume the reverse and write tests that send blank strings expecting a 400.

learnings.title: Heron sidecar truncates log lines over 16 KB
learnings.body: The Heron log shipper cuts any single log line above 16 KB and appends a '[truncated]' marker, which breaks JSON parsing in Quarry. Log a size and a hash for large payloads instead of the full body. If you must keep more, write the payload to the blob bucket and log its key.

learnings.title: WARN means a human should look within one working day
learnings.body: House rule from the on-call retro: WARN is for things that need attention by the next business day, and ERROR is reserved for failed user-facing operations. Anything that retries successfully and self-heals is INFO. Alerts should never be built on WARN counts alone, since the Watchtower rules for WARN are muted by default.

learnings.title: Trace header name and where it gets generated
learnings.body: The edge gateway generates the X-Trace-Ref header if the client did not send one, and every service must copy it into its log context field trace_ref. Do not rename it to request_id in new services, because the Quarry dashboards join on trace_ref. Missing trace_ref in a log line usually means the service was called from a cron job without the propagation middleware.

learnings.title: Prod debug logs are sampled 1 in 50 by default
learnings.body: In production, DEBUG lines are kept at a sample rate set by logSampleRate in the helm values, which defaults to 0.02. To turn full debug on for one pod while investigating, patch the pod annotation log.debug=full, and remember to remove it afterward. ERROR and WARN lines are never sampled.

learnings.title: Quarry retention tiers and how to extend them
learnings.body: Quarry keeps logs hot for 14 days and moves them to cold storage until 90 days, after which they are deleted. Audit-tagged logs stay 400 days in a separate index named audit-*. Requests to extend retention for a specific service go through a ticket to the data platform queue, not through a config change.

learnings.title: Go slog: wrapping errors loses the stack unless you use errs.Wrap
learnings.body: Calling slog.Error with err.Error() as a string discards the stack that our errs package attaches. Pass the error itself with slog.Any('err', err), and the Quarry formatter will expand the frames. Using fmt.Errorf with %w does not capture a stack, so use errs.Wrap for anything that crosses a service boundary.

learnings.title: logger.exception in a hot loop blew the daily quota
learnings.body: A retry loop in the ingest worker called logger.exception on every failed record, producing about 2,000 stack traces per second and exhausting the daily ingest quota by 10 a.m. Log once per batch with the failure count and call logger.exception only for the first failure in the batch. The quota limit is 40 GB per day per service.

learnings.title: Quarry query for errors grouped in five-minute buckets
learnings.body: A useful starting query in Quarry is: service:billing AND level:error | timeslice 5m | count by error_code. Adding the pipe clause with timeslice is faster than a dashboard panel for ad hoc triage. The default time range is the last hour, so widen it explicitly when checking deploys from earlier in the day.

learnings.title: Mask email addresses with libcommon.redact.maskmail
learnings.body: Do not log raw email addresses at any level. Use libcommon.redact.maskmail(), which keeps the first character of the local part and the full domain, so a@example.com becomes a***@example.com. A lint rule in CI flags log calls that pass variables named email or contact without this wrapper.

learnings.title: Fluent Bit multiline parser for Java stack traces
learnings.body: Java stack traces were splitting into one event per line until we enabled the trace_multiline parser in the fluent-bit config map. The parser joins lines that begin with a tab or the word Caused by into the previous event. If you add a new JVM service, add its log prefix to the parser's start_state regex or the traces will fragment again.

learnings.title: Logback async appender silently drops INFO when full
learnings.body: The Logback AsyncAppender in the reporting service has a queue of 8192 entries and discards INFO and DEBUG once the queue is at 80 percent capacity. This is intentional so that ERROR lines are not lost, but it means INFO counts in dashboards are lower than the true number during bursts. Raise queueSize only after checking heap impact, since each entry holds a reference to the MDC map.

learnings.title: pino redact paths for the Node services
learnings.body: Every Node service uses the shared pino config from @acme/log-base, which redacts req.headers.authorization, req.headers.cookie, and any key matching *.password or *.token. If you add a new secret-bearing field, extend the redact array in that package rather than in your service, because services that import the base config get the update on their next build. Redacted values print as [Redacted].

learnings.title: Frontend console.error only reaches Sentinel outside iframes
learnings.body: The Sentinel browser SDK captures console.error calls only when the page is the top-level window, so embedded widgets inside the partner iframe lose their errors. Use Sentinel.captureMessage directly from inside the widget, which posts to the parent through postMessage. Captured messages are rate-limited to 30 per page load.

learnings.title: Event names use dotted lowercase with a noun then verb
learnings.body: Event names in logs follow the pattern noun.verb.outcome, so invoice.sync.failed and invoice.sync.succeeded, never InvoiceSyncFailed or sync_error. The Quarry dashboards group by the first two segments automatically. Name new events in the PR description so the observability reviewer can check for collisions.

learnings.title: Timestamps must be UTC ISO 8601 with millisecond precision
learnings.body: All service logs must emit timestamps in UTC with a trailing Z and exactly three fractional digits, such as 2024-03-11T09:14:05.128Z. Quarry rejects lines with local offsets like +05:30 and drops them into the _unparsed index without an error in the service. Check the formatter setting time_format=rfc3339ms when adding a new logger.

learnings.title: qctl export limit and NDJSON format
learnings.body: To pull logs for an incident, run qctl export --service ledger --since 2h --format ndjson > out.ndjson. The export is capped at one million lines, and anything beyond that is silently truncated, so narrow the level or service filter if you hit the cap. The file is written to your home directory on the bastion and is removed after 24 hours.

learnings.title: Audit events go to a separate Kafka topic, not stdout
learnings.body: Security-relevant actions such as role changes, data exports, and admin logins must be published to the audit.events topic using the audit client, not written as log lines. Stdout logs are sampled and rotated, and audit records must not be. Retention on that topic is seven years, and the schema is versioned in the audit-schemas repo.

learnings.title: Watchtower alert on log pattern count
learnings.body: To alert on a log pattern, create a Watchtower rule with a Quarry query and a threshold, for example more than 25 matches of payment.capture.timeout in 10 minutes. Rules that match on message text instead of event name break whenever someone edits the string, so always match on the event field. Test the rule with wt-rule dry-run before saving it.

learnings.title: Bastion logrotate settings for the batch host
learnings.body: The batch host rotates /var/log/batch/*.log daily and keeps 10 compressed copies, set in /etc/logrotate.d/batch. The copytruncate option is required because the batch jobs hold the file open and do not reopen it on SIGHUP. If a job's log is missing from the archive, check whether it was started with a non-default log directory.

learnings.title: Skip health check paths in access logs
learnings.body: Access logs for /healthz and /readyz are excluded by the ACCESS_LOG_SKIP_PATHS setting, which takes a comma-separated list of paths. The default list already covers those two, so only add to it if a new probe path appears in the load balancer config. Do not skip anything under /api, since those are needed for billing reconciliation.

learnings.title: pytest caplog misses logs from the worker library
learnings.body: When a test asserts on log output and caplog comes back empty, the cause is usually that the worker library sets propagate to False on its logger. Fix it in the test by using the caplog_for fixture from tests/conftest.py, which temporarily re-enables propagation for the named logger. Adding caplog.set_level alone will not help in this case.

learnings.title: Silencing a noisy logger in the sidecar config
learnings.body: To silence a noisy logger without a code change, add an entry to the logfilter block in the sidecar values with the logger name and a minimum level. The filter applies at the shipper, so the lines still count against the local disk buffer but not against Quarry quota. Never add a filter for ERROR, because the lint job will reject the PR.

learnings.title: Mobile crash logs flush on app background
learnings.body: The mobile SDK batches crash and breadcrumb logs in groups of 50 and flushes them when the app moves to the background or when the batch fills. If a user force-quits, unflushed entries from the last 30 seconds are lost, which is why crash rates look lower on iOS than the server-side counts. Set the flushOnBackground flag to true in the release config to reduce the gap.

learnings.title: Notebook logs in analysis workspace via nblog.setup
learnings.body: Analysts should call nblog.setup(project='churn-model') at the top of any notebook that runs a scheduled job, which writes structured logs to the analysis bucket under logs/notebooks/. Plain print statements are not captured by the scheduler, so the run appears successful with no output. The setup call is idempotent, so it is safe to leave in shared templates.

learnings.title: Verified answer: why ERROR logs appear twice in Quarry
learnings.body: If a single error shows up twice with the same trace_ref, the service is probably logging it in both the handler and the outer middleware. This was confirmed in the orders service during the March cleanup, where the middleware re-logged any exception it rethrew. The fix is to log at the boundary only and let inner layers raise without logging.

learnings.title: Retain structured fields, not concatenated strings
learnings.body: Pass values as separate fields such as user_id=42 and dur_ms=318, never interpolated into the message string, because Quarry indexes fields but only does substring search on messages. The common mistake is writing 'processed order 123 in 318ms', which cannot be aggregated later. Use dur_ms for durations in milliseconds, not duration or elapsed.

learnings.title: PagerLoop secondary escalation fires after 90s, not 5 minutes
learnings.body: The escalation policy 'core-api-tier1' pages the secondary only if the primary has not acknowledged within 90 seconds, which is shorter than the 5 minutes listed in the old wiki. The delay is under Escalation > Step 2 > Delay. Changing it requires sign-off from the SRE lead in #sre-policy.

learnings.title: Rollback checkout to last green build with deployctl
learnings.body: Run `deployctl rollback --service checkout --to-last-green --confirm` to revert. Omitting --to-last-green makes it roll back one release, which can land on a build that never passed canary. Verify with `deployctl status checkout` before closing the incident.

learnings.title: pg-failover-check refuses to run when replica lag exceeds 30s
learnings.body: Q: Why does pg-failover-check exit with code 4 during an outage? A: It's a safety guard: any replica lagging more than 30 seconds is excluded and the tool won't promote it. Check lag with `pgmon lag --all` and wait for it to drop, or pass --accept-lag 120 with incident commander approval logged in the ticket.

learnings.title: Postmortem template PM-lite is only for SEV3 incidents
learnings.body: SEV1 and SEV2 incidents must use the full 'PM-Full' template in Inkwell, which requires a contributing-factors section and an action-item owner for every item. PM-lite is fine for SEV3 but has no slot for customer impact numbers, so don't use it for anything customer-facing. Create the doc from `/inkwell new pm-full` in the incident channel.

learnings.title: SEV2 needs an incident commander named within 15 minutes
learnings.body: Per the severity policy, any SEV2 declared without an incident commander named in the channel within 15 minutes gets auto-escalated to the duty manager by the Beacon bot. Name yourself with `/ic me` in the incident channel. Don't leave it blank while you're debugging, because the bot doesn't know the difference.

learnings.title: Lumberyard queries over 60 days time out without an index hint
learnings.body: Searches spanning more than 60 days of logs in Lumberyard hit the 60-second timeout unless you add `USE INDEX(svc_ts)` to the query. The default index is per-day and scans everything when the range is wide. For incident forensics, scope by service first, which usually brings it under 10 seconds.

learnings.title: Grafana checkout-golden 'p99 auth' panel averages across regions
learnings.body: The 'p99 auth' panel on the checkout-golden dashboard shows the mean of the per-region p99 values, not the true global p99, so it can look fine while eu-west is burning. Use the 'p99 auth (global)' panel added in March, which computes from the merged histogram. Don't quote the old panel in status updates.

learnings.title: Flag flips in ff-kill-core take around 45 seconds to propagate
learnings.body: Changes to the ff-kill-core flagset propagate to all edge nodes in roughly 45 seconds. Flipping the same flag back within that window confuses the propagation log and makes it hard to tell which state each node ended in. Wait for the 'converged' event in #flags-ops before flipping again.

learnings.title: Don't send macro INC-07 to customers before comms approval
learnings.body: INC-07 is the customer macro for active outages and it goes out through Zendesk immediately when inserted. It must not be sent until the status page has the incident posted and comms lead has approved the wording in #incident-comms. Sending early has caused contradictory answers twice this year.

learnings.title: Use the incident-update template with ETA left blank
learnings.body: When you post an update in Statusbay, use the 'incident-update' template and leave the ETA field empty if you don't have a confirmed time. Writing 'we expect resolution within the hour' with no basis has repeatedly been cited in customer complaints. Put 'Investigating, next update in 30 minutes' instead.

learnings.title: Drain orders-retry queue in batches with queuectl
learnings.body: To drain the stuck orders-retry queue without spiking the database, run `queuectl drain orders-retry --batch 500 --pause-ms 200`. Larger batches caused connection pool exhaustion during the March incident. Monitor the 'orders_db_conns' panel and stop if it passes 80 percent.

learnings.title: Wildcard certs are silently skipped by the vault-int-ca renewal job
learnings.body: The nightly renewal job for vault-int-ca certificates skips any wildcard certificate and logs nothing at warn level. Check expiry with `certwatch list --wildcard --expiring 30d` every Monday. The next wildcard expiring is *.corp.internal on the 14th, so renew it manually via `vaultctl issue`.

learnings.title: api.internal DNS TTL is 300s, so plan 10 minutes for failover
learnings.body: The Route53 record for api.internal has a TTL of 300 seconds, and some resolvers ignore it and cache longer. When failing over to the secondary region, allow 10 minutes before declaring the switch complete. Confirm with `dig +short api.internal @8.8.8.8` and another public resolver.

learnings.title: Draining gpu-b node pool needs two extra kubectl flags
learnings.body: Draining nodes in the gpu-b pool fails without `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`, because the training sidecars use emptyDir scratch space. Use `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120`. Expect the ML jobs to be rescheduled but not resumed, so notify the ml-platform on-call first.

learnings.title: Quietwire silences expire at midnight UTC, not local time
learnings.body: A silence created in Quietwire with 'until midnight' ends at 00:00 UTC, which for the Pacific team is mid-afternoon. Several overnight pages were missed after a silence was set for the evening shift. Always set silences with an explicit UTC timestamp or a duration like `2h`.

learnings.title: fct_orders_hourly lags up to 2 hours during incidents
learnings.body: During an incident the warehouse table fct_orders_hourly can lag two hours behind real time because the ingest job deprioritizes itself under load. Analysts pulling order counts for impact estimates should use `raw_orders_stream` instead, which is near real time. Note the source in the impact section of the postmortem.

learnings.title: Expedited iOS hotfix review goes through release-ops form
learnings.body: For an iOS hotfix that needs faster App Store review, file the expedite request through the release-ops intake form and tag it with the incident ID. Review is usually 24 hours but that is not guaranteed, and requests without a crash-rate graph attached are deprioritized. Don't email the App Store reviewer directly, since that has gotten the account flagged once.

learnings.title: Rotate team secrets with secretsmith before anything else on suspected leak
learnings.body: If you suspect a credential leak, run `secretsmith rotate --scope team --reason <incident-id>` as the first step, before investigating how it leaked. Then post in #security-ir with the rotation receipt. Rotation invalidates old tokens immediately, so warn the payments on-call that jobs will fail for about two minutes.

learnings.title: Inkwell timeline must be in UTC; Slack bot converts DST wrong
learnings.body: The Beacon timeline importer assumes Slack timestamps are UTC, but the bot reads local display times and converts them incorrectly across DST changes. In the last two postmortems, timeline entries were shifted by an hour. Enter timeline times manually in UTC in Inkwell, or paste the Slack permalink and double-check.

learnings.title: Incident channel names are inc-YYYYMMDD-slug and cap at 30 characters
learnings.body: Running `/incident start` creates a channel named inc-YYYYMMDD-slug, and the slug is truncated to 30 characters without warning. If two incidents start on the same day with similar slugs, the second one fails silently. Pick a short distinctive slug such as `cart-latency` or `auth-502s`.

learnings.title: Shed lowpri traffic only at the gateway, never on search
learnings.body: The load-shedding flag 'lowpri' drops tier-3 traffic at the API gateway. It must not be enabled on the search cluster, because the search tier reads its own priority header and will shed the wrong requests, causing an empty results page. Enable with `shedctl enable lowpri --scope gateway`.

learnings.title: Why cache flushes cause 502s: edge keeps idle connections 75s
learnings.body: Verified cause for the recurring 502s after cache flushes: the edge proxy keeps idle upstream connections for 75 seconds, while the origin cache layer closes them after 60. Requests that reuse a connection in that gap get reset. The fix is to flush with `cachectl flush --drain-conns` which waits for the edge to close its pool first.

learnings.title: Redis shard failover via redisctl, never by restarting nodes
learnings.body: To fail over a Redis shard, use `redisctl failover --shard <name>` so the cluster promotes a replica cleanly. Restarting nodes by hand has caused split-brain twice, leaving stale session data. After failover, check `redisctl topology` shows exactly one master per shard.

learnings.title: Chaos drills pause during real incidents: pause gremlin-lite
learnings.body: The weekly chaos drill runs Thursdays at 14:00 PT using gremlin-lite. If a real incident is open, the drill must be paused with `gremlin-lite pause --all --reason inc` so it doesn't add noise to the investigation. Resume only after the incident commander says so in the channel.

learnings.title: Book IR reviews from the 'IR Review (60m)' calendar template
learnings.body: Schedule post-incident reviews using the 'IR Review (60m)' calendar template so the Inkwell link, the timeline doc, and the action-item tracker are attached automatically. Reviews booked from a blank invite have lost the links and delayed follow-ups. Invite the incident commander and at least one person from the affected team.

learnings.title: On-call handover notes go in the Handover tool, not Slack DMs
learnings.body: At the end of an on-call shift, write the handover in the Handover tool using the 'shift-handoff' template, listing open incidents, muted alerts, and pending deploys. Handovers sent as Slack DMs were missed twice when the on-call rotated. The incoming engineer must acknowledge the handover in the tool before the outgoing one logs off.

learnings.title: VendorDesk: vendor record needs a legal entity ID before PO approval
learnings.body: POs for new vendors bounce with 'missing legal entity' if the vendor record in VendorDesk has no registration number. Pull the number from the W-9 or the vendor's registry extract, not from the website footer, since the footer is often a trading name. Once the field is filled, the PO re-routes automatically and you don't need to resubmit.

learnings.title: SOC 2 bridge letter: ask the vendor 45 days before our audit window closes
learnings.body: Vendors whose SOC 2 Type II period ends before ours need a bridge letter covering the gap. Most vendors take 2 to 3 weeks to produce one, so start the request early. Send it through the trust portal under 'Request Bridge Letter' and log the ticket in SEC-GRC.

learnings.title: Lumen Analytics seat true-ups run on the contract anniversary, not calendar year
learnings.body: Our Lumen contract bills seat true-ups on the anniversary date (March 14), so adding seats in January means we pay for them at the next true-up, not immediately. Reducing seats mid-term is not allowed until renewal. Check the seat count in the Lumen admin console the week before the anniversary.

learnings.title: Run vendorscan diff before accepting a sub-processor change notice
learnings.body: When a vendor emails about new sub-processors, don't just skim the PDF. Run `vendorscan diff --vendor <slug> --from last-approved` to get a line-by-line comparison against the list we signed off on. Anything new in the output goes to the privacy review queue before we reply.

learnings.title: Invoice matching tolerance for Corvane Cloud is 2 percent on usage lines
learnings.body: The three-way match in Ledgerline flags Corvane invoices when actual usage differs from the PO by more than 2 percent. Corvane bills in arrears and usage often lands a few days after month close, so the first invoice of each month almost always flags. Use the 'accrual adjust' button rather than editing the PO.

learnings.title: SLA credit claims must be filed within 30 days of the incident
learnings.body: Brightpath's SLA credit form has a hard 30-day window from the incident date, and they will deny claims filed after that without discussion. Keep a copy of the status page history since they only give credits against what they logged themselves. The claim form lives under Support > Billing > Credits in their portal.

learnings.title: Brightpath SMS sandbox key quietly expired after 90 days
learnings.body: The Brightpath sandbox API key stopped working on a Tuesday with a generic 401 and no email warning. The key lifetime is 90 days and the rotation reminder goes to the original signer, who had left. Rotate with `bp keys rotate --env sandbox` and update the secret in Vault path kv/integrations/brightpath.

learnings.title: Renewal notice periods are tracked in the contracts sheet, column H
learnings.body: Auto-renew contracts need notice of non-renewal anywhere from 30 to 120 days ahead, and the number varies by vendor. Column H of the Contracts Register shows the deadline already computed from the effective date and notice period. Procurement sets a reminder at 45 days before whichever date comes first.

learnings.title: Halvard Maps v1 API sunsets 2025-03-31
learnings.body: Halvard has confirmed that v1 endpoints return 410 Gone after March 31. The migration guide says v2 changes the tile URL structure, so the static tile cache in our CDN config needs a new origin rule. Owner for the migration is the maps squad, with a tracking ticket under PLAT-2291.

learnings.title: New vendors with production data access need a pen test summary first
learnings.body: The security intake checklist requires a pen test summary dated within the last 12 months before any vendor gets production data access. A marketing one-pager does not count, and neither does a self-attestation form. If the vendor only has an internal report, ask for the executive summary, which they are usually willing to share under NDA.

learnings.title: Tessellate CDN purge takes up to 90 seconds; use surrogate keys instead
learnings.body: Full-zone purges on Tessellate took a minute and a half in staging, which is long enough to serve stale assets to a noticeable slice of users. Tag responses with the Surrogate-Key header and purge by tag with `tess purge --tag catalog-v3`. That returns in under 5 seconds in our tests.

learnings.title: Vendor risk tiers decide review cadence
learnings.body: Tier 1 vendors are anything touching customer PII or payment flows, and they get a full reassessment every 12 months. Tier 2 covers internal tooling with no customer data and gets reviewed every 24 months. Tier assignments are in the risk register, and changes need sign-off from the security lead.

learnings.title: ProcureLoop: use 'Request Exception' when a vendor isn't on the approved list
learnings.body: If you need a tool that isn't on the approved vendor list, don't email procurement directly. Open ProcureLoop, choose 'Request Exception', and attach the business case and the vendor's security packet. Exceptions are reviewed on Thursdays, so anything submitted after Wednesday noon waits a week.

learnings.title: Uptime credits exclude maintenance windows posted at least 72 hours ahead
learnings.body: Orbitline's contract excludes scheduled maintenance from the uptime calculation as long as they post it on the status page 72 hours in advance. Last quarter, two windows were posted with only 48 hours' notice, and we successfully argued for those to count. Export the status page history as CSV before disputing, since their dashboard hides older entries.

learnings.title: Security questionnaire intake goes to the shared inbox, not individuals
learnings.body: Vendor security questionnaires should go to sec-vendor-intake, which auto-creates a tracking issue in the GRC board. Answering from a personal inbox means nobody else knows the question was handled. The answer library is in the Trust Center folder, and the newest approved answers are marked with a green tag.

learnings.title: DPA redline template v4.2 is the only approved version
learnings.body: Earlier DPA redlines circulated in the drive, including v3.8 and v4.0, still have clauses that conflict with our current subprocessor notice terms. Use only v4.2 from the Legal templates folder. If a vendor insists on their own DPA, route it to legal with the diff against v4.2 attached.

learnings.title: LogGantry bills per ingested GB, so filter noisy sources first
learnings.body: Our LogGantry bill jumped 40 percent after the load balancer started emitting debug logs in production. Add an exclusion rule in the gantry console under Ingest > Filters, or ship the filter via `gantry filter apply --file filters/lb.yaml`. Check the 'ingest by source' panel on the cost dashboard each Monday.

learnings.title: Vendor offboarding checklist: revoke, rotate, certify
learnings.body: When a vendor contract ends, revoke their SSO app assignment in Okta first so no one can log in during the wind-down. Rotate any shared secrets they held, which are listed in the vendor's row in the secrets inventory. Request a data deletion certificate within 30 days, and file it under Vendors/Offboarding in the compliance drive.

learnings.title: Duplicate vendor records: merge with vmerge, never delete
learnings.body: Deleting a duplicate vendor record in VendorDesk breaks the PO history for the removed copy. Use `vmerge --source VND-1182 --target VND-0457` instead, which moves open POs and invoices to the surviving record. The merge log is written to the audit table, so you can reverse it within 7 days if needed.

learnings.title: Reference call script for prospective vendors
learnings.body: Ask every reference the same three questions: how did they handle the first outage, how fast did the support team respond to a Severity 1, and would they sign again. Record answers in the vendor evaluation sheet under the matching column. Skip questions about pricing, since references are usually not allowed to discuss it.

learnings.title: Orbitline Severity 1 requires a phone call, not a ticket
learnings.body: Orbitline's support portal accepts Severity 1 tickets, but they only start the response clock after a phone call to their emergency line. The number is in the runbook at the top of the vendor wiki page. Ask for the incident bridge ID on the call and paste it into the ticket so it can be linked later.

learnings.title: Pelion egress spikes: check the 'egress by bucket' panel first
learnings.body: When the Pelion invoice jumps, the cause is almost always one bucket serving public downloads without a cache. Open the Pelion cost dashboard and look at the 'egress by bucket' panel for the last 30 days. Turning on the cache rule for that bucket usually cuts egress by more than half within a week.

learnings.title: Signatory matrix: VP sign-off above $50k annual value
learnings.body: Any vendor contract above $50,000 in annual value needs a VP signature, even if the department head approved it. Contracts between $10,000 and $50,000 require a director. Anything below $10,000 can be signed by the budget owner, provided it's logged in the contracts register.

learnings.title: Quarterly vendor scorecard weights are 40/30/20/10
learnings.body: The scorecard weights reliability at 40 percent, support responsiveness at 30 percent, price-to-value at 20 percent, and security posture at 10 percent. The weights were agreed after last year's review and shouldn't be changed mid-year. Enter raw scores in the Scorecards sheet and the weighted total will compute itself.

learnings.title: Two teams want the same tool? Escalate to #vendor-council
learnings.body: When two squads ask for competing tools in the same category, don't let each buy one. Post in #vendor-council with both business cases and the vendor names, and the council will decide within 10 business days. Duplicate purchases have caused two of the last three license audits, so this rule exists for a reason.

learnings.title: Badge reader on 3rd floor east stairwell needs two taps
learnings.body: The reader at the east stairwell door on floor 3 (listed as RDR-3E in the Brivo console) drops the first tap after sitting idle. Tap once, wait for the amber LED, then tap again. Facilities ticket FAC-2291 is open with the vendor, so log any further failures in that ticket. Don't prop the door with a chair, because the door alarm pages the security on-call.

learnings.title: Juniper room display only wakes on HDMI port 2
learnings.body: Meeting room Juniper's wall display ignores input 1 because the cable there is a passive extender that doesn't pass the handshake. Plug the laptop into port 2 and the display wakes automatically. If it still shows no signal, unplug the power at the wall box for 30 seconds, not the display itself.

learnings.title: How to reimage a laptop from the Ferrum netboot console
learnings.body: 1. Hold Option at boot and select the Ferrum NetBoot entry. 2. Log in with your IT admin account, then pick the image 'std-dev-2024Q3' and set the hostname before the disk wipe starts. 3. The full reimage takes about 40 minutes on the wired dock; wireless is too slow and often fails the checksum step.

learnings.title: Q: Why do Okta push prompts not reach my Pixel?
learnings.body: Q: Okta push fails silently on Pixel phones after the Android 14 update. A: Turn off battery optimisation for the Okta Verify app under Settings > Apps, then re-enroll the device in the Okta dashboard under Security Methods. Verified on three devices in the April test batch.

learnings.title: Floor 2 HP printer resets to single-sided after firmware 4.11
learnings.body: After the firmware update on HP-LJ-27 (floor 2 copy room), duplex printing defaults back to off on every job from the Windows print queue. The fix is to set the default in the device web page under Printing > Default Options, not in the driver. Ask IT to push the change to the print server template so it sticks for everyone.

learnings.title: Tessera VPN split tunnel covers the lab subnet only
learnings.body: Tessera VPN is configured with split tunnelling so only 10.44.0.0/16 and the lab hosts go through the tunnel. Everything else, including Slack and Google Docs, goes direct, which is intentional. If you need the internal wiki from home, make sure wiki.corp.example is in the list shown under Settings > Routes.

learnings.title: Vault shared folder naming for vendor credentials
learnings.body: Vendor logins live in the shared Vault folder 'Vendors / <vendor-name> / <env>', for example 'Vendors / Crestline / staging'. Never put a personal account in a vendor folder, since offboarding only revokes the shared owner. Anyone who adds a new vendor folder should add the security-review group as a viewer.

learnings.title: Lanternguest wifi passphrase rotates on the first Monday
learnings.body: The guest network Lantern-Guest rotates its passphrase at 08:00 on the first Monday of each month. The new one is posted on the lobby screen and sent to all team leads by the IT bot. Visitors who connect after the change will hit the captive portal, so have them check in at reception first.

learnings.title: Calendr auto-releases unclaimed room holds after 10 minutes
learnings.body: Rooms booked in Calendr through the 'Hold' option are released automatically if nobody checks in within 10 minutes. Check-in means tapping the room tablet or scanning the QR code on the door. Holds you need to keep past that window should be converted to a regular booking.

learnings.title: Harbor NAS restore test runs Sunday 02:00
learnings.body: The Harbor NAS restore test runs every Sunday at 02:00 and restores a random 50 GB sample to the /restore-test scratch volume. Don't schedule maintenance on that NAS for that window, because the job will fail and page the infra on-call. The result shows up in the #backups channel as a green or red summary.

learnings.title: Use the @it-bot reset-timeout command for stuck laptops
learnings.body: If a laptop's login is locked after too many failed PIN attempts, message @it-bot with 'reset-timeout <hostname>' in the #helpdesk channel. The bot clears the lockout for 15 minutes and posts a confirmation. Do not use it on shared kiosk machines, because those need a ticket to the kiosk team.

learnings.title: Floor 4 parcels go to locker bank B via Parcelhub
learnings.body: Courier parcels addressed to floor 4 are scanned into Parcelhub and left in locker bank B by the mail room. The pickup code arrives by email from noreply at parcelhub, usually within an hour of delivery. Lockers are cleared every Friday at 17:00, so anything still there after that is moved to the mail room shelf.

learnings.title: Quillon intermediate CA renewal steps
learnings.body: The Quillon intermediate CA used for internal TLS expires in March and must be renewed about 60 days early. Run 'certctl renew --ca quillon-int --days 825' from the bastion host, then push the new chain to the load balancers with the rollout job. Double check the chain with 'certctl verify' before anything gets switched over.

learnings.title: Fleetwise blocks Docker Desktop unless approved
learnings.body: Docker Desktop is blocked on managed Macs by the Fleetwise profile 'Dev-Mac-Standard' unless you're in the containers group. Request membership in Access Hub under 'Developer Tools', and the approval usually lands within one business day. Colima is allowed without approval if you need a local runtime right away.

learnings.title: git.lumen.internal only resolves on the VPN
learnings.body: The hostname git.lumen.internal is served by internal DNS only, so it fails with NXDOMAIN off the VPN. Don't add a public DNS record for it, since the security team flagged that during the last audit. If you're travelling and need the repo, connect to Tessera VPN first, then run 'git pull' as usual.

learnings.title: New-hire laptops must be ordered three business days early
learnings.body: Order the laptop for a new hire through Procure at least three business days before their start date, otherwise it won't arrive in time for day-one setup. Choose the 'Standard Engineer' bundle, which includes the dock and monitor. The onboarding checklist in People Hub has a reminder that fires automatically at T minus five days.

learnings.title: Deskly hot-desk reservations clear at midnight
learnings.body: Hot-desk bookings in Deskly expire automatically at midnight on the day they were made, so there's no point booking a desk for the following week more than once. Desks on floor 3 north are only bookable by the platform team on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Desk sensors show a green dot when the desk is free, which is a faster check than the app.

learnings.title: Dashline seats are reclaimed after 30 days idle
learnings.body: Analyst seats in Dashline are reclaimed automatically once a user has been inactive for 30 days, and the user loses saved dashboards only if they're not shared. To restore a seat, ask IT to raise a ticket in the BI queue within seven days. After that the seat goes back to the pool and the dashboards get archived to the cold bucket.

learnings.title: Bean-to-cup kitchen machine shows E4 when the descale is due
learnings.body: The bean-to-cup machine in kitchen 2 shows error code E4 when it needs descaling, even though the water is fine. Run the descale cycle with the blue tablet kept in the cupboard above the sink, which takes about 25 minutes. Log the date on the sticker inside the door so the next person knows when it was last done.

learnings.title: Visitor parking permits must be printed the day before
learnings.body: Visitor parking passes are issued through Parkwise and need to be created the day before the visit, because the gate reads the plate from the booking. Print from the front-desk printer, not the one on floor 2, since only the front-desk machine has the permit template loaded. Passes expire at 18:00 on the visit date.

learnings.title: Scan-to-email relays through scan-relay on port 587
learnings.body: Multifunction scanners send scans to email via scan-relay.corp.example on port 587 with STARTTLS. Scans sent to external addresses are dropped by design, so use Drive links instead for anything going to customers. If a scanner stops sending, check that its service account isn't locked in the directory, which is the cause most of the time.

learnings.title: macOS fleet auto-locks after 10 minutes idle
learnings.body: Fleetwise enforces a 10-minute screen lock on all managed Macs, and the setting cannot be overridden locally. Linux dev boxes use loginctl lock-session on idle instead, which is set in the dotfiles repo under the 'desktop' profile. If you're presenting and the screen keeps locking, use the Caffeine setting from Self Service, which is allowed for up to two hours.

learnings.title: Team folder quota is 500 GB; media goes to Vault Archive
learnings.body: Each team folder in Drive has a hard quota of 500 GB, and uploads will start failing with a quota error after that. Large video and raw camera files should go to the Vault Archive bucket, which has no quota but is slower to retrieve. Ask IT to move a folder to the archive tier rather than deleting anything, so the audit trail stays intact.

learnings.title: Hive room Zoom camera needs a power cycle at the ceiling box
learnings.body: When the camera in Hive room disappears from Zoom Rooms, the USB hub in the ceiling box has usually crashed. Power cycle it by unplugging the grey 12V brick at the box for 20 seconds, then reboot the Zoom Rooms controller. Don't unplug the HDMI cable at the table, because that just drops the display signal and makes things look worse.

learnings.title: P2 tickets are for when more than five people are blocked
learnings.body: Helpdesk tickets are rated P2 only if more than five people are blocked or a customer-facing system is down, otherwise they're P3. P1 is reserved for outages that page the on-call rotation directly. Tickets marked P2 for a single person get bumped back to P3 by the queue triage bot, so set the priority correctly the first time.

learnings.title: Power BI gateway service account rotates first Tuesday
learnings.body: The Power BI gateway service account svc-pbi-gw has its password rotated on the first Tuesday of each month, and the gateway goes offline for about five minutes during the change. Schedule refreshes shouldn't be set between 06:00 and 06:30 on that day, or they'll fail with an authentication error. The new credential is pulled from Vault automatically, so nobody needs to update it by hand.

learnings.title: Old APNs tokens linger after reinstall; tokensweep prunes them
learnings.body: When a user reinstalls the iOS app, APNs issues a new device token and the old one starts returning 410 Unregistered. The tokensweep cron job (runs daily at 03:10 UTC) deletes a token after two consecutive 410 responses. Don't hand-delete rows in device_tokens, because the sweep uses the failure counter and you'll break its bookkeeping.

learnings.title: Use priority high only for time-sensitive alerts on Android
learnings.body: FCM messages sent at normal priority get batched by Doze, and we measured 25 to 45 minute delays on Pixel 6 test devices in staging. Set priority: high in pushgate only for categories flagged time_sensitive=true, such as delivery arrival and 2FA codes. Marketing and digests should stay normal.

learnings.title: Silent pushes are capped at 2 per device per hour
learnings.body: iOS silently drops content-available pushes once an app exceeds its background budget, and the drops look like delivery success on our side. pushgate enforces silent_max_per_hour: 2 per device in config/pushgate.prod.yaml. If a feature needs more frequent background refresh, it should poll on foreground instead.

learnings.title: Rotating the APNs .p8 key: canary first, then kid update
learnings.body: Upload the new .p8 to vault at secret/mobile/apns/prod and bump the key id (kid) in pushgate's apns block. Deploy to the canary pool (pushgate-canary-1 and -2) and send a test to the qa-push-pool group before the full rollout. Keep the old key active for 24 hours so in-flight sends using the old kid don't fail.

learnings.title: Badge counts drift when users read on web
learnings.body: The badge number we send is computed at dispatch time from the unread_count view, but a read on web doesn't push a badge reset to the device. Result: phantom badges on iOS until the next push arrives. The fix is the badge_sync flag, which sends a silent badge-only update on web read events, and it is on for accounts created after March.

learnings.title: Android 8+ drops notifications sent to channels that don't exist yet
learnings.body: If the payload's channel_id isn't registered on the device, Android silently discards the notification with no error callback. Channels must be created client-side at app start, and orders_v2 was missing from builds before 4.11. Check the logcat tag NotificationService for 'No Channel found' when debugging.

learnings.title: Lantern counts 'received' not 'delivered' for push metrics
learnings.body: The provider's delivered number only means the message reached Google or Apple, not the device. Lantern's push panels use client acks (the push_received event) as the denominator instead. If you see a gap of more than 15 percent between delivered and received, check whether the app's ack handler is running in the notification service extension.

learnings.title: Q: Why don't our alerts break through iOS Focus mode?
learnings.body: Focus mode suppresses everything unless the notification has interruption level time-sensitive or the user allowlisted the app. Time-sensitive requires the com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive entitlement, which we have had since app 4.12. Set interruptionLevel to 'time-sensitive' in the payload only for the categories listed in the push policy doc.

learnings.title: Test sends must use the qa-push-pool group, never prod audiences
learnings.body: dispatch in staging has an allowlist, but it only covers user IDs, so a prod audience pasted into a staging campaign will still go to real customers if the allowlist is turned off. Use the qa-push-pool group (six test accounts with physical devices) for every manual send. The ops checklist requires a screenshot of the target audience count before any send.

learnings.title: Deep links must use the deeplink key, not url
learnings.body: The payload field named url is ignored by the iOS and Android handlers since the 2023 refactor, so taps open the app home screen instead of the target. Use deeplink with a value like acme://orders/88213. The Android handler also expects the scheme to be registered in AndroidManifest, so new schemes need a manifest change.

learnings.title: APNs payload limit is 4KB; notifyctl truncates bodies at 178 chars
learnings.body: Even though APNs allows 4KB total, the lock screen truncates bodies around 178 characters on most devices, and longer text hides the important part. notifyctl enforces the 178-character limit by default and logs a warning with the template name. Use --allow-long only for rich notifications that show an expanded view.

learnings.title: Send localized pushes with loc-key and args, not rendered strings
learnings.body: Render-time strings are locked to whatever language the server had when it built the message, which is wrong for users who changed their device language. Use loc-key and loc-args, with keys defined in i18n/push_keys.json. A missing key falls back to English silently, so run `notifyctl lint-keys` before merging any new template.

learnings.title: Support check before escalating 'I stopped getting pushes'
learnings.body: Look up the user in tokenbank first, because roughly 80 percent of these cases are OS-level permission being off. The os_permission field shows 'denied' or 'provisional' for those users, and the fix is a pointer to Settings. Only escalate to mobile if os_permission is 'granted' and the token shows 410 failures.

learnings.title: Push opens are double-counted without open_id dedupe
learnings.body: When a notification launches a cold app, both the notification-open callback and the app-launch analytics event fire, which inflates open counts by about 12 percent. Every outbound payload includes an open_id, and Lantern dedupes opens with the same open_id within a 60-second window. Don't count opens from raw event logs directly.

learnings.title: Use the staging Firebase project for debug builds only
learnings.body: The google-services.json in the repo is for the prod Firebase project, and debug builds that accidentally ship with it will register device tokens against production. Use the debug flavor, which points to the acme-staging project, and check the applicationId suffix .dev before running on a shared device. The build script fails if the project_id doesn't match the flavor.

learnings.title: Scheduled pushes need jitter to avoid the top-of-hour spike
learnings.body: Campaigns scheduled for 09:00 used to send all at once, which caused queue backlog and a 4-minute median delay in the Hermes queue. Set jitter_seconds in the campaign config to spread sends over a window, 90 seconds is the standard for daily digests. Cron-triggered sends from the scheduler should always have jitter enabled.

learnings.title: Dry-run command for template changes
learnings.body: Run `notifyctl send --env staging --token <device_token> --template order_shipped --dry-run` to render the full payload without sending it. The output includes the final loc-args, channel_id, and deeplink, which is what most template bugs turn out to be. Dry-run doesn't hit APNs or FCM, so it's safe to use on prod tokens.

learnings.title: Notification service extension has about 30 seconds; cap images at 1MB
learnings.body: The iOS notification service extension gets killed around the 30-second mark, and image downloads over 5 seconds are cut off with a generic placeholder. Our image proxy resizes to 1024px and caps output at 1MB, which keeps downloads under the budget on LTE. Serve images from the cdn-push subdomain, which has the shortest latency from our edge nodes.

learnings.title: Must delete the device registration before clearing keychain on logout
learnings.body: If the app clears the keychain before calling DELETE /v2/devices/{id}, the device token stays linked to the old user and pushes keep arriving after logout. This caused a privacy incident in January, and the fix is now in the shared AuthSession teardown. Any new logout path must call unregisterDevice first and wait for the response before clearing local state.

learnings.title: Push copy A/B tests use push_copy_q3 with a 10 percent holdout
learnings.body: The experiment key push_copy_q3 assigns users to variants A, B, or holdout, and holdout users get no push at all for that campaign. Holdout is 10 percent, fixed by hash of user ID, so the split stays stable across sends. Don't read conversion from variant opens alone, since the holdout is the only valid baseline.

learnings.title: Android 13 notification permission: ask after the second session
learnings.body: On Android 13 and above the POST_NOTIFICATIONS prompt can only be shown once, and denial is hard to recover from. Our soft-ask screen appears after the second app session and after the user completes a transaction, which raised the opt-in rate from 41 to 58 percent in the March test. Never show the system prompt during onboarding before the user has seen value.

learnings.title: FCM topics are capped at 2000 per app instance
learnings.body: Each app instance can subscribe to at most 2000 FCM topics, and subscribe calls beyond that fail silently on Android. Our store-alert topics are per store ID, so a power user following every location can hit the cap. Use the topic_bundle service for regional alerts instead of subscribing directly to each store.

learnings.title: Quiet hours use the profile timezone, not the device timezone
learnings.body: Dispatch evaluates quiet hours (22:00 to 07:00) against the timezone stored on the user's profile, because device timezones are unreliable for travelers who haven't updated their phone. This means a user who moved cities but didn't change their profile may get pushes at night. The support macro quiet_hours_tz explains this to customers and offers a profile update link.
